Does a past IRS audit outcome impact the determination of an individual's independent contractor status?

If the IRS did not assess employment tax deficiencies for amounts paid to individuals holding positions substantially similar to the worker's position in a past audit, this may be considered in determining the individual's status under the UC Independent Contractor Guidelines (GU-FA-20-0506_UCIndependentContractorGuidelines_Accessible.pdf).

We ordered supplies via telephone from our vendor. The shipment arrived with only a packing slip that lists quantities and item descriptions, but doesn't show the prices we were charged. Is this acceptable documentation?

No, this is not sufficient. According to the policy, for telephone orders, the department must obtain a document that accompanies the shipment (such as a packing slip) that provides pricing/billing information along with enough detail to allow verification of the items purchased. The packing slip must include both the item details and the pricing information to comply with the documentation requirements.
hey quick q - if i grab a desk for like 5k, does that count as capital equipment that needs to go on inventory?
Yes, because the desk has a unit cost of $5,000 or more and a normal lifespan of greater than one year, making it capital equipment under Policy BFB-BUS-29.
Are there activities that are allowed for former UC employees related to the University?

Former UC employees may engage in formal participation in a panel or conference for educational purposes or to disseminate research, as well as attendance at general informational meetings, seminars, or similar events, as outlined in the mm-postemployment-coi-rules-10-2023.pdf policy.
What documentation and records does our department need to keep on file for equipment purchases made by our PIs?

The Principal Investigator must maintain up-to-date departmental records that reconcile to the official records maintained by the Equipment Management Office. These records must include the location (current building number and room number) of each item, as well as manufacturer, model number, and serial number information. (Policy: UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf)
What is the deadline for submitting meal and entertainment expenses for reimbursement?
Expenses must be submitted within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed 45 days. After that deadline, campuses and locations have options available for the reporting of reimbursements.
Who is authorized to sign DEA registrations on behalf of UC, and what alternative arrangement can be made if the primary person is unavailable?

According to the policy, an authorized individual can sign all DEA registrations on behalf of UC or National Laboratory locations through a Power of Attorney. Alternatively, that person can sign a Power of Attorney to authorize the CSPO (Controlled Substances Program Officer) or additional individuals to sign DEA registrations on their behalf.
If our department didn't receive delegation to handle the sale of excess property from the campus, who would be responsible for selling it and what costs might be deducted from what we receive?

The Surplus operation would conduct the sale. If the Surplus operation handles the sale, the cost of handling and transportation, plus administrative costs, may be deducted from the amount credited to your department.
Can I start negotiating with a private company for a job while I'm still employed at UC, and then represent that company in matters I worked on at the University?

No. According to the policy, you cannot represent other parties in matters you influenced while at the University for one year after you leave. You should also be careful about conflicts of interest while still employed - you must address any conflicts related to prospective employment before leaving the University.
Who is responsible for developing the overall procurement strategy that addresses University savings, pricing, and operational efficiency goals?

The Associate Vice President and Chief Procurement Officer of Procurement Services at the University of California Office of the President is responsible for developing the overall strategy. This is done in collaboration with the Executive Vice President-Chief Finance Officer, and the strategy addresses the University's overall needs in terms of savings, pricing, operational efficiencies, and continuous improvement.
I just had an interview with a company that does business with UC. Do I need to recuse myself from decisions involving that company?

Yes. Once you have had an interview with a prospective employer, you are considered to be "negotiating" or "have an arrangement" concerning prospective employment. This means you must recuse yourself entirely from any University decisions that directly relate to that prospective employer. You may not make, participate in making, or influence such decisions.
If I transfer equipment from my department at UC Davis to another department at UC Berkeley, do I need to treat this as a disposition on my campus inventory?

Yes. According to the policy, intercampus transfers are considered dispositions at the transferring location because the equipment has been removed from that location's inventory. Although the equipment will appear on the receiving location's inventory at UC Berkeley, your Davis department must treat the transfer as a disposition and remove it from your campus records.
Can I make changes to a UC Template Document without getting approval from the Policy Exception Authority?

No. Changes cannot be made to UC Template Documents except those that are specifically contemplated in the annotated version of the appropriate Template Document. Any other modifications require approval from the Policy Exception Authority or their delegee(s). The Policy Exception Authority may also seek input from the Office of General Counsel as they deem appropriate.
How should I determine whether to issue a vendor check payment or a 1099-MISC payment to an individual who performs work for UC?

According to the UC Independent Contractor Guidelines, vendor check payments to employees should be reported on Form W-2, while payments to employees reportable on Form 1099-MISC should be handled differently. The specific determination criteria are detailed in Section VIII.E. regarding Dual Status Workers. The excerpt indicates these are two distinct payment types with different tax reporting requirements, though the full criteria for which payment type applies to specific situations is covered in the referenced sections of the policy.
What forms do we need to use when we're recording encumbrance transactions according to our policy?

The following forms are used to record encumbrance transactions and serve as the official documentation for those transactions: 1) Purchase order copy or a copy of the contract on the given transaction. (UC-FO-00-0180_a-000-7.pdf)
What is the effective date of this UK GDPR Addendum, and who issued it?
The Addendum came into force on 21 March 2022 and was issued by the Information Commissioner for Parties making Restricted Transfers.

As the Principal Investigator on a federally-funded grant, who should I contact to ensure compliance with institutional procurement protocols for controlled substances, and what documentation will be required for my research project?

The Materiel Manager is responsible for the procurement of Controlled Substances, DEA Listed Chemicals, and California Precursor Chemicals for Authorized University Activities, in compliance with DEA registrations, University or Laboratory policies, and the requirements of the location’s Campus Controlled Substance Program. (UC-RK-25-761_ControlledSubstances_Accessible.pdf)

Hey, I'm new here and trying to understand our procurement policy - could you help clarify the difference between plant equipment and industrial plant equipment? I keep seeing both terms and I'm not sure which one applies to what we're buying.

Plant equipment is included in section c) Buildings, structures and improvements thereto, while industrial plant equipment is excluded from section d) Plant equipment. This distinction is outlined in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
What is the difference in reporting frequency for subcontract awards to HBCUs and Minority Institutions between DOD/NASA contracts versus civilian agency contracts?

Based on the policy excerpt, DOD, NASA, and Coast Guard contracts have specific reporting periods for subcontract awards to HBCUs and Minority Institutions (the excerpt does not specify the exact frequency for these agencies). In contrast, civilian agencies (non-DOD or NASA) require annual submission of this reporting information.
hey, do u know what health coverage stuff suppliers need to have when they're sending temp/extra staff to UC?

Suppliers must offer health coverage to full-time employees providing Services, either through group coverage meeting Minimum Essential Coverage and Affordable standards (for non-Applicable Large Employers) or individual coverage satisfying PPACA requirements. For Applicable Large Employers, fees must include the cost of health coverage and be higher than Services without coverage. This is outlined in the UC Terms and Conditions-04-01-25.pdf policy.
If we exercise our option to purchase leased equipment, what warranty coverage will we receive?

When UC exercises the purchase option, the remaining portion of the manufacturer's warranty period will be honored. The warranty period is calculated as having started from the date the lease agreement commenced, not from the date of purchase. UC will receive whatever warranty time remains from the original manufacturer's warranty period that was in effect when the equipment was installed.
Um, so like, when the university finds equipment lying around somewhere, how do they actually figure out like... what it's worth? Like, do they just guess or is there some kind of system for that?
The value is estimated by the user or custodial department, as verified by Equipment Management. The date found is used as the date received. (Policy: UC-FA-21-0555)
Do we need to offer a used vehicle with an estimated fair value of $75,000 to other UC locations before we can sell it publicly?

No. According to the policy, automotive equipment is exempt from the requirement to offer excess property to other University locations first, even if the vehicle's estimated fair value is $50,000 or more. You may place the automotive equipment on public sale without first offering it to other UC locations.
Should UC credentials be shared with third-party vendors for procurement purposes?

Sharing UC credentials with third-party vendors is prohibited under Rule 14 of the appendix-data-security.pdf policy. Institutional Information must not be used or copied for unauthorized purposes as outlined in Rule 15.
Does the procurement card policy in BUS-43 apply to employees working at the Laboratory?
No. Part 6 of the policy explicitly states that it does not apply to the Laboratory. A separate policy governs the procurement card program for the Laboratory.
What information should I include when reporting a security incident to my supervisor?

According to the policy, when reporting a security incident, you should include the nature of the breach and/or security incident, as well as details about which institutional information and/or IT resources were affected.

The policy BFB-BUS-29: Management and Control of University Equipment outlines the responsibilities for managing and controlling university equipment, but the specific roles are not detailed in the provided excerpt.
Who do I contact if I have questions about Strategic Sourcing Agreements or Price Schedule Agreements?

You should direct your questions to the Director of Procurement Services. The Director provides input to the Procurement Services Staff regarding questions related to Strategic Sourcing Agreements, Price Schedule Agreements, Commodity Planning, and other Procurement-related questions.
I left my position as a department manager last month. Can I now consult with my former department on a matter that was pending before us when I was supervising that area?

No, you cannot consult on that matter. As a former supervisor, you are deemed to have participated "personally and substantially" in proceedings that were pending before your former agency and were under your supervisory authority. Since you had primary responsibility for directing the operation or function of the program where this proceeding was initiated or conducted, you would be restricted from participating in it post-employment under the conflict of interest rules.
Who needs to approve the list of people authorized to use procurement cards before our campus can implement the system?

According to the policy, the Chancellor or the VP of ANR (or their designee) must submit a written request listing the names of specific individuals designated as Authorized Signers to both the Procurement Services Department and the Office of the Chief Investment Officer before implementing a procurement card system.
What documents do I need to submit along with my Administrative Fund Summary of Expenditure Reports if I'm a checking account recipient?

According to the policy, checking account recipients must submit the following documents with each report: a copy of the bank statement, a copy of the General Ledger, a log of outstanding checks, and a receipt or invoice for each expenditure.
Can a department head be issued a procurement card?

No, in general, department heads cannot be issued a procurement card. The policy states that department heads and Management Services Officers cannot be issued a procurement card because the person responsible for the independent reconciliation and verification process should not be the subordinate of any procurement cardholder.
Does our UC facility need to comply with Chemical Facility Anti-Terrorism Standards (CFATS)?

According to the policy excerpt, Chemical Facility Anti-Terrorism Standards (CFATS) is listed as a relevant regulatory framework that UC employees should be aware of. The DOD Form DD 1342/DOD Property Record is prepared as prescribed by the Government Property Administrator, per UC-FA-21-0555.
When we do a cost comparison analysis between having our University staff perform a service versus contracting it out, what types of costs should we include for the in-house option?

All moves of the employee and members of his or her household should be completed within one year of the date an appointee first reports to the new job, even if his or her appointment date was effective prior to the report date. Policy: UC-FA-18-0381_BFB-G-13_MovingRelocationPolicy

The revision history is located in section VIII of the policy, as indicated in the policy source UC-IT-19-0480_IS-3_Accessible.pdf.

Does a facilities use agreement where a third party uses a UC building for a summer camp serving children under 18 fall under the 'Minors' category in this risk matrix?

According to the policy, contracting for services is permitted when the services are of such an urgent, temporary, or occasional nature that delay would result from using the University's regular hiring process, or when inefficiencies or difficulties would arise from utilizing University employees. This means temporary services can be contracted out rather than requiring regular employee hiring.
According to the federal procurement policy governing our grant, who is responsible for establishing the fair market value determination for excess property?
The fair value of each item of property is determined by the Equipment Administrator, in consultation with the Useful Life Schedule, as stated in the University of California Policy BFB-BUS-38.

When property is permanently transferred between UC departments, an amount that is mutually agreeable to both departments may be transferred from the receiving department to the releasing department. An independent contractor relationship exists when the University has the right to control only the result of the service, not the manner of performance. An independent consultant relationship exists when the University does not control either the result of the service or the manner of performance. What acquisition code should I use when my campus borrows equipment from another UC location?

You should use acquisition code 37 when your campus borrows equipment from another UC location. Additionally, the lending campus will record the loan using the appropriate loan code, and your borrowing location should report the intercampus loan in the same manner as an intercampus transfer.
A 5-year contract at $25,000/year — is the total $125,000 subject to bidding?

No. Based on the policy excerpts provided, the $25,000/year contract is **not subject to competitive bidding requirements**.

**Rationale:**

Excerpt [1] specifies that competitive bidding is required for "Purchase Agreements involving an expenditure of more than **$100,000 annually**" under California Public Contract Code Section 10507 et seq.

Excerpt [5] confirms that for "Common Goods, Materials, and Services **$100,000 or less Annually in Value**," negotiation is allowed and competition is discretionary (sought only if the Procurement/Supply Chain Director determines it necessary).

**Key distinction:** The policy measures the threshold on an **annual basis** ($25,000/year), not the total contract value over 5 years ($125,000 total). Since the annual expenditure is $25,000, which does not exceed $100,000 annually, competitive bidding is not required.

However, the contract may still be subject to the small business set-aside program noted in Excerpt [5], as it falls within the $10,000-$250,000 annually range.

The laptop should be expensed, not capitalized. According to UC policy, theft-sensitive items valued at less than $5,000, including computers and communication devices such as laptops, should be expensed rather than capitalized.
Can I make a photocopy of our University's tax-free alcohol permit to give to our supplier as proof of authorization?

Yes, you may photocopy the permit exclusively for the purpose of furnishing proof of authorization to withdraw tax-free alcohol from tax-free alcohol suppliers. yo so like who's actually allowed to give controlled drugs to the research animals at UC?

Only researchers engaged in Authorized University Activities who are acting within the scope of their authorized professional practice and with the approval of all applicable Institutional Animal Care and Use Committees (IACUC), as outlined in UC-RK-25-761_ControlledSubstances_Accessible.pdf.

Hey, I'm new here and just got assigned a project involving some building alterations. Do I need to get sign-off from Facilities Management before I submit a Purchase Order for this, or can I just go ahead and place it?

How does the University handle equipment that has reached the end of its depreciation period?
The Office of the President transmits to each University location a list of assets that reached full depreciation during the preceding year, which are then written off prior to the next fiscal year.
As the PI on a federally-funded award, I need to clarify which entities and individuals fall under the scope of the BFB-IS-3 policy to ensure our institution's compliance with grant requirements.

The BFB-IS-3 policy applies to all UC campuses and medical centers, the UC Office of the President, UC Agriculture and Natural Resources, UC-managed national laboratories, and all other UC locations. As the Principal Investigator on this federally-funded award, who holds the delegated authority to execute final procurement decisions on behalf of my grant for services and related expenditures?

If the arbitrator submits their written decision after 30 calendar days from the completion of the hearing, is the decision still valid and binding?

Hey, I'm new here and trying to understand the procurement rules. If we have a contract that's going to run for 5 years at $25,000 per year, does that mean the full $125,000 total gets counted toward the bidding threshold, or do we only look at the annual amount?

No. Based on the policy excerpts provided, the $25,000/year contract is **not subject to competitive bidding requirements**.

**Rationale:**

Excerpt [1] specifies that competitive bidding is required for "Purchase Agreements involving an expenditure of more than **$100,000 annually**" under California Public Contract Code Section 10507 et seq.

Excerpt [5] confirms that for "Common Goods, Materials, and Services **$100,000 or less Annually in Value**," negotiation is allowed and competition is discretionary (sought only if the Procurement/Supply Chain Director determines it necessary).

**Key distinction:** The policy measures the threshold on an **annual basis** ($25,000/year), not the total contract value over 5 years ($125,000 total). Since the annual expenditure is $25,000, which does not exceed $100,000 annually, competitive bidding is not required.

However, the contract may still be subject to the small business set-aside program noted in Excerpt [5], as it falls within the $10,000-$250,000 annually range.

What are the key factors I should consider when determining whether someone should be classified as an employee versus an independent contractor?

According to UC policy, the primary factors to consider include: (1) whether the worker receives employee-type benefits such as vacation days, sick days, and health insurance; (2) whether a written contract exists that sets forth the worker's duties and terms and conditions; (3) whether the relationship is expected to be permanent; (4) whether the worker can be discharged at any time without penalty; and (5) whether the worker's activities are part of the regular business activities of the employer. Additionally, less important factors include whether the individual works part-time or full-time, whether the employment is temporary, the location where work is conducted, and the required hours of work.

Who should I contact if I have suggestions about state supply schedules or contracts that could benefit the University?

You should submit your reports and suggestions regarding state supply schedules or contracts to the Associate Vice President and Chief Procurement Officer - Procurement Services through the Commodity Managers.
Which staff members are we authorized to reimburse for meals and light refreshments, and who needs to sign off on those reimbursements?

The department head (or equivalent authority) is authorized to approve the reimbursement of meals, light refreshments, and other expenses permitted under this Bulletin. Additionally, each authorizing individual must have on file a Signature Authorization or Cancellation Form (Form U242) or an equivalent form or electronic signature authorization. (Policy: UC-FA-22-0617_BUS-79 Bus Meetings Entertainment_updated-accessible_12.15.2022.pdf)
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Can the ICO revise the Approved Addendum, and if so, under what circumstances?

Yes, the ICO may issue a revised Approved Addendum which makes reasonable and proportionate changes to the Approved Addendum, including correcting errors in the Approved Addendum; and/or reflects changes to UK Data Protection Laws. The revised Approved Addendum will specify the start date from which the changes are effective and whether the Parties need to review this Addendum. (Policy: Addendum C (UK GDPR) template to SCC_0.docx)

messages.content: Wait, so like... who is actually supposed to go get those photocopies of the permit thing and then... destroy them? I'm confused about whose job that even is?
The University is responsible for obtaining and, as applicable, destroying all photocopies of its permit, as stated in UC-PS-12-0031_Tax-FreeAlcoholPermitsRecordsOperations (3).pdf.
If a UC department requests our data in a specific format, like CSV instead of our default PDF export, are we required to provide it?

Yes, according to the policy, the Processor agrees to provide an up-to-date copy of the Data in the format requested by the Controller upon reasonable request. So if the department makes a reasonable request for a specific format like CSV, you should accommodate that request.
If we hire an independent contractor, can we require them to perform the work themselves rather than having someone else do it?

Yes, according to UC policy, you can require that the worker perform the services personally. Additionally, the worker must adhere to all applicable State and Federal guidelines as part of their engagement.

Hi everyone, I'm brand new here and I'm trying to understand something - if there's an issue with Section C not being followed, how long do I have to file a grievance about it under Article 5.C.? Is there a specific deadline I need to know about?

A grievance under Article 5.C. must be filed directly with the Executive Director-Labor Relations at the Office of the President no later than 14 calendar days after AFSCME receives the RFP or, where no RFP will issue, notice of a pending contract, or within 14 calendar days of the meeting provided for in Section D.6. (Policy: Article 5: Contracting Out, source: article-5-contracting-out-1-31-20.pdf)
URGENT: I need to know RIGHT NOW - do I have to get approval before taking on outside professional activities as a Senior Management Group member?!

Yes, SMG members must get approval in advance for both compensated and uncompensated outside professional activities, and must also report such activities annually to the President and the Regents (compendium-of-conflict-of-interest-and-related-policies-guidance-formerly-bfb-g-39.pdf, section 5).
Can a contractor be exempt from indemnification requirements, and if so, who needs to approve it?
Yes, exceptions to the contractor's indemnification requirements are possible, but they must be reviewed and approved by either the local Risk Manager (or their designee) or UC Legal.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What documentation is required to support cost sharing contributions on federally sponsored projects?

Accounting officers must retain copies of the Cost Sharing Contribution Report prescribed by Chapter 5 of the Contract and Grant Manual for Federal audit or examination. Principal Investigators must also provide supplementary information and records as practicable to explain the costs certified as contributed. This policy is outlined in UC-FO-00-0180_a-000-7.pdf.
Can I take old or broken equipment home for personal use? I need an answer ASAP — this is urgent!

No, according to UC-PS-12-0068_DispositionExcessPropertyTransferPropertyTransfer Policy, University employees may not remove excess property (regardless of value or condition) from University premises for personal use, distribution to third parties, or sale.

Can we use NAICS codes to exclude suppliers whose primary business classification involves controlled substances (such as pharmaceutical wholesalers classified under NAICS 424210) from our $500,000+ procurement contracts, and what are the procurement policy implications for doing so?

Yes, the policy allows campuses to exclude purchases from suppliers of controlled substances or radioactive materials using NAICS codes. This is outlined in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
How should we properly classify an individual as an independent contractor to ensure we remain compliant with UC policy and avoid any tax or penalty issues?

Yes, under the Safe Harbor rules of Section 530 of the Revenue Act of 1978 (and subsequent modifications), UC employers may avoid taxes and penalties if all three conditions in the Safe Harbor Rules are met. This is outlined in policy GU-FA-20-0506_UCIndependentContractorGuidelines_Accessible.pdf.
When we acquire personal property through a lease-purchase agreement, who do we need to report this to and why?

You must report all personal property acquisitions funded by lease-purchase agreements or Conditional Sales Contracts to the Assistant Vice President, Financial Services and Controls. This reporting is required for inclusion in the University's Financial Position Report.
yo, what's the deal with how we're supposed to buy IT services around here?
The policy mentioned is UC-IT-19-0480_IS-3_Accessible.pdf, which focuses on electronic information security and does not provide specific details about procurement procedures.

So like, if we're hiring someone through UC to clean our office or whatever, do we need to do that Fair Wage Fair Work thing? Or does that not apply when you're using a vendor that UC already knows about?

No, the Fair Wage Fair Work verification does not apply to contracts for Covered Services, which include cleaning services, as defined in UC Terms and Conditions-04-01-25.pdf and further detailed in BUS-43.
Who is responsible for overseeing the acquisition and disposition of University vehicles across all UC locations?

The AVP - Chief Procurement Officer is the responsible officer for UC Policy BFB-BUS-8 on Acquisition and Disposition of University Vehicles. The Procurement Services (PS) office is the responsible office that implements this policy across all campuses, Medical Centers, and other UC locations.
Can I include the salary costs of our lab technician who spent 200 hours fabricating this equipment in the total cost for capitalization?

No. According to the policy, departmental labor, travel, payroll expenses, and overhead must not be considered part of the cost of acquiring a fabricated asset for capitalization purposes. The cost should only include materials, supplies, and services from outside vendors or authorized recharge activities.

Um, so like... when we're paying someone to do work for us, do we have to make sure they have some kind of insurance or something? Like, what insurance stuff are we supposed to ask them about or require them to have?

When contracting for services, the Contractor/External User must meet the established minimum insurance requirements, which can be fulfilled through self-insurance (see [1]). For contracts other than High Risk contracts, a Certificate of Insurance must be provided to the University upon request, showing compliance with these requirements or a signed statement from an authorized officer if self-insured (see [2]). The University’s policy BFB-BUS-63 outlines these minimum insurance requirements, which must be maintained throughout the contract term (see [3]). Exceptions to this policy are only permitted under extenuating circumstances after review by the local Risk Management Office. For high-risk activities, the Contractor/External User must contact their local Risk Management Office early in the contract process to assess risks and determine appropriate insurance requirements (see [4]).
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
If we need to reuse parts from decommissioned equipment, what is the required procedure?

The custodial department must submit an Equipment Inventory Modification Request (EIMR, or University location equivalent) to Equipment Management to report the cannibalization. Cannibalized parts not re-used shall be sent to the Surplus Operation, or directly disposed of by the custodial department if so delegated the authority. (Policy: UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf)
Can faculty clubs use University funds to buy materials that are exempt from federal taxes?

Yes, organizations closely allied to or officially associated with the University, such as a faculty club, may be permitted to purchase materials not subject to federal tax through the Location’s Procurement/Supply Chain Management/Procurement Office with the approval of the Chancellor, as stated in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.

What is the proper procedure if my department has $15,000 in laboratory equipment that is no longer required for our current research project, and how should we handle the disposal or redistribution of these assets through UC procurement channels?

Report any excess property immediately to the Contract and Grant Officer, or designee, who will then report to the Government Contracting Officer. (UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf)
hey so if the conservatory gives me a studio space and handles tuition stuff, can they actually tell me i can't teach anywhere else?

Yes, the teacher agreed not to teach elsewhere within the vicinity without the consent of the conservatory as part of the arrangement outlined in the GU-FA-20-0506_UCIndependentContractorGuidelines_Accessible.pdf policy.

If I'm hired to work as a secretary-receptionist and my supervisor gives me detailed instructions on both what tasks to complete and exactly how to perform them, could I be classified as an independent contractor instead of an employee?

No. Based on the policy excerpt, if your supervisor controls not only the results you're supposed to accomplish but also how you accomplish those results—such as giving you detailed instructions on work methods and supervising your performance—you would be classified as an employee, not an independent contractor. The IRS has ruled in similar situations that this level of control over both what and how work is performed indicates an employment relationship rather than an independent contractor arrangement.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What packaging requirements must suppliers follow for UC procurement?

Suppliers must comply with the Toxics in Packaging Prevention Act and meet all standards and requirements set forth in the Policy. Additionally, all packaging must meet at least one of the criteria listed, such as using bulk packaging or reusable packaging. (UC Terms and Conditions-04-01-25.pdf)
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Who is responsible for ensuring laboratory purchases align with the Strategic Sourcing Initiative?

The Laboratory Director is responsible for purchasing and providing the goods and services required in a manner consistent with this Bulletin and with the Strategic Sourcing Initiative requirements. (Policy: BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf)
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Can we transfer surplus laboratory equipment to a private company for their research purposes?
Transfer of property to individuals or for-profit organizations is prohibited unless specific provisions are made in the terms of an award. (UC-PS-12-0068)

Um, so like... if the University is trying to get a really big contract from the federal government—I think you said over $700,000?—and there's going to be other companies involved to help do the work... what are we supposed to do exactly? Like, what things do we need to have or do to make that happen?

The University must prepare a Small Business Subcontracting Plan, with collaboration between the Campus Small Business Officer or Supplier Diversity Coordinator and the originating department. This requirement is outlined in BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
What happens if someone breaks the rules during procurement - could this affect our department?

The Compendium of Conflict of Interest and Related Policies – Guidance states that unacceptable conduct is subject to sanctions outlined in APM 016, which may be applied when misconduct is substantiated by a formal process.
Who should I contact if I have questions about UC's risk transfer and insurance requirements?
You should contact Gary Leonard, who is the Executive Director of General Liability. You can reach him by email at Gary.Leonard@ucop.edu or by phone at (510) 987-9186.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What acquisition code is used when equipment is recorded after completion of a construction or repair requisition?
Acquisition code 31 (Purchase Order) is used when equipment is recorded after the service department reports the date of completion, as stated in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Do I need to seek help if a procurement decision could affect my spouse's financial interests?

Yes, you should seek help if the UC decision affects personal finances of you, your spouse, or immediate family. This is outlined in the Conflict of Interest Training-Procurement-2024.pdf policy under Government Code Sections 87103 & 87407.
If a student participates in a university program where the agency supervises their daily activities, would the student be considered an employee of the university or the agency for tax purposes?

According to IRS Ruling PLR 9439004, the student would be considered an employee of the university for FICA and income tax withholding purposes, not the agency. This is because the university has control over the payment of wages, which is the determining factor for employment classification in this situation.
As a UC employee, am I allowed to use a personally-owned cellular phone for university business, or must I use a UC-issued device?

Based on the excerpt provided, the specific guidelines regarding personal versus UC-issued cellular phones are contained in policy BFB-G-46 (March 30, 2012). The excerpt does not include the detailed content of that policy, only its title and reference. To get a definitive answer about personal device usage policies, you would need to consult the full BFB-G-46 policy document.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Which UC policy governs the procurement of goods and services?
The UC Presidential Policy BFB-BUS-43 governs the procurement of goods and services; Supply Chain Management.
If we discover a Critical CVE vulnerability in our systems, how much time do we have to fix it according to UC policy?
You must use commercially acceptable efforts to remediate any Critical CVE vulnerability within twenty (20) business days.
Who is responsible for establishing and overseeing the Campus Controlled Substances Program?

The Responsible Official, as designated by the Chancellor or National Laboratory Director, is responsible for establishing and overseeing the Campus Controlled Substances Program in accordance with federal and state laws, best practices, and the Policy.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What information needs to be included when reporting a gift or contribution?
The Summary of Elements to be Substantiated in Exhibit IV outlines the required information for reporting gifts, contributions, and miscellaneous items, as specified in UC-FO-00-0190_a-253-27.pdf.
If our department hosts an event where we're serving alcohol that we purchased tax-free under our permit, what records do we need to maintain?

Based on UC Policy BFB-BUS-2, you must maintain records related to your tax-free alcohol permit and operations. The policy requires departments to keep documentation of their alcohol purchases and use under the tax-free permit. You should consult your campus's business and financial services office for specific record retention requirements and formats, as these may vary by location within the UC system.
If the ICO issues a revised Approved Addendum that significantly increases our compliance costs, can we immediately terminate our data transfer agreement?

No, you cannot terminate immediately. According to the policy, you may only end the Addendum if you are a Party selected in Table 4, you have first taken reasonable steps to reduce the substantial and disproportionate costs or risks, and you provide written notice for a reasonable notice period to the other Party before the start date of the revised Approved Addendum. The termination takes effect at the end of that reasonable notice period, not immediately.
Is there a designated administrator responsible for the Strategic Sourcing Initiative?

The Associate Vice President and UCOP Chief Procurement Officer are responsible for administering the Strategic Sourcing Initiative, as stated in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf policy.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Who is responsible for ensuring compliance with the Risk Transfer Insurance Requirements?
The policy outlines that compliance responsibilities are detailed in section IV of UC-RK-25-762_BFB-BUS-63.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What is UC's role in data processing under this agreement?
UC is the data controller as defined in the Appendix GDPR (EEA and UK) policy.
URGENT: What insurance requirements MUST independent contractors meet when hired by UC - need this answered NOW?

According to the UC Independent Contractor Guidelines (GU-FA-20-0506), individuals retained as independent contractors must show evidence of adequate insurance coverage. University policy (BUS-63) requires that locations contact the respective Risk Manager to determine appropriate levels of coverage for such individuals.
Do I need to get Agency approval in writing before we can start the process to acquire new equipment for our department?
Yes. According to the policy, the University will not initiate an acquisition until written approval has been obtained from the Agency.
If we upgrade a piece of equipment for $3,500, should we capitalize it or expense it?
Equipment upgrades valued at less than $5,000 should be expensed as non-capital transactions. Since your $3,500 upgrade is below the $5,000 threshold, it should be expensed rather than capitalized.
When I'm evaluating whether a supplier's quoted price is reasonable, do I need to account for any incentive payments they've included in their proposal?

Yes. According to the policy, the Procurement/Supply Chain Director must include the value of the incentive payment when determining price reasonableness. This means you need to factor in any incentive payments that are part of the Purchase Order or Purchase Agreement to properly assess whether the total quoted price is reasonable.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Do I need to ensure funds are available before creating a Pool Purchase Order?

Yes, Pool Purchase Orders shall be entered into only when the Commodity Manager has been assured that funds are available to cover the definite or guaranteed minimum quantities to be ordered. (Policy: BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf)
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Can I expense a meal for a donor cultivation event under the University's entertainment policy?
Yes, entertainment expenditures include meals and light refreshments for events that support the University’s mission, such as donor cultivation, as defined in UC-FA-22-0617_BUS-79.
Do I need to sign a Power of Attorney if I want to authorize my CSPO to obtain and execute order forms for Schedule II Controlled Substances?

Yes, according to the policy, if you want to authorize your CSPO or additional individuals to obtain and execute order forms for Schedule II Controlled Substances, you must sign a Power of Attorney to grant them that authorization.

In the event that the lessor breaches this agreement and fails to deliver the Goods and/or Services as specified, what remedies and recourse options are available to the University, and what are the potential financial impacts on my grant budget and project timeline?

UC may by written notice terminate the Agreement for Lessor’s breach, and may use or secure Goods and/or Services elsewhere, with Lessor liable for any excess costs incurred. This is specified in the TC-Operating Lease-Equip Rental.docx policy.
If a lessor wants to present equipment options to our department, what format should they use for their marketing materials?

All marketing materials and presentations must be provided in electronic format that is easily transferable to UC staff. Hard copies or physical materials are only permitted if a UC representative specifically requests or requires them.
If I file a grievance before a contract is signed, what happens to the contracting process?
If the grievance was filed prior to the formation of a contract, the University shall not proceed with the contracting process.
URGENT: I need an immediate answer - what's the critical difference between Code 30 and Code 31 for University Inventorial Equipment acquisitions? This can't wait!
Code 30 is used for equipment recorded as 'Purchased, Government Retains Title,' while Code 31 is used for equipment recorded as 'Purchase Order.' This information is from the UC-FA-21-0555 policy.
hey, so if a supplier doesn't want to do the whole third-party certification thing, can they just do something else instead?
Yes, a supplier may use an alternative to a third-party review if approved by the responsible UC Information Security Officer, as stated in the appendix-data-security.pdf policy.
URGENT: I need an immediate answer - am I allowed to use the University's name on my personal website to promote my consulting business RIGHT NOW?

No, the Policy on Representation of the University on Letterhead and Business Cards restricts the use of the University's name and seal to purposes consistent with its mission, which excludes commercial activities not under the University's auspices.
URGENT: What equipment exactly falls under this policy for management and control? Need this answer ASAP!

The policy covers University Inventorial Equipment, Government Inventorial Equipment, Other Government Property, and Other Inventorial Items, as stated in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.

Um, so like, when the university gets more money after the first round of funding, who is actually supposed to make sure all the equipment stuff doesn't just, like, disappear or get lost? Like, who's in charge of keeping track of it all?
The University accepts responsibility and accountability for those balances under the terms of the follow-on award, as stated in Policy BFB-BUS-29.
If we experience a security incident with a vendor, what information do we need to request from them in their incident response?

According to the policy, you should request that the Supplier provide information about what they have done or will do to mitigate any deleterious effects of the security incident, as well as what corrective action they have taken or will take to prevent future security incidents.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Who is eligible to receive allocations from the Administrative Fund?

The Principal Officers of The Regents and certain Officers of the University are eligible. Funds for Principal Officers are allocated to the Vice President for Legal Affairs and General Counsel of The Regents, the Chief Investment Officer and Treasurer of The Regents, and the Secretary and Chief of Staff to The Regents. Funds for Officers of the University are allocated by the President to the Provost and Executive Vice President, the Executive Vice Presidents, the Senior Vice Presidents, Chancellors, Laboratory Director, and other administrators of the University. (Policy: UC-FO-00-0190_a-253-27.pdf)
How do we go about getting a supplier prequalified if they've got a good track record working with us here at the university?

Yes, known suppliers with a current record of satisfactory performance and reliability may be considered prequalified for goods and services they have previously supplied, as stated in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
Under the terms of my federally-funded grant, may I charge first-class airfare to the administrative allocation for official project-related travel?

First-class airfare may be reimbursed from the Administrative Fund if it is authorized under the circumstances set forth in G-28, Policy and Regulations Governing Travel, as specified in UC-FO-00-0190_a-253-27.pdf.
URGENT: We need an immediate answer - does the IRS ruling impact our cleaning contractor classification under independent contractor guidelines? This is critical and needs to be addressed NOW.

The IRS ruling indicates that the company exercised, or retained the right to exercise, the degree of direction and control necessary to establish an employer-employee relationship, as stated in the GU-FA-20-0506_UCIndependentContractorGuidelines_Accessible.pdf policy excerpt.
If our department's alcohol storage location moves to a different room, what do we need to do with our current permit?

You must file an amendment on Form 5150.22 when any information on the approved permit changes. Since your storage location has changed, this would constitute a change in permit information requiring an amendment to be filed.

When a UC department purchases $150,000 worth of custom-fabricated laboratory equipment from a vendor, what specific acquisition code should be entered in the UC procurement system to properly classify this capital equipment purchase?
Fabricated equipment is recorded using acquisition code 32 (Fabrication), as stated in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
Who is responsible for supervising the students' daily activities in this program?
According to the policy, the students' daily activities are supervised by the agency that provided the funding for the program.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Which policies address conflicts of interest for UC faculty and staff?

Regents Policy 1110: Policy on Conflicts of Interest in Accordance with the Political Reform Act (For Regents) (March 16, 2017) and the University of California Conflict of Interest Code (Financial) (October 2014) apply. See also related guidance in the Appendix, attached.
Do I need to get written approval from the Government Contracting Officer before using university equipment on a different government award?
Yes, according to the policy, when it is desirable to use the property on another award, you must secure prior written approval from the Government Contracting Officer before doing so.
hey so like can i just use the lab stuff for my own projects or do i gotta ask someone first?

No, employees shall not use University property or property in the care and custody of the University for personal purposes without pre-approval by the Chancellor or Laboratory Director. This is outlined in UC-FA-21-0555.
hey do you know what sections are in that UC-IT-19-0480_IS-3_Accessible.pdf document? kinda need to know what's covered in it
The policy includes Section 1: General Overview and Section 2: Organizing Information Security, as stated in UC-IT-19-0480_IS-3_Accessible.pdf.
Must each UC location develop procedures regarding the procurement of Controlled Substances for research?

Each location must develop and publish written procedures addressing federal or state requirements for ordering, procurement, and distribution of Controlled Substances for research purposes, as outlined in UC-RK-25-761_ControlledSubstances_Accessible.pdf.
I work as an administrative assistant in the department. Do I need to comply with the post-employment conflict of interest rules?

No, if your position is purely clerical, secretarial, or ministerial in nature, you are not required to comply with this rule. However, if your duties extend beyond purely clerical, secretarial, or ministerial functions, you would need to comply with the post-employment conflict of interest rules.
Must specific steps be taken if there is a modification, change, or cancellation of insurance coverage under the policy?

The Regents of the University of California must comply with the policy provisions regarding any modification, change, or cancellation of insurance coverage, and indicate that they are an additional insured as described in the contract. Policy name: UC-RK-25-762_BFB-BUS-63_RiskTransferInsuranceRequirements_Accessible (1).pdf

Um, so like... how do you actually know if something is supposed to be part of that Strategic Sourcing Initiative thing? Like, what makes something qualify for that, or is it just random? I'm confused about what the rules are for whether something gets picked for that or not.

The Commodity Manager identifies items for inclusion in the program which are purchased by multiple Locations in sufficient quantities that an economic advantage can be gained by creating a Strategic Sourcing Initiative. (BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf)
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Who should I contact if I need advice on exceptions to indemnification requirements for a subaward agreement?

UC Legal will advise on exceptions to the indemnification requirements mandated in Standing Order 100.4(dd)(9) in subawards, material/data transfer agreements, or land access agreements. Policy: UC-RK-25-762_BFB-BUS-63
Do I need additional approval if I want to use entertainment funds to take a guest to a baseball game?
Yes. According to the policy, tickets to a sporting event are among the expenses that require additional approval at a higher level beyond standard entertainment expense authorization.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Can I purchase the vehicle during the lease term or at its expiration?

Under the Lease with Purchase Option, the terms are those of a straight lease, allowing the property to be purchased either during the term of the lease or at its expiration. Payments may also be applied to the purchase of the property under lease. (Policy: UC-PS-12-0029_AcquisitionDispositionUniversityVehicles.pdf)
How should we record Government-furnished property or equipment purchased with Government grant funds in our inventory system?

Government-furnished property or University-acquired property purchased by direct charge to a Government award should be recorded using the University's management and control system for inventorial equipment, which must provide the minimum data listed under section III.B.7 of this Bulletin. These records should be maintained separately from standard University-owned inventorial equipment records.
If our Chancellor hosts a donor appreciation dinner, what is the maximum we can reimburse for expenses without needing additional approval?

Events held by the Chancellor are subject to reimbursement of expenses up to 200% of the listed limits without additional approval. However, this special rule does not apply to events for internal senior leadership.

As the Principal Investigator on this federally funded award, what is the expected timeline for receipt of the completed inventory listing and signed certification statement following the conclusion of the physical inventory process?

The listing and signed statement will be furnished with a minimum of delay at the completion of the physical inventory, as stated in the UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf policy.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Who is responsible for approving exceptions to the reviewer reporting relationship under Policy BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main?

The Administrator (or other individual approved by the Controller) shall approve exceptions to the reviewer reporting relationship, as specified in Policy BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main.
What records does the University need to maintain for completed products produced under a Government award when the product is shipped right after Government inspection and acceptance?
When shipment immediately follows Government inspection and acceptance of the completed product, the records consist of a summarization of quantities accepted or shipped.
I'm still pretty new here - when do we need to have insourcing work completed by under this policy?
The deadline for insourcing the work shall be as soon as possible, but in any event no later than one year from the date of ratification. (Policy: article-5-contracting-out-1-31-20.pdf)
What information do I need to include when documenting a piece of equipment for the university inventory?

At a minimum, you should provide the following information: Property Number, Description, Equipment Classification Code, Manufacturer's Name, Manufacturer's Model Number, Serial Number (if available), Cost, Acquisition Code, CAAN/Building and Room Number, Reference Number (typically the purchase order number), Custody Code, Receipt Date, Fund Number, Original Fund Source Code, and UC Location 2 Indicator.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Do I need to track equipment purchased with grant funds according to the policy?

Yes, the University must record both agency-furnished and University property acquired under an award in the equipment inventory records, listing equipment by fund number for fiscal and inventorial reports to the agency. Post-employment conflict of interest restrictions for UC employees include: 1) A permanent ban on "switching sides" in cases or proceedings, which likely prohibits former employees from taking positions contrary to their former role or influencing ongoing matters related to their former employment [4]. 2) Restrictions under the Public Contract Code prohibiting contracts to provide goods or services to the UC or related entities for a specified period after leaving employment, to prevent conflicts of interest arising from former positions [4]. Employees are required to consult the Office of the General Counsel or their campus Conflict of Interest Coordinator for specific guidance on these restrictions [4].
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Who is responsible for processing financial adjustments when a payment recording error occurs, such as an incorrect object code or sales tax error?

The Accounting Office, or if delegated the responsibility, Equipment Management shall process financial adjustments for discrepancies due to errors in recording payment, as stated in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
As a UC employee who processes student financial aid, what federal law do I need to comply with regarding the protection of financial information?
You need to comply with the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLBA), which applies to student financial aid processing at UC.
How do I know what cybersecurity responsibilities my department should handle versus what the vendor is responsible for?

According to UC policy, cybersecurity responsibilities of each party must be clearly documented. You should refer to your Statement of Work (SOW) or UC's Terms and Conditions, which will outline who is responsible for specific cybersecurity tasks between your department and any external parties involved.
If my department has both a UC policy and a specific administrative procedure for contracting services, which one should we follow?
According to the policy, the more specific procedure will take precedence. You should follow the specific administrative procedure rather than the general UC policy when the two conflict.
Can I give a non-cash award to an employee as a gift for their retirement?

The excerpt provided does not contain sufficient detail to answer this question. While the document is titled 'Employee Non-Cash Award Gifts' and appears to have procedures outlined in Section V, the specific content of those procedures is not included in the excerpt. To determine whether non-cash awards can be given for retirement, you would need to review the full procedures section of the policy document.
If our department contracts out services that could affect my job, what kind of support might the University provide?

The University may provide support that includes training or retraining programs, transfer and re-employment opportunities, job counseling and placement services, and assistance with job applications, resume preparation, and interviewing skills.
Hey, I'm new here and still getting up to speed – when am I supposed to reach out to the local Risk Management Office about insurance and indemnification stuff in contracts?

Consult the local Risk Management Office early in the contract process regarding insurance and indemnification contract provisions. Policy: UC-RK-25-762_BFB-BUS-63_RiskTransferInsuranceRequirements_Accessible (1).pdf
Can we offer supplier incentive payments on our purchase orders, or should we always negotiate discounts instead?

While the Procurement/Supply Chain Director should generally negotiate quantity or payment discounts in lieu of supplier incentive payments, incentive payments are permitted on Purchase Orders or Purchase Agreements. However, if you do include incentive payments, you must follow the specific procedures outlined in the policy for those arrangements.

As a PI managing controlled substances under my federal grant, which UC office should I contact to ensure proper notification to the DEA field division in the event of theft or significant loss of controlled materials in my laboratory?

Individual Campus Controlled Substance Program procedures must specify which division or office is responsible for notifying the local DEA field division office within one (1) business day, as outlined in UC-RK-25-761_ControlledSubstances_Accessible.pdf.
What level of documentation should I require when a department wants to pay an honorarium to a guest speaker?

According to the policy, accounting officers should exercise professional judgment in determining the type of documentation necessary to assure that the expenditure is proper and appropriate. The specific documentation requirements may vary depending on the circumstances of the honorarium payment, so you should assess what documentation is needed on a case-by-case basis to ensure the expenditure is justified and follows UC guidelines.
Can I use the same password across my UC email account and other UC system logins?

No. According to UC policy, you must prevent the use of passphrases or other authentication secrets that are common across multiple unrelated UC sites or units. Each UC system login should have its own unique password rather than reusing the same password across different UC platforms.
Where should I retain a consultant agreement documentation for a non-payroll disbursement?

Consultant agreement documentation must be retained in the Accounting Office, unless it contains confidential information or agreements with extraneous details beyond the disbursement process, in which case it may be retained in other appropriate offices with approval from the Chancellor.
What steps should our suppliers take if they accidentally receive Protected Health Information (PHI) while working on tasks related to our agreement?

Supplier will notify UC immediately and use commercially reasonable efforts to return the PHI to UC, maintain its confidentiality, and execute the UC Appendix - Business Associate or modify the Agreement if access to PHI becomes necessary, as outlined in UC Terms and Conditions-04-01-25.pdf §16.5(c).
Who is responsible for maintaining and updating the UC BUS-63 Risk Matrix?

The Office of Risk Services is responsible for maintaining the UC BUS-63 Risk Matrix, which establishes the risk level for various University activities. The matrix will be updated as necessary and circulated to internal stakeholders.
Which Business and Finance Bulletin should I reference if I need to understand the university's policy on providing a gift to an external consultant who is not a UC employee?
You should reference BFB G-42, Gifts Presented to Non-Employees on Behalf of the University, as this bulletin governs gifts presented to non-employees on behalf of the University.
Hey, do you know what the UC Fair Wage rate was starting Oct 1, 2017?
The UC Fair Wage as of October 1, 2017, is $15 per hour, as stated in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf policy.
What documentation is required when UC Davis needs to process a $50,000 equipment purchase from a new vendor, or when a department requests a $15,000 contract amendment mid-fiscal year?
Official documentation is required for all university financial transactions, as specified in the UC-FO-00-0180_a-000-7 policy under the ACCOUNTING MANUAL section A-000-7.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Do I need to replace my existing university vehicle if it's still functional and safe?

The policy requires evaluating whether existing fleet vehicles can perform necessary specific functions (Question 2) and whether replacement is needed for safety or other reasons (Question 3). This guidance is from UC-PS-12-0029_AcquisitionDispositionUniversityVehicles.pdf.
hey, do you know where i can find the different doc process options for the different campuses?
The options for selecting the documentation process are listed in the 'Notes' section at the bottom of page 2 of the Federal Funds Checklist-121525 (2).docx policy.
What should I do if our physical inventory reveals that some Government Inventorial Equipment is missing or doesn't match our official records?

Any discrepancies disclosed by physical inventory of Government Inventorial and Other Equipment shall be reported to the Government Property Administrator. You should also notify Equipment Management, which will update the official records accordingly.
As a procurement officer, what am I responsible for regarding commodity agreements and price schedules?

You are responsible for scheduling advantageous purchases and timely renewal of commodity agreements and price schedules in a manner consistent with work schedules. You should also evaluate existing consolidated purchase arrangements to determine if they can be expanded or modified.

So like, if the university bought something with money from the government, can we just sell it to another department in the school if they're gonna pay for it with government money too? Is that allowed or something?

No, University-titled property originally purchased with Government funds must not be sold to other departments, campuses or educational institutions if the purchaser intends to use Government funds as the payment source. (UC-PS-12-0068)
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Are there restrictions on communicating with the University regarding post-employment activities?

Yes, per Rule 4, individuals are prohibited from appearing before or communicating with the University in matters related to their post-employment activities. Policy: mm-postemployment-coi-rules-10-2023.pdf

Hey, I just started here and I'm a bit confused about something—if someone's providing services to multiple clients while they're working on a University engagement, does that automatically mean they'd be classified as an independent contractor?
No, the individual must provide more than de minimis services to other clients during the University engagement, as stated in GU-FA-20-0506_UCIndependentContractorGuidelines_Accessible.pdf.
How often should we perform authenticated vulnerability scans on our IT Resources that store Institutional Information at Protection Level 3?

The policy excerpt does not specify the frequency for performing authenticated vulnerability scans. It only states that authenticated vulnerability scans must be performed for IT Resources that process or store Institutional Information classified at Protection Level 3 or higher, but does not provide details about how often these scans should occur.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What is the aggregate gift limit for gifts received in the past 12 months?
The aggregate gift limit is $590, as stated in the Sources of Gifts section of the Conflict of Interest Training-Procurement-2024.pdf policy.
What security measures do we need to implement when physically transporting hard drives containing sensitive student records between our campus locations?

According to UC Policy BFB-IS-3 section 8.3.3, you must use secure methods for the transfer of electronic media containing Institutional Information classified at Protection Level 2 or higher. Additionally, your unit must track these transfers. Since student records typically qualify as Protection Level 2 or higher information, you are required to employ secure transportation methods and maintain records of when and how these transfers occur to protect against loss, unauthorized access, misuse, or corruption during transit.
When we purchase items in bulk for our department's business meetings, what documentation do we need to maintain?

According to Policy BUS-79, you should prepare a separate inventory sheet for each item purchased in quantity. The inventory record should include the item purchased, cost, number of items, reason for purchase, and then track the item usage by month/year, purpose and name of recipient(s), and the remaining balance.
As a Workforce Manager, what information security items should I include when recruiting for a new position?

According to the policy, when recruiting, you should establish the security duties of the position and include them in the job description or appointment letter. You should also follow the appropriate Location onboarding procedures related to information security.
How are Physical Inventories distributed to the Custodial departments?
Physical Inventories may be distributed either via hard copy or electronically to the University location's Custodial departments.
Under UC policy, what are the criteria that determine whether equipment or property falls below the de minimis threshold for federal funding purposes on our grant?

Property is considered de minimis when its fair value is negligible, that is, below the costs required for handling, record keeping, storage, removal and other costs associated with its trade, sale or disposition. This definition is outlined in UC-PS-12-0068_DispositionExcessPropertyTransferProperty.pdf.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What criteria determine if an item is included in a Strategic Sourcing Initiative under the UC procurement policy?

The Commodity Manager identifies items for inclusion in the program which are purchased by multiple Locations in sufficient quantities that an economic advantage can be gained by creating a Strategic Sourcing Initiative. (BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf)

I'm new here and just got assigned to procurement - I'm a bit confused about how we should handle incentives and discounts that suppliers offer but don't include in the actual sales price. Can someone walk me through what we're supposed to do with those?

Incentives and discounts not reflected in the sales price, allowances, or similar payments received from Suppliers should be remitted to the appropriate Location office as determined by Procurement Services at the Office of the President, for Locations to use in support of Strategic Sourcing. (Policy: BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf)
What are the requirements for UC staff and Subprocessors regarding data confidentiality?

According to the policy, UC staff and approved Subprocessors must either have agreed to keep the Data confidential, or be otherwise under a statutory obligation to protect the confidentiality of the Data.
If I'm tagging equipment acquired in 2019 at the Davis location, what should the first four digits of the tag be?

The first two digits should be '19' for the year 2019. For Davis, you would need to check the location code list, but the second pair of digits represents the University location with the digits reversed from their normal order. So you would use the reversed code for Davis as the second pair of digits.
If a UC department enters into a contract with an instructor who agrees not to teach elsewhere in the area without permission, could that instructor be classified as an independent contractor?

Based on the IRS ruling referenced in the policy, probably not. The excerpt explains that when a conservatory required teachers to obtain consent before teaching elsewhere and guaranteed the conservatory a specified portion of fees, the IRS determined these teachers were employees, not independent contractors. The IRS found that the conservatory had sufficient right to direct and control the manner of performance of the teachers' services. The key principle is that the degree of direction and control over how work is performed is a critical factor in determining employment status. If UC has similar contractual controls over an instructor's work, that would suggest an employee relationship rather than independent contractor status.
