What should be done with incentives and discounts not included in the sales price from suppliers?

Incentives and discounts not reflected in the sales price, allowances, or similar payments received from Suppliers should be remitted to the appropriate Location office as determined by Procurement Services at the Office of the President, for Locations to use in support of Strategic Sourcing. (Policy: BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf)
What procedures do we need to follow in our department before we can declare government property as excess when it's no longer required for our grant or contract?

Before declaring government property excess, it shall be screened against the needs of other awards. If there is a need for the property, the Government Contracting Officer shall be asked for authority to use or transfer it. (Policy: UC-FA-21-0555)
What procurement and supply chain management policy should I be referencing here at UC?
The policy name is BFB-BUS-43 Purchases of Goods and Services; Supply Chain Management.

I'm trying to figure out... when the UC hires people who aren't regular employees, like independent contractors or something... what kind of help or services are they supposed to get? Is that part of the contract, or like, what exactly does UC have to provide for them?

The contract includes maintenance, repairs, supplies, equipment, janitorial services, laundry services, personnel, and other support services, as stated in the GU-FA-20-0506_UCIndependentContractorGuidelines_Accessible.pdf policy.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What criteria does the surplus administrator use to determine if an item can be disposed of as excess property?

The surplus administrator determines whether an item has no further value to the University and can be disposed of as excess property, per UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
If we want to transfer excess University property to another UC campus, do we have to charge them fair value for it?

Yes, University-owned property must be sold to the recipient institution at fair value, unless there is a specific exception that permits otherwise. You would need to consult section 2 of this policy to determine if any exceptions apply to your situation.
If I'm a UC researcher working at a non-UC facility that doesn't have its own Campus Controlled Substances Program, what do I need to do to legally use controlled substances in my research?

You will need to register independently for an individual DEA registration. You are responsible for procuring, maintaining security of, keeping records for, and disposing of controlled substances in accordance with federal and state regulations.
I'm still getting up to speed here, but could someone help me understand who's supposed to be in charge of making sure university equipment is properly managed and controlled?
All UC employees and students are responsible for the proper management and control of university equipment. Policy: University of California – Policy BFB-BUS-29
As a location unit manager, what are my primary responsibilities under this information security policy?
Location Units are accountable for implementing information security and protecting privacy within their research collaboration activities.
Can I share my login credentials with a colleague so they can access a shared drive on my behalf while I'm on vacation?

No. According to UC policy, you must prevent the sharing of passwords or authentication secrets that provide access to Institutional Information and/or IT Resources. Instead, you should work with your IT department or supervisor to set up proper access permissions for your colleague or implement an alternative solution that does not involve sharing your credentials.
Can I contact the Office of the Chief Procurement?
You can contact the Office of the Chief Procurement at ProcurementAdmin@ucop.edu or (510) 987-0768. This information is from the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.
What is the difference between a grant and an award according to this policy?

According to the policy, an award is a legal document that commits parties to a project involving work in exchange for funding, and the term award includes grants as well as contracts and cooperative agreements. This means a grant is a type of award, not a separate category.
When we're considering whether to buy a used vehicle instead of a new one through the State Cooperative Purchasing Program, what two main factors should we evaluate?

According to the policy, you should evaluate two main factors: (1) whether the cost of the used vehicle compares favorably with the cost of a new vehicle purchased through the State Cooperative Purchasing Program, and (2) whether the used vehicle closely approximates the specifications for vehicles purchased through the State Cooperative Purchasing Program, including EPA and Bureau of Automotive Repair standards for the year of manufacture.
hey so like do we gotta follow all the stuff in this doc if we're using federal grant money?

Yes, the policies and requirements in this Bulletin apply to purchases funded by federal agencies to the extent they are in conformance with applicable federal law, the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR), and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) standards, as stated in BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
Does the administrative review documentation require a physical signature, or can we use electronic signatures?
Either method is acceptable. The document must be signed and dated, but this can be done electronically or on paper. The choice between the two is at your discretion.
Is a specific form required to document the loss, damage, or destruction of university equipment under DOD and NASA contracts?
The DOD Form DD 1342/DOD Property Record is prepared as prescribed by the Government Property Administrator, per UC-FA-21-0555.
Um, so like... if the university owns something, what are the rules for like, giving it to someone else or moving it around? Is there like a specific thing I need to follow for that?
The policy is University of California Policy BFB-BUS-38: Disposition of Excess Property and Transfer of University-Owned Property.

What specific criteria and dollar thresholds does the University use to determine whether a $50,000 annual spend category—such as office supplies, IT equipment, or janitorial services—qualifies for inclusion in a Strategic Sourcing Initiative, and at what point would a department's $25,000 request for specialized lab equipment trigger a mandatory sourcing review?

The University identifies items for inclusion in the Strategic Sourcing Initiative if they are purchased by multiple Locations in sufficient quantities to gain an economic advantage, as outlined in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf policy excerpt.
When our campus receives Administrative Fund payments under the Checking Account Option, how should the Controller record the expenditures in the general ledger?

The Controller will transfer the reported expenditures from the cash account to the expenditure account designated for the recipient. All Administrative Fund expenditures must be recorded in the general ledger by the Controller and charged to the same account, fund, and sub-budget associated with the recipient's Administrative Fund allocation.
When we discover a security breach, how do we determine when corrective actions need to be completed?

According to the policy, the timeline for corrective and preventive actions should be mutually agreed upon and based on the nature of the Breach and/or Security Incident. This means the specific timeline will depend on the severity and circumstances of each individual breach or security incident.
Does the policy specify codes that are used to record equipment upon receipt?

The equipment is recorded by receipt date as Code 30 (Purchased, Government Retains Title) or Code 31 (Purchase Order). Policy: UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf
I'm not sure if the standard insurance limits are sufficient for a contractor we're about to hire. Who should I contact to discuss whether we need higher limits?

You should contact your local Risk Management Office. They can assist you in determining if higher insurance limits are needed. If necessary, your local Risk Management Office can also engage the Office of the President, Risk Services, and/or the University's insurance broker to help determine what insurance coverage is appropriate for your specific situation.
If we receive transferred equipment but the original acquisition cost isn't listed on the transfer document, who is responsible for finding out what that value should be?
The Government Property Administrator is responsible for obtaining the value of the equipment when it is not indicated on the transfer document.

As a PI administering federal funds, what insurance coverage and liability requirements must our institution's vendors and service contractors maintain to comply with our federal award terms and conditions?

When contracting for services, the Contractor/External User must meet the established minimum insurance requirements, which can be fulfilled through self-insurance (see [1]). For contracts other than High Risk contracts, a Certificate of Insurance must be provided to the University upon request, showing compliance with these requirements or a signed statement from an authorized officer if self-insured (see [2]). The University’s policy BFB-BUS-63 outlines these minimum insurance requirements, which must be maintained throughout the contract term (see [3]). Exceptions to this policy are only permitted under extenuating circumstances after review by the local Risk Management Office. For high-risk activities, the Contractor/External User must contact their local Risk Management Office early in the contract process to assess risks and determine appropriate insurance requirements (see [4]).
What documentation do we need to provide to the University to demonstrate that we meet the insurance requirements?

You must furnish a Certificate(s) of Insurance indicating compliance with all requirements. Alternatively, if your entity is self-insured, you may provide a signed statement from an authorized officer and evidence of compliance with the established minimum insurance requirements. The University may request this documentation at any time.
When I need to purchase office supplies for my department, what approach should I take to ensure I'm following UC's procurement policy?

You should utilize regional and University-wide pool purchases, strategically sourced commodity agreements, and price schedules to the maximum practicable extent. This approach helps satisfy the University's needs at the lowest overall total cost while fulfilling optimal qualitative requirements through planned, quantity purchasing, which is the core of UC's Strategic Sourcing Initiative.
Can we use reserve funds to purchase a van for departmental/university use?
Yes, the reserve may be used for capital expenditures including equipment, and vans are classified as general purpose vehicles under the policy.
What sampling techniques can we use when Equipment Management conducts verification of our physical inventory?

According to the policy, University locations may incorporate various sampling techniques as part of the verification process, including statistical, stratified, judgmental, purposeful or other sampling or testing methods.
When the Government directs us to dispose of certain items, what steps should our department follow to ensure we're in compliance?
The University should request the Government to remove such items or enter into a storage agreement covering them. (Policy: UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf)
When reporting a security incident, what specific details should I include in my escalation report?
According to the policy, your escalation report should include ticket numbers and system identifiers, as well as a description of the nature of the breach and/or security incident that occurred.
URGENT: What financial liability does an unauthorized person face if a purchase gets canceled?? Need this answered ASAP!

The unauthorized individual may be required to pay the difference between the charges such individual incurred and those the University may reasonably have incurred if the purchase had been properly executed. Policy: BFB-BUS-43
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Who is responsible for maintaining records of re-delegations of the authority to sign tax-free alcohol permit applications?

The CFO Finance is responsible for maintaining a record of re-delegations of the authority to sign tax-free alcohol permit applications. (UC-PS-12-0031_Tax-FreeAlcoholPermitsRecordsOperations (3).pdf)
When I have a goods or services contract valued over $100,000 annually, what am I required to do in the UC Procurement Portal?
You must document the purchase file in the UC Procurement Portal to reflect the reason for the exception.
Can our faculty club purchase office supplies tax-free using the University's procurement process?

Yes, your faculty club can purchase materials not subject to federal tax through the Location's Procurement/Supply Chain Management/Procurement Office, provided that the Chancellor approves this discretionary use. As an organization officially associated with the University, you are eligible for this arrangement with the appropriate approval.
Can I delegate the task of procuring controlled substances to our department purchaser, or do I need to handle it myself?

You may delegate the task of procuring controlled substances, DEA listed chemicals, and California precursor chemicals to your department purchaser, but only with approval from the CSPO (Controlled Substances Program Officer). You cannot delegate this responsibility without obtaining that approval first.
Can UC definitely rely on Section 530 relief when classifying workers as independent contractors?

No, there is uncertainty about whether Section 530 relief is available to UC. According to the policy, there are conflicting rulings regarding the applicability of Section 530 to government agencies and instrumentalities like the University, so it cannot be determined with certainty whether the University can claim Section 530 relief.
If we contract with a physician to provide services at our UC family health clinic, would they be considered an independent contractor or an employee?

Based on the IRS guidance in this policy, a physician providing medical services at a UC family health clinic would likely be classified as an employee rather than an independent contractor. The policy indicates that physicians working at clinics (similar to the example of physicians at family health clinics in Situation #3) who work under contract to provide services would be subject to employment classification, particularly when they follow prescribed routines during fixed hours as part of regular clinic operations.
What should I do if our data processor asks us to verify they've implemented proper security measures for protecting personal data?

According to the policy, you can request that the Processor provide evidence demonstrating their implementation of technical and organizational security measures as required by Applicable Data Protection Law. The Processor is obligated to provide this evidence upon your request as the Controller.
URGENT: Who do I need to contact RIGHT NOW about data protection issues with our data exports?

The data exporter must provide the contact person’s name, position, and contact details in the specified section of the policy. This information should be completed by the data exporter as required by Addendum B to Appendix GDPR - SCC_0.docx.
If we recover stolen equipment that was reported missing six months ago, do we need to file another EIMR to document that it's been found?

Yes. According to the policy, if any stolen equipment is subsequently located, the recovery must be reported to Equipment Management on an Equipment Inventory Modification Request (EIMR, or University location equivalent).
URGENT: What policy do I need to reference RIGHT NOW for university equipment management and control procedures?
The policy BFB-BUS-29: Management and Control of University Equipment outlines the management and control procedures for university equipment.
What are the procedures for participating in 'Take-Away' programs when we have excess property to dispose of?

According to UC Policy BFB-BUS-38, 'Take-Away' programs are available as an option for disposition of excess property. The specific procedures for these programs are detailed in Section V.C. of the policy document.
Under the terms of our federal grant award, are contract workers permissible for specific project roles, and what are the applicable conditions and compliance requirements for their engagement?

Contracting out should be used sparingly and treated as an option of last resort to address temporary needs, not as a means to replace employees with lower-wage contractors. This policy is outlined in Regents Policy 5402.
What should I do if a supplier gives me a receipt that doesn't have enough detail to verify what I purchased with my procurement card?

According to the policy, you must obtain source documentation from the supplier that is sufficient in detail to allow the reviewer to verify the items purchased. If the receipt lacks adequate detail, you should follow your campus's detailed procedures for defining acceptable forms of documentation, which are outlined in this Policy and the UC Sales & Use Tax Manual. You may need to request additional documentation from the supplier that meets these standards.

What is the approval process for purchases exceeding $5,000?
All purchases exceeding $5,000 must be approved by the department head or designee, as specified in University of California Policy BFB-BUS-43.
What are my responsibilities regarding written instructions for equipment that the university owns?

According to the policy, you are responsible for issuing written instructions relating to the acquisition, use, and disposition of inventorial equipment and Government property for which The Regents are responsible.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Can I hire a contractor for a temporary project that doesn't fit into our regular hiring processes?

Regents Policy 5402 allows the University to perform urgent, temporary, or occasional services through its regular hiring processes instead of contracting, as long as the services are not part of a long-term or regular operational need.

messages.content: When our UC location needs to purchase a vehicle valued at $45,000, such as a departmental sedan for faculty transportation, who holds the procurement authority and budget responsibility for this purchase?

The Vehicle Commodity Manager, as designated by the Materiel Manager, Purchasing Director, or Director of Procurement, is responsible for the purchase of vehicles for Location use. This is outlined in UC-PS-12-0029_AcquisitionDispositionUniversityVehicles.pdf.
Who should I contact if I have questions about UC procurement policies and procedures?
You should contact the Office of the Chief Procurement Officer. You can reach them by email at ProcurementAdmin@ucop.edu or by phone at (510) 987-0768.
I just purchased a software license for $6,500. Should I capitalize it as equipment inventory or handle it differently?

No, do not capitalize it as inventorial equipment. Since the software value is $5,000 or more, you should capitalize it using object code 9235 or 9230 (or your University location equivalent) and report it as a CAAN asset instead. However, note that software license fees are expensed regardless of cost, so you should expense this license fee rather than capitalize it.
Is there a difference between Code 30 and Code 31 for University Inventorial Equipment acquisitions?
Code 30 is used for equipment recorded as 'Purchased, Government Retains Title,' while Code 31 is used for equipment recorded as 'Purchase Order.' This information is from the UC-FA-21-0555 policy.
When we need to report excess equipment that isn't industrial plant equipment, which form should we use and what is it called?

You should use the General Services Administration (GSA) Standard Form 120, which is titled 'Report of Excess Personal Property.' This form is the appropriate one for reporting equipment other than industrial plant equipment.
When we receive a new government grant, who is responsible for informing Equipment Management about the reporting requirements and title ownership details?
According to the policy, the Contract and Grant Office is responsible for notifying Equipment Management of the award provisions regarding reporting and vesting of title upon receipt of an award.
What could happen if I remove University equipment from campus without getting the required written approvals first?

According to UC policy BFB-BUS-38, Section VII.D, you must obtain appropriate prior written approvals before removing University or other property. If you remove property without these approvals, it is considered unauthorized removal and may result in criminal proceedings being filed against you.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What factors are considered when determining the need for additional university vehicles?

The policy UC-PS-12-0029_AcquisitionDispositionUniversityVehicles.pdf addresses determining the number of replacement or additional vehicles needed and determining the specification for the new or used vehicles.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Who is responsible for overseeing the University's procurement card program at each campus location?
The Administrator, designated by the Card Program Manager, is responsible for overseeing the Location Procurement Card Program as per the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.

Hey, I just started working here at UC and I'm trying to figure out—are there any rules I need to follow after I leave about conflicts of interest, or is it just something I need to worry about while I'm actually employed here?

Post-employment conflict of interest restrictions for UC employees include: 1) A permanent ban on "switching sides" in cases or proceedings, which likely prohibits former employees from taking positions contrary to their former role or influencing ongoing matters related to their former employment [4]. 2) Restrictions under the Public Contract Code prohibiting contracts to provide goods or services to the UC or related entities for a specified period after leaving employment, to prevent conflicts of interest arising from former positions [4]. Employees are required to consult the Office of the General Counsel or their campus Conflict of Interest Coordinator for specific guidance on these restrictions [4].
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Under what circumstances can bid documents be opened publicly according to the policy?

Bid documents are not opened publicly unless, in the judgment of the Procurement/Supply Chain Director, a public opening will be advantageous to the University. (Policy: BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf)
What should I do with my procurement card if I'm being transferred to a new department next month?
You must follow proper procedures for surrendering your procurement card upon transfer to a new department, as outlined in the UC procurement card policy.
Who has the authority to sign Systemwide Agreements on behalf of the Office of the President?

According to the policy, the Associate Vice President and Chief Procurement Officer has signatory rights for all Office of the President and Systemwide Agreements, including agreements for goods and services. This authority is delegated to them by the Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.
Can I use a different marking method to identify Government inventorial equipment instead of the standard one?

Yes, other methods of marking may be used to identify Government inventorial equipment, but you must first obtain approval from the Government Property Administrator before implementing any alternative marking method.
hey - do I gotta set up a separate record for stuff like accessories that come with plant equipment or can I just lump it all together?
Accessory and auxiliary equipment is recorded on the record of the item of plant equipment. (UC-FA-21-0555)
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Can the University assume liability for the conduct of third parties, such as Contractors or External Users, under a contract?

No. A contract between Contractors/External Users and the University may not include an agreement by which the University assumes liability for conduct of persons other than University officers, agents, employees, students, invitees, and guests. See Regents’ governing documents (currently Regents’ Standing Order 100.4(dd)(9)).
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Can meals or refreshments provided during occasional meetings between students and faculty or administrators be reimbursed under UC policy?
Yes, the cost of meals or light refreshments may also be reimbursed for occasional meetings between students and faculty or administrators, as stated in UC-FA-22-0617_BUS-79.
Who do I need to contact to get the purchase order submitted for our department's university vehicles?
The State shall receive the University's purchase order, as stated in policy BFB-BUS-8.
hey, do we actually need official docs for like every money thing the uni does?
Yes, official documentation is required in support of university financial transactions, as stated in the UC-FO-00-0180_a-000-7 policy.
If a supplier's employee causes damage during a project and UC gets sued, who is responsible for paying UC's legal fees?

According to Article 9.1, the Supplier is responsible for defending and indemnifying UC, which includes paying UC's reasonable attorneys' fees and costs. The Supplier must defend UC against claims arising from the acts or omissions of the Supplier, its employees, agents, sub-suppliers, or anyone under the Supplier's direction and control. However, UC has the right to participate in the defense and must provide prompt notice to the Supplier of any such claim.

As a Principal Investigator managing federal grant funds, what documentation and supporting materials must I maintain and submit to comply with University and federal procurement requirements for expenditures charged to my award?
Official documentation is required in support of university financial transactions, as stated in the Contract and Grant Manual: Chapter 5, Financial-Cost Sharing (UC-FO-00-0180_a-000-7.pdf).
Is there a specific cost threshold for Department of Defense (DOD) equipment under this policy?
The cost threshold for DOD equipment is $15,000 or more, as specified in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
What types of alternative fuels does UC policy recognize for university vehicles?

According to UC policy, recognized alternative fuels include methanol, compressed natural gas, electric power, and liquefied petroleum gas, as referenced in California Health and Safety Code Section 40603.
If we contract out for janitorial services and it results in a current University custodian losing their position, what are we required to do?

According to the policy, displacement of University employees through service contracts should not occur. However, if displacement is unavoidable, the University must make available another position for which the employee is qualified. This alternative position must be in the same bargaining unit and at the same campus, medical center, or laboratory where the employee was displaced. Additionally, the new position cannot result in a reduction in pay and benefits, and the work location cannot change by more than ten miles from the original location.

As the PI on a federally funded project, what training requirements must cardholders complete in accordance with the institutional procurement policy, and what specific topics or competencies does this training cover?
The new cardholder training includes a review of local policies and procedures regarding procurement card usage, as stated in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.

Hi, I'm new here at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and I'm not sure who to reach out to about getting reimbursed for business meeting and entertainment expenses. Could someone point me in the right direction?

For questions regarding business meetings and entertainment expense reimbursements, please contact David Won, Tax Compliance Manager (Email: hui.won@ucop.edu, Phone: (510) 587-604). Policy: UC-FA-22-0617_BUS-79
As the PI on a federally funded project, what are the submission deadlines I need to meet for DOD and NASA property accountability forms related to equipment held by our contracted vendors?
According to UC-FA-21-0555, the DOD Form DD 1662 is due on 31 October, and the NASA Form 1018 is due on 15 October.
How do I determine whether a system falls under Moderate or High digital risk classification?

According to the policy, digital risk classification is determined by the Digital Risk Matrix. Systems classified as Moderate Digital Risk or High Digital Risk should be evaluated using the Digital Risk Matrix provided in BUS-63 to assess which category they fall under.
URGENT: Do vehicles bought through the State Cooperative Purchasing Program HAVE to meet EPA and BAR standards based on when they were made? Need answer ASAP!

Yes, vehicles purchased through the State Cooperative Purchasing Program must comply with EPA and BAR standards for the year of manufacture, as specified in UC-PS-12-0029_AcquisitionDispositionUniversityVehicles.pdf.
What is the data retention timeline for personally identifiable information collected under this federally-funded agreement, and does it comply with the requirements of my funding agency?
Data shall be processed for the duration of the term of this Agreement, except as otherwise specifically set forth herein. Policy: Addendum B to Appendix GDPR - SCC_0.docx
What is the minimum wage I need to pay employees who are performing services for UC?

According to UC policy, you must pay employees performing services for the University of California no less than the UC Fair Wage. This requirement applies to all Suppliers of Fair Wage/Fair Work Services, including Suppliers of Public Works.
As the PI on this federally-funded award, I need to understand who has the authority to approve exceptions to this procurement policy.
The President, in concurrence with the Board Chair, must approve any exceptions to this policy. (Regents Policy 5402_ Policy Generally Prohibiting Contracting for Services)
Should written confirmation of small, diverse, or disadvantaged business status be requested from suppliers?

Yes, the policy requires obtaining written representation (either/or federal and state) from suppliers regarding their status as a small, diverse, or disadvantaged supplier, as outlined in BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf, Section B.
What is the deadline for a Supplier to report a vulnerability that has been rated as CVE Critical?
According to the policy, a Supplier must report any vulnerability rated as CVE High or Critical within twenty (20) business days.

What specific information must be included in the University's management and control system for inventorial equipment valued at $5,000 or more, such as documenting the original purchase price of $8,500 for a laboratory microscope, the acquisition date, physical location in Building B Room 215, current condition status, and depreciation schedules for assets like a $12,000 computer server?

The University's management and control system for inventorial equipment, at a minimum, must provide the following information: Property Number, Description, Equipment Classification Code, Manufacturer’s Name, Manufacturer’s Model Number, Serial Number (if available), Cost, Acquisition Code, and CAAN / Building and Room Number. This requirement is outlined in the UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf policy.
How do I know which disclosure category applies to my position when filing Form 700?

You should review your Disclosure Category as defined by the UC Conflict-of-Interest Code. The scope of what you must disclose on Form 700 is determined by which disclosure category your position falls under according to the UC Conflict-of-Interest Code.
Wait, so if I'm borrowing some equipment from somewhere, do I like... have to make some kind of property thing for it? Like, is that something the rules say I have to do?
Yes, Equipment Management shall create a property record for each item of borrowed equipment, using the appropriate acquisition code. (Policy: UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29)
If our department sells approved excess property, how should we handle the money we receive from the sale?

All proceeds from the sale must be routed to the Surplus Administrator for deposit into the appropriate income account. After that deposit is made, your department's share of the proceeds will be appropriated to it. However, if your University location has decentralized its sales of excess property, the proceeds must be deposited according to your local policies instead.
If UC contracts out a service that my department currently provides, could I be laid off?

No, according to Article 5, contracts for covered services shall not displace University employees. Displacement includes layoff, so UC cannot lay you off as a result of contracting out covered services.
Under our federal grant award, what is the disposition of unobligated funds from our annual allocation that surpass the allowable carryforward threshold?
Any unused portion beyond 25% of a recipient's annual allocation must be returned to the accounting office at the end of the fiscal year. This is outlined in UC-FO-00-0190_a-253-27.pdf.

Um, so like... who's actually in charge of making sure all the stuff that UC needs to buy actually gets ordered and shows up? Like, is there one person doing this, or is it a whole department thing, or...?
The Procurement Office is responsible for managing the supply chain, as stated in policy BFB-BUS-43.

If I want to use a $15,000 confocal microscope in the biology lab for a personal research project that could potentially generate $5,000-$10,000 in outside revenue, do I need to obtain written approval from the department before proceeding, and what are the potential liability costs if I use it without authorization?

No, employees shall not use University property or property in the care and custody of the University for personal purposes without pre-approval by the Chancellor or Laboratory Director. This is outlined in UC-FA-21-0555.
As a UC staff member, what policy should I review to understand the rules about conflict of interest situations that might affect my employment?

You should review Personnel Policies for Staff Members (PPSM) 82: Conflict of Interest, which was last updated on July 14, 2016. This policy outlines the conflict of interest requirements that apply to UC staff members.
Are there consequences for misconduct in procurement processes?

The Compendium of Conflict of Interest and Related Policies – Guidance states that unacceptable conduct is subject to sanctions outlined in APM 016, which may be applied when misconduct is substantiated by a formal process.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What qualifies as an incentive under the procurement policy?

Incentives include gifts (monetary or free goods/services), cash or credits based on total purchases, and any other value provided by a supplier to the University. This definition is outlined in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
If we discover a security breach involving our vendor's systems on a Friday evening, how quickly do we need to designate a contact person and notify UC?

According to the policy, you must designate a contact person within 72 calendar hours after the discovery of the Breach and/or Security Incident. This contact person will be the point of contact to whom UC directs inquiries and who will communicate your responses to UC. So in your Friday evening scenario, you would have until Monday evening at the latest to complete this requirement.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What types of documentation are required for procurement transactions according to the policy?

The policy requires documentation such as requests and approvals, invoices, receipts, packing lists, or other documentation confirming billing and receipt, as outlined in BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
Can our CSPO delegate their authority to sign DEA registrations to another staff member without getting a new Power of Attorney from the Chancellor?

Yes, according to the policy, the CSPO or other authorized personnel may authorize additional individuals to sign institutional DEA registrations or issue orders for Schedule I or II Controlled Substances through their own Power of Attorney, unless the Chancellor's original Power of Attorney specifically restricts them from doing so.
Like, who's actually in charge of buying all those cars and trucks that the UC campus uses? Is that like a specific person's job or a whole department or something?

The Vehicle Commodity Manager, as designated by the Materiel Manager, Purchasing Director, or Director of Procurement, is responsible for the purchase of vehicles for Location use. This is outlined in UC-PS-12-0029_AcquisitionDispositionUniversityVehicles.pdf.
Is a non-negotiable gift certificate an allowable retirement gift for an employee?

Yes, a non-negotiable gift certificate for tangible personal property may be presented to an employee under the retirement award category, subject to the requirements described in the section on allowable awards for employee recognition (see above). Policy: UC-FA-23-672_BFB-G-41_EmployeeNon-CashAwardGifts_Accessible.pdf
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
I want to hire an independent contractor for $15,000. What do I need to do?

To hire an independent contractor for $15,000, follow these steps: 1. Ensure the contractor meets the criteria for an independent contractor under UC guidelines, including full discretion over their work and only being subject to the direction of an attending physician (per [1][2]). 2. Verify the contractor is not misclassified as an employee; they must operate independently and provide their own taxes, benefits, and insurance. 3. Execute a written contract outlining scope of work, payment terms, and independent contractor status. 4. Confirm the contractor is not a small business concern (unless re-representing size status per [3]), though small business reporting requirements do not apply here since the contract amount ($15,000) is below the $700,000 threshold for federal reporting. 5. Maintain records to demonstrate compliance with independent contractor guidelines and procurement policies.

Wait, so when people have like, lunches or dinners for work stuff, how do you even decide if it's okay to pay for that? Like, what things are you supposed to think about before you say yes to spending money on food for a meeting?

The approving authority must consider reasonableness, allowability, benefit to the University, budget, availability of funds, cost-effectiveness, and the best use of public funds, as outlined in UC-FA-22-0617_BUS-79.
If we need to purchase office supplies and there's no strategically sourced agreement in place, what's the maximum dollar amount where we're required to consider Small Business or DVBE suppliers?

The maximum dollar amount is $250,000. According to the policy, the University requires the purchase of goods and services from Small Business (SB) or Disabled Veteran Business Enterprise (DVBE) suppliers for amounts not exceeding the $250,000 small business purchase threshold, when strategically sourced agreements do not exist.
How does the University determine whether someone should be classified as an independent contractor versus an employee?

According to UC policy, two key factors are considered: (1) whether the worker makes their services available to other employers, and (2) whether the University pays the worker by the hour, week, or month rather than by commission or by the job. If a worker makes services available to other employers and is paid by commission or by the job rather than hourly/weekly/monthly, they are more likely to be classified as an independent contractor.
Do I need to get written approval from the Government Property Administrator before we spend government funds on a major repair to federally-funded equipment?
Yes. According to the policy, you must obtain written approval from the Government Property Administrator prior to effecting any major repair or rehabilitation at cost to the government.
As a UC employee handling electronic protected health information (ePHI), what safeguards am I required to implement?

You must use appropriate safeguards and comply with 45 C.F.R. § 164 Subpart C with respect to ePHI to prevent the use or disclosure of PHI other than as provided for by the Underlying Agreement(s) and the Appendix BAA.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
If equipment is not listed as a specific deliverable in an award, what form must the University submit to the Agency, and which policy outlines this requirement?

The University must submit a Department of Defense DD Form 1419/DOD Industrial Plant Equipment Requisition to the Agency, as outlined in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
Should application access methods used in development or testing be removed or disabled before moving software/systems to production?

Before software or systems are moved into production, Units must ensure that all application/program access methods utilized in development or testing, other than the formal user access methods or formally defined interfaces, are: deleted, disabled, or formally documented by the Unit as a production feature in the Risk Assessment. (Policy BFB-IS-3)
What's our responsibility and next steps if there's a personal data breach on our end under this contract?
Any personal data breach may be grounds for immediate termination of the Agreement by Controller, as stated in appendix-gdpr-eea-uk-4-27-21.pdf.
URGENT: Need immediate clarification - am I eligible to participate in UC procurement if I'm a small shareholder with only $25,000 or less invested? This needs to be resolved NOW.

Yes, under the *Exception Regulation: 18702.1(b) Small Shareholder Exception*, individuals with a shareholder investment interest valued at $25,000 or less are exempt from certain conflict of interest provisions. This policy is outlined in *Conflict of Interest Training-Procurement-2024.pdf*.
hey quick q - can i charge a meal to the entertainment budget if it's for like a donor thing? does that fall under the policy?
Yes, entertainment expenditures include meals and light refreshments for events that support the University’s mission, such as donor cultivation, as defined in UC-FA-22-0617_BUS-79.
Where can I find information about how UC handles information security during business continuity situations?
According to the policy document, information security aspects of business continuity are covered in Section 17 on page 34 of the UC Information Security policy.
Hey, I'm new here and still getting up to speed - could someone clarify who's responsible for registering aircraft and watercraft according to UC policy?

The designated University location representative secures required federal and state registration for all aircraft and watercraft, as stated in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
When we have a specific University-controlled fund source with terms that conflict with what's outlined in this Bulletin, which one do we follow?
The more restrictive of the two shall apply, as stated in the policy set forth in UC-FA-22-0617_BUS-79 Bus Meetings Entertainment_updated-accessible_12.15.2022.pdf.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Do I need to create a separate inventory record for each quantity purchase?
Yes, a separate inventory sheet should be prepared for each quantity purchase, as stated in the Administrative Fund Inventory Record guidelines under UC-FO-00-0190_a-253-27.
Can we extend a UC contract for goods and services beyond ten years if we get special approval?

No. According to the policy, the maximum duration of any UC contract for goods and/or services, including the initial term and all amendments or extensions combined, cannot exceed ten years. While exceptions to policy require approval by the appropriate Policy Exception Authority, this authority would need to grant an exception to the ten-year maximum duration policy itself, not simply extend an existing contract beyond that limit.
When a department purchases $5,000 worth of office supplies from another UC campus department, is the SSPR Form required for this interdepartmental transaction?
No, you do not need to use this form for internal use, only with outside vendors. (Policy: UC SOURCE SELECTION & PRICE REASONABLENESS (SSPR) FORM – FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS)
I retired from UC last month from a policy-making position in procurement. Can I immediately contract with the University to provide consulting services?

Yes, you can contract with the University immediately following your retirement to provide consulting services, provided that you did not participate in any way while serving as an employee in the making of that specific contract. However, if you propose to sell or lease goods to the University instead, the post-employment restrictions apply, meaning you must wait until at least one year has elapsed since your separation from University employment.
Who do I need to contact to find out if something we have is considered excess property?

Surplus Administrators, in consultation with the custodial department if necessary, are responsible for determining whether an item has no further value to the University and can be disposed of as excess property, as outlined in UC-PS-12-0068.
What should I do with equipment that we're not currently using but will need again in the future?

You should store any temporarily idle equipment that is required for authorized future use in accordance with sound business practices. The equipment must be adequately protected from corrosion, contamination, and damage to sensitive parts. Additionally, you must note the exact storage location on the equipment records.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What information needs to be provided in the 'Data importer(s)' section of the SCC clauses?

The UC must complete the 'Data importer(s)' section with their details, including the name as 'Regents of the University of California, on behalf of its ______ location' and the address, as specified in the policy Addendum B to Appendix GDPR - SCC_0.docx.

metadata.source: Addendum B to Appendix GDPR - SCC_0.docx

messages.content: What procedures must be followed to properly close out an intercampus loan arrangement under our federally funded project, and are there specific documentation or reporting requirements I need to fulfill with my grants office?

The lending department shall inform Equipment Management when the loan is terminated. Equipment Management shall inform its counterpart at the borrowing University location of the loan termination, in case the borrowing department has not notified it. (UC-FA-21-0555)

Hey, I'm new here and I'm trying to understand the prequalification process - once someone gets prequalified as a bidder, can we still reject them later on, or is prequalification like a guaranteed green light?

Yes, the Procurement/Supply Chain Director may determine that a prequalified bidder should be rejected or that a rejected bidder should be prequalified based on subsequent information, as stated in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
Is the department manager responsible for approving the EIMR before it is sent to Equipment Management?
The receiving department approves the EIMR and sends it to Equipment Management. (UC-FA-21-0555)
What documents do I need to keep on file to substantiate accounts receivable transactions?

According to UC policy, substantiating documents for accounts receivable transactions include: Financial Journal (U FIN 288), Financial Journal created by a computerized subsystem, sundry debtor bills and sundry debtor bill cancellations, copies of bills or listings showing payment details, promissory notes, and vendor credit memos.
What information do I need to include when submitting an Equipment Inventory Modification Request for loaned equipment?

According to the policy, you must list all equipment being loaned and provide the property number and new location of the equipment on the Equipment Inventory Modification Request (EIMR) or equivalent form when sending it to Equipment Management.

If our department has $15,000 worth of excess laboratory equipment that we no longer need, who should we contact to report it, and what are the specific steps we need to follow to properly dispose of or reallocate these items?

You should report any excess property immediately to the Contract and Grant Officer, or their designee, who will then report to the Government Contracting Officer. This is outlined in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
What are the ownership requirements for a business to be certified as a DVBE?

To be certified as a DVBE, the business must be at least 51% owned by one or more disabled veterans. If the business is structured as a limited liability company, it must be wholly owned by one or more disabled veterans. Additionally, daily business operations must be managed and controlled by one or more disabled veterans.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What factors determine if a worker is classified as an independent contractor under UC policy?

Under GU-FA-20-0506_UCIndependentContractorGuidelines_Accessible.pdf, a worker is classified as an independent contractor if: i. The employer had a reasonable basis for treating the worker as an independent contractor; and ii. The employer treated workers performing similar services as independent contractors.
Does the President have the authority to execute contracts on behalf of the University?

Yes, according to Bylaw 30, the President has been delegated the authority to execute on behalf of the Corporation all contracts and other documents necessary in the exercise of the President's duties. However, this authority does not extend to activities within the responsibility of the Principal Officers.
If we receive a security patch from our medical device supplier, how quickly do we need to make it available to UC?

According to the policy, the supplier must provide all patches and security updates to UC within thirty (30) days of the patch's commercial release, or as otherwise recommended by the supplier or their sub-supplier, whichever is earlier. This means UC should receive the patches within whichever timeframe is sooner.
Are suppliers prohibited from using Institutional Information and IT Resources for purposes other than providing the Goods and/or Services?
No. Suppliers may not access or use Institutional Information and IT Resources for any purpose except to provide the Goods and/or Services. This is outlined in the appendix-data-security.pdf policy.

Under the federal grant's effort reporting requirements, if I teach multiple short courses throughout the award year, does the 12-calendar-day limitation apply independently to each individual course or to the aggregate of all short course instruction combined?

The 12-calendar-day limit applies cumulatively across all courses taught in a calendar year, as each day devoted to teaching counts toward the total, regardless of the number of hours worked per day. This is specified in GU-FA-20-0506, sections c and d.
How do I determine if I should split a purchase order into separate transactions for equipment and its installation?

According to the policy, you should consider three key factors to determine if separate transactions are advantageous to the University: time, cost, and supplier requirements. Evaluate whether separating the equipment purchase from the installation would be beneficial based on these factors before proceeding.

Um, so like... when stuff shows up, who's supposed to make sure that what's actually in the boxes matches what the paper says should be there? And also check if anything looks broken or messed up when it arrives? Is that someone's job or...?

The Receiving Department, whether University location Receiving or the custodial department, determines that the number of packages corresponds to the bill of lading and that there is no visible damage. Policy: UC-FA-21-0555
As a PI relocating to another institution, what are the approval procedures I need to follow to transfer equipment purchased with federal grant funds?

Yes, as part of Faculty relocations to other institutions, you must coordinate and approve all transfers of University property, including no-cost transfers, and approve all donations of surplus property. (UC-FA-21-0555)
Does UC Policy G-13 cover moving expense reimbursement for all employee classifications at the university?

No. According to UC Policy G-13, moving expense reimbursement applies specifically to Managers and Senior Professionals (MSP) and Professional and Support Staff (PSS) personnel. Other employee classifications are not covered under this policy.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
If a company provides office space, secretarial services, and materials to an individual working on a project, is that individual considered an employee or independent contractor?

The individual is considered an independent contractor under the policy, as the company provided office and desk space, secretarial and telephone services, and all necessary materials and equipment, which aligns with the facts outlined in GU-FA-20-0506_UCIndependentContractorGuidelines_Accessible.pdf.
URGENT: Need immediate clarification - are other discretionary funds held to the same regulatory standards as Administrative Funds or not?!
Yes, they are subject to the same regulations and reporting requirements applicable to Administrative Funds, as stated in UC-FO-00-0190_a-253-27.pdf.
What additional approvals do I need to get for a property transfer request beyond the standard approvals already listed in subsection 1.c?

According to the policy, in addition to the approvals listed under subsection 1.c, your property transfer request must also be approved by the entities specified in subsection 1.c.ii. The policy excerpt does not detail which additional approvers are required, but it indicates there are supplementary approval requirements beyond the standard ones, and you should consult the complete subsection 1.c.ii for the specific list of required approvers.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What documentation is required to demonstrate a sound business need for contracting out services exceeding $100,000 per year?

To demonstrate a sound business need, the policy requires selecting at least one option (e.g., responding to budgetary limitations) and providing supporting documentation, such as a complete financial analysis comparing the actual cost of performing services in-house (including all related costs and administrative expenses) to the cost of contracting for services (including the total contract cost and associated administrative costs). This comparison must be articulated over the life of the contract. (Policy: GU-HR-23-0643_ContractingforServices_Accessible.pdf)
If my supervisor verbally tells me that UC is waiving a particular contract requirement for our vendor, does that waiver apply?

No. According to Section 18.6 of the UC Terms and Conditions, no waiver of a provision or nonperformance of an obligation is effective unless it is in writing in accordance with Article 18.7. Verbal waivers, even from supervisors, do not constitute valid waivers under this policy. Any waiver must be documented in writing and signed by both parties' authorized representatives to be enforceable.
If I'm uncertain about what a specific clause in a sponsored research award means, who should I contact for clarification?
You should refer your question concerning the interpretation of specific award clauses to the University location Contract and Grant Office.
Hey, I'm new here and trying to understand the procurement process - what exactly should we be documenting in our management and control system when it comes to inventorial equipment?

The University's management and control system for inventorial equipment, at a minimum, must provide the following information: Property Number, Description, Equipment Classification Code, Manufacturer’s Name, Manufacturer’s Model Number, Serial Number (if available), Cost, Acquisition Code, and CAAN / Building and Room Number. This requirement is outlined in the UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf policy.
If I was a contract worker doing the same job for 12 months and get hired as a UC employee, do I still have to complete the full probationary period?

No, you will receive three months of credit toward the standard probationary period. This means if the standard probationary period is 12 months, you would only need to complete 9 additional months as a UC employee since your 12 months as a contract worker counts for 3 months of the probationary requirement.
