A Data Security Appendix is required in a vendor contract when the contract involves processing personal data, financial information, health data, or other sensitive information under UC policies. It is also required when the vendor has access to UC systems, networks, or data, or when the contract involves data processing activities that necessitate compliance with UC data security standards. Specific requirements are outlined in [1], [2], [3], and [4] of the appendix, which detail scope, obligations, and data protection measures.
Is there a designated individual responsible for overseeing the University's procurement card program at each campus location?
The Administrator, designated by the Card Program Manager, is responsible for overseeing the Location Procurement Card Program as per the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
If we receive a price decrease notice from the lessor's supplier, are we required to pass that savings through to UC immediately?
Yes. According to the policy, the Lessor agrees to immediately notify UC of any price decreases from its Lessors and to pass through to UC any price decreases.
Who should I contact at UC regarding FERPA and data security compliance for our federally-funded project's data exports?

The data exporter must provide the contact person’s name, position, and contact details in the specified section of the policy. This information should be completed by the data exporter as required by Addendum B to Appendix GDPR - SCC_0.docx.
URGENT: What do departments NEED to provide RIGHT NOW regarding technical data for equipment management?

Departments must provide, in timely fashion, all descriptive and operating technical data required to enable Equipment Management, Extramural Accounting, the Contracts and Grants office or other departments involved to meet the reporting requirements of the awarding or other agencies. (Policy BFB-BUS-29)

So like, if we're using that government money to buy parts for equipment we already have, how do we... um... label it or whatever for when we have to tell people about it? Does the equipment get a different code or something?

The entire piece of equipment shall be coded as Government Inventorial Equipment for purposes of reporting to Office of the President (EFA 100), as per UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
I retired from UC last year. Can I now contact the media about a project I worked on during my employment?

Yes, you can communicate with the press. According to the policy, communications with the press are explicitly permitted activities for former UC employees. However, note that this permission applies to communications generally - you should still ensure any information you share complies with other applicable laws regarding confidentiality or proprietary information.
URGENT: Does a UC employee need to return their old computer when they leave, or can they take it home for personal use? Need answer ASAP!

No. As indicated under Section III.E.1. of University of California Policy BFB-BUS-38, "Regardless of value or condition... in no case may a University employee remove, or cause to be removed, excess property from University premises for personal use..."
hey do you know which office handles recording costs for inventory equipment we buy through POs?

The Accounting Office records the cost of inventorial equipment acquired through purchase orders, as outlined in UC Accounting Manual, Chapter P-415-2, Plant Accounting: Costing and Reconciling Inventorial Equipment Acquisitions.
What types of procurement-related matters should I direct to the Procurement Services Staff for input from the Director?

According to the policy, you should direct questions related to Strategic Sourcing Agreements, Price Schedule Agreements, Commodity Planning, and other procurement-related questions to the Procurement Services Staff, who will provide input from the Director on these matters.
If I discuss a potential contract with a vendor during my employment at UC, does that automatically trigger the post-employment conflict of interest ban?

No, simply discussing a potential contract during your employment would not be sufficient to trigger the ban. The ban only applies if the details of the potential contract and the likelihood of a contract were 'arranged' during your employment at the University.
What information do I need to include in the equipment records when documenting university equipment?
According to the policy, all equipment records must include the manufacturer, model number, and serial number information for each piece of equipment.
How long do we need to keep copies of the Gift, Contribution, and Miscellaneous Expenses report (UFIN 110) in our department files?

According to the retention period specified in the policy, the Office of Record in Accounting must retain the report for 5 years. Other copies may be kept for 0-5 years, meaning they can be retained anywhere from immediately discarded to 5 years, depending on your department's needs.

Hey, I'm new here and still getting up to speed on our procurement policies. Can you help me understand - when we replace parts of a system, is that considered maintenance, or are there specific situations where it's handled differently?

Replacement of components and equipment is considered maintenance if it is required on a routine or recurring basis and does not constitute replacement of greater than 50% of the replacement value of that system. Maintenance does not include erection, construction, alteration, repair, or improvement of University structures, buildings, roads, or other improvements. (Policy: BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main)
How long do I need to keep usage logs for controlled substances after they've been completely used or disposed of?
According to UC policy, you must maintain usage logs for three (3) years after the full use or disposal of controlled substances, as required under California Business and Professions Code § 4105.
I just started here and I'm trying to understand the timeline—after we finish doing a physical inventory, when should we expect to get the listing and signed statement back?

The listing and signed statement will be furnished with a minimum of delay at the completion of the physical inventory, as stated in the UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf policy.
If a department requests delivery of materials in an unreasonably short timeframe, what should the Procurement/Supply Chain Director do before issuing a solicitation?

According to the policy, the Procurement/Supply Chain Director must verify the needs and determine whether the specification requirements, including the abnormally short delivery or performance times, are reasonable and necessary prior to soliciting a quotation. This verification process helps avoid paying premium costs that may be required to meet unrealistic timelines.
I'm a UC researcher who needs to purchase specialized equipment from a company where my spouse owns 8% of the shares. Can I still proceed with this purchase?

No, you cannot proceed with this purchase. According to the Conflict of Interest Statement, no UC employee or near relative of a UC employee can hold more than a 10% ownership or controlling interest in the supplier. Since your spouse owns 8% of the company, this falls within the restricted range and presents a conflict of interest. The only exception noted in the policy is if you have teaching or research responsibilities and the goods or service is not commercial, which would not apply to purchasing equipment from a company in which your spouse has ownership interest.
As an instructor of technical classes at the conservatory, what are my primary responsibilities if I'm classified as Group A?

As a Group A instructor of technical classes, you are required to spend designated hours instructing regular conservatory classes, conducting examinations, and performing other duties as occasionally required by the conservatory. These are core responsibilities associated with your regular remuneration position.
Can my department get delegated purchasing authority outside the Procurement Department?

Yes, it is possible. The Procurement/Supply Chain Director may provide delegated purchasing authority to individuals outside the Purchasing Department if your department meets the conditions. Specifically, your department must have a historical level of purchase activity that is sufficient, in the judgment of the Procurement/Supply Chain Director, to ensure that a higher level of authority will result in more cost effective procurement.
What are the allowable conditions under which the Laboratory may utilize Strategic Sourcing agreements in compliance with federal grant requirements and institutional policy?

Strategic Sourcing agreements may be used by the Laboratory when agreements are cost effective and there is no conflict with federal requirements, as stated in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
Can I get reimbursed for a farewell dinner I'm organizing for a colleague who is leaving the university after 3 years of service?

No, you cannot be reimbursed for a farewell gathering. According to the policy, entertainment expenses for farewell gatherings are not allowed, with the exception only for celebrations related to retirement or for employees separating from University employment with at least 5 years of service. Since your colleague has only 3 years of service, this expense would be unallowable.
Am I required to use the university's approved vendor list when purchasing office supplies for my department?

The provided excerpt does not contain sufficient detail to answer this question. While the policy is titled 'Purchases of Goods and Services; Supply Chain Management,' the excerpt text itself was not included in the source material. To provide an accurate answer about vendor requirements, the full policy content would need to be reviewed.
When we acquire equipment through the State Surplus Property Program, what acquisition code should we use to record it in our system?
Equipment secured through the State Surplus Property Program should be recorded using acquisition code 31 (Purchase Order).
Who has the authority to make the final decision on whether to contract for services according to this policy?

According to the policy, the final decision on whether to contract for services is made by the Chancellor or a designated Vice Chancellor, with review by the Office of the President as appropriate and as described in the Guidelines.

When is a Data Security Appendix required in a vendor contract?

A Data Security Appendix is required in a vendor contract when the contract involves processing personal data, financial information, health data, or other sensitive information under UC policies. It is also required when the vendor has access to UC systems, networks, or data, or when the contract involves data processing activities that necessitate compliance with UC data security standards. Specific requirements are outlined in [1], [2], [3], and [4] of the appendix, which detail scope, obligations, and data protection measures.
yo so like what do cardholders gotta do after they finish the training thing?

The cardholder must sign an agreement stating he/she acknowledges and understands the requirements associated with the proper use of the card, as outlined in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
Can I use Administrative Funds to purchase season tickets to the symphony, and if so, how should I handle the inventory tracking?

Yes, you can purchase season tickets to musical events using Administrative Funds for the purpose of using individual tickets as official entertainment or as occasional gifts. You should maintain an Administrative Fund Inventory Record for Quantity Purchases (Exhibit VI) for the season tickets and report this to the accounting office at fiscal year end.

How frequently should we conduct formal reviews of our $2-5M equipment inventory to identify surplus assets exceeding departmental utilization rates, and what dollar threshold should trigger a mandatory disposition review?
The policy requires periodically reviewing current property needs to identify excess property. (Policy: UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf)
As a department admin, what reporting duties does the Small Business Officer handle?
A Small Business Officer may have responsibility for filing annual Small Business Reports with the Office of the President, as outlined in BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
As a Chancellor, am I eligible to use the Checking Account Option for Administrative Fund disbursements?
Yes, as a Chancellor, you are eligible to use the Checking Account Option. According to the policy, the Checking Account Option is available to the President, Chancellors, and LBNL Director.
How does the level of control a UC hospital exercises over workers factor into determining whether they should be classified as employees rather than independent contractors?

According to the policy excerpt, the IRS considers whether the hospital exercises sufficient control over workers to ensure the hospital's success or failure as a key factor in employee classification. If a UC hospital exercises sufficient control over workers' duties and performance in a way that affects the hospital's success or failure, this indicates an employment relationship rather than an independent contractor relationship.
When evaluating whether a Strategic Sourcing Initiative provides economic advantage to the University, what two types of cost reductions should we consider?

According to BUS-43, both administrative cost avoidance (a reduction of internal administrative costs) and price avoidance (a reduction of the price increases of the commodity) should be considered in determining economic advantage.
A department purchases a laboratory microscope for $750. What form must be completed to document this individual equipment item?

The Department of Defense (DOD) Form DD 1342/DOD Property Record may be used for individual record cards for items costing between $500 and $1,000. (UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf)
When we trade in old equipment as part of a new equipment purchase, should we list the traded-in equipment on the purchase order, and how should we value the new equipment?

Yes, the traded-in equipment, including its property number(s), must be listed on the purchase order for the new equipment. The new equipment should be valued at its full list price, with the trade-in credit not deducted from that valuation.
hey so if i'm teaching a bunch of short courses throughout the year, does the 12-day limit reset for each course or is it like a total thing added up together?

The 12-calendar-day limit applies cumulatively across all courses taught in a calendar year, as each day devoted to teaching counts toward the total, regardless of the number of hours worked per day. This is specified in GU-FA-20-0506, sections c and d.
What policies are governing administrative fund expenditures RIGHT NOW according to the policy excerpt—need this answered ASAP!
The policy excerpt states that administrative fund expenditures are governed by the policies and business and finance bulletins mentioned in UC-FO-00-0190_a-253-27.pdf.
Do we need to get approval before using AI systems that can access UC's institutional data?

No, the use of AI systems with UC Institutional Information is not permitted except with prior written consent from the Chancellor or delegate for the applicable UC Location(s) or as explicitly set forth in the SOW. Policy: UC Terms and Conditions-04-01-25.pdf
As a Principal Investigator managing federal grant funds, what documentation must I maintain to support all expenditures charged to my award in accordance with federal compliance requirements?
Official documentation is required in support of university financial transactions, as stated in policy UC-FO-00-0180_a-000-7.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Who has the authority to make final decisions on procurement decisions for services?

The Chancellor or designated Vice Chancellor has the authority to make final decisions, with review by the Office of the President as appropriate. Policy: GU-HR-23-0643_ContractingforServices_Accessible.pdf
As the PI on this federal grant, I need to understand: who is authorized to negotiate reasonable prices and terms on our procurements to ensure we're meeting federal compliance requirements?
The Procurement/Supply Chain Director has the authority to negotiate reasonable prices and terms when determined appropriate, as stated in BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
Does this Business Associate Agreement apply to all UC health care components, or just the one I work for?

This BA Agreement applies to all UC health care components. UC has designated all of its HIPAA health care components as a single component of its hybrid entity, known as the Single Health Care Component (SHCC), so the BA Agreement is binding on all other UC health care components collectively.
Do I need to submit Form DD 1851 before purchasing a new server for our DoD-funded research lab that costs $28,000?

Yes. According to UC policy, prior to acquiring Department of Defense automatic data processing equipment with a cost of $25,000 or more, the University must submit Form DD 1851 to the Director of the Defense Automation Resources Management Program Center (DARMPC). Since your server costs $28,000, it meets the $25,000 threshold and requires this submission before purchase.
When I'm preparing a Request for Proposal, am I required to include small, diverse, and disadvantaged suppliers in my solicitation?
Yes. According to UC policy, you must make a concerted effort to target and solicit responses from small, diverse, and disadvantaged suppliers in all Requests for Information, Quotation, or Proposal.
What is my responsibility as a cardholder when it comes to committing University funds?

As a cardholder, you must formally authorize new cardholders and ensure that any commitments of University funds are made in accordance with the policy's provisions regarding Low Value Purchases. You are responsible for following the specific guidelines outlined in this policy when using your card to commit funds on behalf of the University.
Do we need to competitively bid a purchase agreement if we're planning to spend $150,000 annually on office supplies?

Yes. According to California Public Contract Code Section 10507 et seq., all Purchase Agreements involving an expenditure of more than $100,000 annually must be competitively bid, unless an exception applies. Since your planned expenditure of $150,000 annually exceeds the $100,000 threshold, competitive bidding is required unless a specific exception to this requirement is applicable.
As a department admin, am I able to establish a services or goods contract with someone who is employed by UC?
No, services/goods contracts are prohibited with UC Officers and Employees per Public Contract Code Section 10516 in Conflict of Interest Training-Procurement-2024.pdf.
Can I use administrative funds to purchase office supplies for my department?

Based on the excerpt provided, I cannot give a definitive answer. The excerpt only shows the table of contents indicating that sections on 'Examples of Allowable and Unallowable Expenditures' exist, but the actual details of what is allowable or unallowable are not included in this excerpt. You would need to review section B of the complete policy document to determine whether office supplies are permitted administrative fund expenditures.
Can I provide meals to employees more frequently than normal if they have to work through their regular lunch break?

Yes, according to the policy, meals provided to employees who are required to be at their work stations during a normal meal time may be furnished on a more frequent basis. However, you should refer to Section III.A.2.e for specific guidelines on how frequently this can occur.
How often do we need to review our Electronic Information Security procedures to stay compliant with UC Policy BFB-IS-3?

According to UC Policy BFB-IS-3, you must adhere to a documented periodic review cycle, with a minimum requirement of at least one review every three years. The CIO-appointed committee, unit head, or assigned designee is responsible for conducting these reviews.

As a PI managing federal grant funds, how should I handle situations where a team member involved in procurement decisions for grant-related purchases has a potential financial conflict of interest, and what are my reporting obligations to the University and federal sponsors?

The employee must not participate in the decision-making process, as prohibited by the California Political Reform Act and Government Code Section 81000-81016, and the University Conflict of Interest Code must be observed per the policy BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
If our clinic terminates a physician's contract, do we need to provide a reason for the termination?

No, according to the policy, the contract between the clinic and the physician can be terminated at any time, with or without cause, by either the clinic or the physician. This means a reason does not need to be provided for termination.
Can we use depreciation charges the same way we use money from selling off University vehicles in our department?

Yes, funds generated from depreciation charges may be utilized in the same manner as funds obtained through the disposition of vehicles, as stated in UC-PS-12-0029_AcquisitionDispositionUniversityVehicles.pdf.
What internal records and documentation do we need to maintain so UC can verify our HIPAA compliance during an audit?

You must make your internal practices, books, and records relating to the use and disclosure of PHI (Protected Health Information) available to UC and to the Secretary for purposes of determining UC's compliance with HIPAA, HITECH, and their implementing regulations. This includes maintaining documentation that allows UC to verify your compliance activities.
Can I use my departmental budget to take a client to lunch during a business meeting to discuss a potential contract?

Yes, you can use departmental budget for business meal entertainment, provided it is a reasonable expenditure directly related to conducting University business. However, you must follow UC Policy BUS-79 requirements, which include obtaining proper approval before the expenditure, documenting the business purpose, attendees, and date, and ensuring the amount is reasonable and appropriate. The meal must be connected to a legitimate business objective such as discussing contracts, partnerships, or other official University matters.
hey quick q - do vendors have to follow any specific sustainability stuff when they're working with UC?

Yes, suppliers must conduct business using environmentally, socially, and economically sustainable products and services as defined in the UC Sustainable Practices Policy (https://policy.ucop.edu/doc/3100155) and the UC Sustainable Procurement Guidelines.
Can full drum deliveries be made from Storehouse Stock?
The policy prohibits full drum deliveries from Storehouse Stock at any time, as outlined in UC-PS-12-0031_Tax-FreeAlcoholPermitsRecordsOperations (3).pdf.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What factors should be considered when approving meal expenses for business meetings?

The approving authority must consider reasonableness, allowability, benefit to the University, budget, availability of funds, cost-effectiveness, and the best use of public funds, as outlined in UC-FA-22-0617_BUS-79.

If we determine that government property is no longer needed for our award, what steps should we take before declaring it excess?

Before declaring government property excess, it shall be screened against the needs of other awards. If there is a need for the property, the Government Contracting Officer shall be asked for authority to use or transfer it. (Policy: UC-FA-21-0555)
What reports do I need to submit to awarding agencies to comply with our UC procurement policy requirements?
Under UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf, all required annual and final inventory reports must be submitted to awarding agencies.

If UC allocates $250,000 in grant funds to an external research institution to conduct a specific study on climate change mitigation, does this expenditure qualify as a "service" under UC's procurement policy, or would it be classified differently for compliance purposes?
Yes, services include providing grant, contract, or gift funds for research, as stated in the Conflict of Interest Training-Procurement-2024.pdf policy.

Hey, I'm new here and trying to understand compliance requirements - what federal policies do I need to know about when it comes to protecting human subjects and genetic information in our procurement processes?

The applicable policies are the Federal Policy for the Protection of Human Subjects (Common Rule) and the Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act (GINA), as listed in the appendix-data-security.pdf policy.

Hi! I'm new here and I'm still learning about how procurement works at UC. If a lessor doesn't hold up their end of the deal and doesn't deliver the goods or services they're supposed to, what can we actually do about it? And what would that mean for us financially?

UC may by written notice terminate the Agreement for Lessor’s breach, and may use or secure Goods and/or Services elsewhere, with Lessor liable for any excess costs incurred. This is specified in the TC-Operating Lease-Equip Rental.docx policy.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Who is responsible for deciding which commodities the University will bid out and in what order?

The Associate Vice President and UCOP Chief Procurement Officer is responsible for developing long-range plans that determine which commodities the University will bid out and in what order, as stated in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
As a cardholder, what am I responsible for reviewing before approving an invoice or packing list?

You are responsible for reviewing and approving invoices, packing lists, or other documentation to confirm that the items or services received match what was ordered, that the billing is appropriate, and that the ordered and received items or services are the same as those requested.
I'm being relocated and I'm currently renting my apartment under an unexpired lease. Can the University help me break my lease, and if so, what's the maximum they'll cover?

Yes, the University may reimburse actual and reasonable costs directly associated with settling your unexpired lease if you must break it to relocate. However, the reimbursement is limited to the lesser of six months of lease payments or $25,000, and this includes any penalty paid to terminate the lease. Note that the University will not offer reimbursement if you knew or reasonably should have known that relocation was imminent before you signed the lease agreement.
Can we reject a quotation if we think the price is too high, even if the vendor meets all our technical requirements?

Yes, all quotations may be rejected when an award will not result in a reasonable price and/or terms, regardless of whether the vendor meets technical requirements. The Procurement/Supply Chain Director has the authority to make this determination.

How long will personal data be retained under this agreement?
Data shall be processed for the duration of the term of this Agreement, except as otherwise specifically set forth herein. Policy: Addendum B to Appendix GDPR - SCC_0.docx

messages.content: Can the Laboratory use Strategic Sourcing agreements even if they're not available to the campuses?

Yes, the Laboratory can use Strategic Sourcing agreements for government sources not generally available to the campuses. However, these agreements may only be used when they are cost effective and there is no conflict with federal requirements.
Um, so there's this one-year ban thing... what exactly does it apply to? And like, where in all these policy documents would I even find the rules about it?

The one-year ban applies to University employees, officers, and consultants who make or participate in making governmental decisions, as outlined in Section 87406; Regs. 18746.1 and 18746.2 of the mm-postemployment-coi-rules-10-2023.pdf policy.
Under the terms of my federal award, am I permitted to use University-provided cellular equipment for personal use when not engaged in grant-related activities?
Yes, the guidelines for the purchase and use of cellular phones and other portable electronic resources, BFB-G-46, permit the use of University-provided devices outside of the workplace.
I'm planning to import some controlled substances for my research project on campus. What should I do first?

You must notify and consult with your campus CSPO (Controlled Substance Program Officer) before importing controlled substances to be used on campus or in connection with authorized university activities. Your campus may also have local policies or procedures that require additional steps. The Campus Controlled Substance Program can provide assistance in the form of checklists, guidance documents, and FAQ materials to help guide you through the process.
What is the purpose of requiring contractors and external users to maintain insurance coverage?

The insurance requirement is designed to protect the University from losses, expenses, damages, and liabilities caused by or resulting from the Contractor/External User's negligent or intentional acts that arise out of the performance of the contract.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Are other discretionary funds subject to the same regulations as Administrative Funds?
Yes, they are subject to the same regulations and reporting requirements applicable to Administrative Funds, as stated in UC-FO-00-0190_a-253-27.pdf.
Can I give a UC employee a non-cash gift as recognition for their outstanding work performance?

According to UC Policy Section 274(b), non-cash gifts may be provided as employee achievement awards. However, these gifts are subject to the requirements outlined in 2 CFR Part 200 (Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards) and the guidelines specified in Rev. Proc. 2022-38. You should consult the complete policy details to ensure the gift complies with applicable federal regulations and UC guidelines regarding value limits, documentation, and other requirements for employee achievement awards.
URGENT: I need the exact name of the UC procurement and supply chain management policy - can someone tell me NOW?
The policy name is BFB-BUS-43 Purchases of Goods and Services; Supply Chain Management.
Under the federal grant procurement requirements, which personnel on my grant are eligible to obtain a Procurement Card?
The policy allows approval for requests to issue Procurement Cards to both central purchasing unit employees and non-University employees as outlined in BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Can I receive additional compensation for services as a faculty consultant?
Yes, the policy on additional compensation for services as a faculty consultant is outlined in Academic Personnel Manual Section 664 (July 1, 2014).
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What is considered 'Data' under this agreement?

Under this agreement, 'Data' means all personal data processed by (or on behalf of) the Processor for the Controller under or in connection with the Agreement, including in the provision of the Services. If Appendix DS applies to this Agreement, 'Data' as used herein shall also be considered UC Institutional Information as defined in Appendix DS. (Policy: appendix-gdpr-eea-uk-4-27-21.pdf)
Can I charge late fees on my personal credit card to my University business account if I was delayed in paying a bill while traveling for UC business?
No, late fees associated with charge cards are not allowable expenses, even if they were incurred while on University business.
What accounting methods should we use when establishing depreciation schedules for university vehicles?

According to UC policy PS-12-0029, vehicle depreciation schedules must be established in accordance with accepted accounting methods. The policy does not specify which particular accounting methods to use, but requires that whatever methods are selected must be recognized and accepted accounting methods.

Um, so like... once you pick someone to be the arbitrator person, how much time does the whole fast-track arbitration thing actually take? Like, is it weeks? Months? I'm not really sure how this all works...

The expedited arbitration process shall be conducted within thirty (30) calendar days of arbitrator selection, as stipulated in the Article 5.C. grievance policy (article-5-contracting-out-1-31-20.pdf).
If our department maintains internal files for procurement transactions, do we still need to attach the SSPR form to the requisition in the eProcurement system?

Yes, the SSPR form should be attached to the requisition in the campus eProcurement system once it is signed and approved. Additionally, if your department keeps files internally, the form should also be filed with the records for that transaction.
URGENT: I need an immediate answer - what exactly qualifies as an incentive under our procurement policy? This is critical and time-sensitive!

Incentives include gifts (monetary or free goods/services), cash or credits based on total purchases, and any other value provided by a supplier to the University. This definition is outlined in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
URGENT: Does the conservatory have the legal right to ban me from teaching anywhere else just because they're giving me studio space and collecting tuition? I need an answer ASAP!

Yes, the teacher agreed not to teach elsewhere within the vicinity without the consent of the conservatory as part of the arrangement outlined in the GU-FA-20-0506_UCIndependentContractorGuidelines_Accessible.pdf policy.
Who is responsible for implementing the Procurement/Supply Chain Management Policy at our location?
The Procurement/Supply Chain Director at your location is responsible for the implementation of this Policy.

As a PI managing a federally-funded research project at UC, which policy document should I consult to understand the institutional guidelines for identifying and managing conflicts of interest in my research activities?
Policy Analysis Coordination, Operating Guidance 11-05, Summary Statement of Principles and Policies on Institutional Conflict of Interest in Research (June 1, 2011)
Is it permissible for staff members to utilize university facilities and resources for personal projects outside of their departmental duties?

Faculty are prohibited from using University resources or facilities on a significant scale for personal, commercial, political, or religious purposes without authorization, as stated in the compendium-of-conflict-of-interest-and-related-policies-guidance-formerly-bfb-g-39.pdf (Academic Personnel Manual Sections 015 and 016).
URGENT: Do I qualify for reimbursement on moving expenses I paid to a common carrier?? Need answer ASAP!
Reimbursement for common carrier expenses is allowed if the carrier is included on the University’s preferred vendor list, as stated in UC-FA-18-0381_BFB-G-13_MovingRelocationPolicy.
Um, so like... what's this E1 thing supposed to mean? Is that some kind of code or something? I'm not really sure what the policy is saying about it...
The condition code E1 indicates equipment that is used, reconditioned, and in excellent condition, as per UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
Is there a designated person or department responsible for processing financial adjustments when a payment recording error occurs, such as an incorrect object code or sales tax error?

The Accounting Office, or if delegated the responsibility, Equipment Management shall process financial adjustments for discrepancies due to errors in recording payment, as stated in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
I'm new here and trying to understand the policy better – who would be the person or team responsible for actually developing and updating the security standards that are mentioned in this document?
ITLC is responsible for developing, implementing, revising and consulting on standards in support of this policy. (UC-IT-19-0480_IS-3_Accessible.pdf)

What is the policy regarding procurement of IT services?
The policy mentioned is UC-IT-19-0480_IS-3_Accessible.pdf, which focuses on electronic information security and does not provide specific details about procurement procedures.

How often must departments review the use of property according to the policy?
Departments must review the use of property every two years, as stated in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
Like, um, what rule or whatever do they use at UC to like, handle giving employees stuff that's not money? Like gifts and prizes and things like that?

The policy is governed by UC-FA-23-672_BFB-G-41_EmployeeNon-CashAwardGifts_Accessible.pdf, which references 2 CFR Part 200-Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards.

At what dollar amount does a UC purchase trigger the requirement to obtain competitive bids, and how does this threshold change if a department needs to procure $150,000 in laboratory equipment versus $75,000 in office supplies?

The competitive bidding threshold for UC purchases is $100,000 annually for state-funded purchases, as mandated by California Public Contract Code Section 10507 et seq. [2]. For federal funds, the threshold is lower: federal contract purchases ≥$15,000 and federal grant/cooperative agreement purchases ≥$50,000 require competitive bidding [3]. However, the UC applies the stricter state threshold of $100,000 for all purchases unless exceptions apply (e.g., small business set-asides up to $250,000 with two price quotations) [2][4]. Mixed funding transactions are governed by the stricter threshold (e.g., $100,000 for state funds or federal funds ≥$10,000) [4].

As the PI on a federally funded grant, am I required to obtain approval from the campus Facilities Management Department prior to initiating a Purchase Order for any building alterations that may be charged to my grant account?

Yes, according to the UCOP Procurement Supply Chain Management Main Policy, no Purchase Orders shall be placed for requests involving alterations to buildings without approval by the campus Facilities Management Department.
If I label someone as an independent contractor in a written contract, does that automatically make them an independent contractor for UC purposes?

No. According to the policy, the fact that the parties entered into a contract classifying someone as an independent contractor is irrelevant to the final determination of their actual status. UC will evaluate the actual working relationship, including factors such as whether the company exercised the right to direct and control the person in performance of their services, whether there was a continuous relationship, whether the person was engaged in an independent business enterprise, and whether they could incur a loss. The written contract classification alone does not determine independent contractor status.
How should I record equipment purchases that fall between $500 and $1,000 in our procurement process?

Equipment costing more than $500 and less than $1,000 is recorded in the same manner as industrial plant equipment, as outlined in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What should I do with a leased university vehicle at the end of the contract term?
At the end of the contract term, the property must be returned to the lessor at the place agreed to by the parties, as stated in UC-PS-12-0029_AcquisitionDispositionUniversityVehicles.pdf.
Do you need approval before purchasing automatic data processing equipment for your department?

Yes, the University will not initiate an acquisition of the automatic data processing equipment until written approval has been obtained from the Director, DARMPC. (Policy: UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf)
Should cost savings be the primary factor in prioritizing procurement projects?
According to the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy, commodities providing the maximum savings to the University should be developed as projects early in the Strategic Plan.

When a federal contract is valued at $750,000 and includes subcontracting opportunities totaling $200,000, what specific requirements must the prime contractor meet regarding subcontracting plans, including documentation, reporting thresholds, and compliance certifications?

The University must prepare a Small Business Subcontracting Plan, with collaboration between the Campus Small Business Officer or Supplier Diversity Coordinator and the originating department. This requirement is outlined in BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
If our equipment rental vendor fails to fix an accessibility issue with the rented equipment after we report it, what recourse do we have under this policy?

According to the policy, the Lessor warrants that they will promptly respond to remediate any identified accessibility defects in the Goods and Services to conform to WCAG 2.0 AA standards, and agrees to promptly respond to and use reasonable efforts to resolve and remediate any accessibility complaints. If the vendor fails to do so, they would be in breach of their warranty obligations under the agreement, which would give UC grounds to pursue remedies available under the contract terms.
If I'm a UC employee and I want to pursue external funding for my research, what process do I need to follow?

You are required to submit your proposals for extramural support through the appropriate local contracts and grants office at your UC location. Additionally, any awards received must be made to The Regents of the University of California, rather than to you individually.

What is the specific policy name and policy number that governs the procurement and management of university equipment purchases exceeding $5,000, including guidelines for capitalization thresholds, depreciation schedules, and disposal procedures?
The policy is named BFB-BUS-29: Management and Control of University Equipment, with the policy number UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29.
So like... when you're buying some kind of made thing, there's stuff that costs money but apparently doesn't count toward the actual cost? Which expenses are those exactly?

Departmental labor, travel, payroll expenses, and overhead are not considered part of the cost of acquiring a fabricated asset. (Policy: UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf)

So like, who's actually supposed to be in charge of making sure all our stuff and data doesn't get hacked or messed with? Is that like a specific person or department or something, and what exactly do they do?
The policy does not specify exact roles or responsibilities beyond the sections titled 'Organizing Information Security' and 'Roles and Responsibilities' in UC-IT-19-0480_IS-3_Accessible.pdf.
Can I purchase office supplies directly from a vendor without going through the established procurement process?

No. According to UC Policy BFB-BUS-43, all purchases of goods and services must follow the established procurement and supply chain management procedures. Direct purchases outside of this process are not permitted and would violate university policy.
Can you let me know what details we need to include when filling out the 'Data importer(s)' section in our SCC clauses?

The UC must complete the 'Data importer(s)' section with their details, including the name as 'Regents of the University of California, on behalf of its ______ location' and the address, as specified in the policy Addendum B to Appendix GDPR - SCC_0.docx.

Does the policy include specific guidelines on allocating minimum percentages or dollar thresholds—for example, requiring that 15% of a $500,000 annual procurement budget or a minimum of $50,000 in contracts be directed to certified women-owned, minority-owned, or other diverse supplier categories?
Yes, the policy includes guidelines on supplier diversity initiatives in Part 3: Supplier Diversity and Federal Planning and Reporting.

What reports must be submitted to awarding agencies under the UC procurement policy?
Under UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf, all required annual and final inventory reports must be submitted to awarding agencies.

Can a supplier use an alternative to a third-party review instead of obtaining a third-party certification or review?
Yes, a supplier may use an alternative to a third-party review if approved by the responsible UC Information Security Officer, as stated in the appendix-data-security.pdf policy.
If we need to modify our Commercial General Liability insurance policy, how much notice do we need to give UC?

You must provide UC with not less than fifteen (15) days' advance written notice of any modification, change, or cancellation to your insurance coverage. You must also promptly obtain replacement coverage that complies with the policy requirements.

So like... if a hospital basically gives a doctor who does that pathology stuff everything they need - like the office space, all the machines and equipment, and even the people working there - does that mean the doctor is actually working for the hospital as an employee, or are they like their own boss doing contractor work? I'm trying to figure out what PLR 9149001 says about this situation.

The physician is considered an employee of the hospital under PLR 9149001, as the hospital furnished the necessary space, equipment, facilities, and personnel required for the operation of the pathology department.
If I'm a UC vendor and I hire a subcontractor to help deliver services to UC, do I need to make sure they follow the same data security requirements outlined in this Appendix?

Yes. According to the policy, you must ensure that any sub-supplier you retain to provide or assist in providing goods or services to UC is bound by written contract to follow the same terms and conditions contained in this Appendix on data security.
URGENT: Who needs to submit the purchase order for university vehicles RIGHT NOW?
The State shall receive the University's purchase order, as stated in policy BFB-BUS-8.
Can we charge UC for shipping and handling costs on this equipment rental?

No, UC will not pay shipping, packaging, or handling expenses unless they are specifically listed in the Agreement or Purchase Order. Freight should be FOB destination unless otherwise agreed to in writing.
How should our department handle incentives and discounts that suppliers offer separately from the listed sales price?

Incentives and discounts not reflected in the sales price, allowances, or similar payments received from Suppliers should be remitted to the appropriate Location office as determined by Procurement Services at the Office of the President, for Locations to use in support of Strategic Sourcing. (Policy: BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf)

What is the difference between a Commodity Agreement and Common Goods and Services under the procurement policy?

Commodity Agreements are primary/secondary strategically sourced agreements for goods/services via competitive bid or negotiation, with firm prices or negotiated price bases, while Common Goods and Services are standard commercial items readily available through conventional marketing channels. (Policy: BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main)
Who should I contact to get the property number(s) removed from our system when we cancel equipment?
Equipment Management cancels the property number(s), using the appropriate disposal code. (UC-FA-21-0555)
Like, who's the person or department that like... runs the whole Procurement Card thing? Is it like a specific team that handles all that stuff, or does everyone just kind of do it themselves?
The Procurement Card Program is administered consistent with this section of the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf Bulletin.
We have an equipment rental agreement with a lessor that's expected to exceed $100,000 in annual spend. What verification requirements does the lessor need to meet?

The lessor must provide an annual independent verification performed by a licensed public accounting firm or their independent internal audit department. This verification must demonstrate compliance with UC's Fair Wage/Fair Work requirements and follow UC's required verification standards and procedures. The lessor must submit this verification to UC in an acceptable form no later than ninety days after the end of the 12-month period in which $100,000 in spend is reached. Additionally, if UC conducts an interim audit, the lessor's independent accountant or auditor must make available their work papers related to the Fair Wage/Fair Work verification.

We're adding a new component to an existing piece of equipment that was originally purchased with Government funds. The enhancement is being paid for with departmental operating funds. How should we code this equipment in our inventory reporting to the Office of the President?

The entire piece of equipment should be coded as Government Inventorial Equipment for purposes of reporting to Office of the President (EFA 100), regardless of the fact that the enhancement was funded with departmental operating funds. Once Government title applies to the initial equipment, any component parts and enhancements added to it maintain that Government Inventorial Equipment classification for reporting purposes.
Is the primary goal of purchasing goods and services according to policy to obtain the best value for money?
The primary goal is to obtain the most favorable prices, terms, and conditions, which will result in the lowest overall cost consistent with need, as stated in policy BFB-BUS-43.

Can a UC campus establish procurement policies that are more restrictive than the statewide policies outlined in this Bulletin?
Yes, each University location may establish local policies more restrictive than those set forth in this Bulletin, as stated in UC-FA-21-0555.
Who should I contact if I notice that the incentive rewards from our Procurement Card Issuing Bank don't match what we were promised under the University program?

You should report this discrepancy to the Procurement Unit Manager. They will be responsible for verifying that proper incentive amounts are being received under the University program with the Procurement Card Issuing Bank and taking appropriate action.

If a department shares student personally identifiable information (PII) valued at approximately $50,000+ in records with a third-party SaaS vendor without executing a required Data Processing Agreement (DPA), would this scenario trigger a Breach notification requirement under UC policy, and what are the associated costs for breach notification and potential regulatory fines?
Yes, sharing Institutional Information with an unauthorized party constitutes a Breach under section (a) of the UC Terms and Conditions-04-01-25.pdf policy.
Does the University maintain records for completed products under a Government award?

The University maintains a record of all completed products produced under a Government award, consisting of a summarization of quantities accepted or shipped when shipment immediately follows Government inspection and acceptance of the completed product. (Policy: UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf)
URGENT: Need immediate clarification - does the policy classify component replacements as maintenance work, and if so, what are the specific conditions that apply? This needs to be answered ASAP.

Replacement of components and equipment is considered maintenance if it is required on a routine or recurring basis and does not constitute replacement of greater than 50% of the replacement value of that system. Maintenance does not include erection, construction, alteration, repair, or improvement of University structures, buildings, roads, or other improvements. (Policy: BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main)
hey when can we actually open bid docs in front of everyone? like what's the policy on that?

Bid documents are not opened publicly unless, in the judgment of the Procurement/Supply Chain Director, a public opening will be advantageous to the University. (Policy: BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf)
If we need to contract for services at a facility that's 12 miles away from the nearest UC campus, does that automatically qualify as a remote facility exception under Policy 5402?

Yes. According to the policy, all services at remote facilities—defined as those not within a ten (10)-mile radius of a University campus, medical center, or Laboratory—fall within the exception that allows contracting for services. Since your facility is 12 miles away, it exceeds the 10-mile radius threshold and would qualify as a remote facility under this exception.
Must the shipping activity provide documentation to the University according to the policy?

The shipping activity shall furnish the University with copies of documents necessary for University records to accurately reflect the transaction. (Policy: UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf)
Is an information security plan required from suppliers during procurement?
The supplier must submit an Initial Information Security Plan as part of the procurement process, as outlined in the University of California Appendix Data Security Exhibit 2.

Under what circumstances might UC discontinue a $500,000 annual software licensing contract or a $2 million facilities management service agreement, and what specific financial thresholds or performance metrics would trigger contract termination according to the contracting policy?

The university may discontinue a service to respond to budgetary limitations or reductions, or to adhere to the principles of sound business and fiscal management, such as discontinuing services that have become cost prohibitive due to changes in technology, regulatory, or safety requirements, as outlined in GU-HR-23-0643_ContractingforServices_Accessible.pdf.
What are the key things we need to think about in our department when we're deciding whether it's time to get rid of one of our university vehicles?

Any decision concerning disposition of vehicles should include consideration of whether continued operation of a vehicle(s) would be unsafe. (UC-PS-12-0029_AcquisitionDispositionUniversityVehicles.pdf)

Who should I report excess university equipment to, and what is the process?

You should report any excess property immediately to the Contract and Grant Officer, or their designee, who will then report to the Government Contracting Officer. This is outlined in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
What should I do if I need to report a data security issue that doesn't fit into the standard categories listed in this policy?

You can use the 'Other' section provided in the policy document to describe and report data security issues that don't fit into the standard categories. There are designated fields (U. Other and V. Other) available for documenting such cases.

Which entities and individuals are covered under the BFB-IS-3 policy?

The BFB-IS-3 policy applies to all UC campuses and medical centers, the UC Office of the President, UC Agriculture and Natural Resources, UC-managed national laboratories, and all other UC locations. It also covers all Workforce Members, Suppliers, Service Providers, and other authorized users of Institutional Information and IT Resources. Note: This policy does not generally apply to students who are not Workforce Members.
What criteria should we look at to figure out whether our current vehicles can handle the jobs we need them to do?
The policy asks whether necessary specific functions can be performed by existing fleet vehicle(s) (Question 2) as outlined in UC-PS-12-0029_AcquisitionDispositionUniversityVehicles.pdf.

Can a faculty member be reimbursed for their spouse's business travel expenses related to university activities?
Yes, bona fide business travel or entertainment expenses of a spouse or domestic partner are allowable under BFB BUS-79, Expenditures for Business Meetings, Entertainment, and B.
Can I choose any moving company I want for my relocation, or are there restrictions?

You must use a common carrier from the University's preferred vendor list. The University may pay the cost of transporting your household goods and personal effects directly to the mover, but only if they are on the preferred vendor list. Any such payments must be requisitioned using a purchase order.
What happens if I'm caught making an inappropriate purchase with my procurement card?

Improper use of a procurement card may result in disciplinary action and will result in cancellation of your card. Additionally, each location has established guidelines for appropriate sanctions to address misuse. If the misuse involves fraud, waste, or abuse, it will be immediately referred to campus security and/or Internal Audit for appropriate action.
How do we determine which items should be included in a Strategic Sourcing Initiative?

According to the policy, items should be identified for inclusion if they are purchased by multiple Locations in sufficient quantities where an economic advantage can be gained. The process involves developing specifications and standards through value analysis and consultation with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), and securing usage data from Locations that expect to participate in the initiative.
Equipment bought on a grant expires — who owns it after the grant ends?

Based on the policy excerpts provided, **ownership depends on whether the University acquired title to the equipment**.

According to excerpt [4]:

> "Upon completion or termination of the award, records for property to which the University has acquired title are updated to reflect the change in title (if any), but the fund number and fund source code remain unchanged."

The policy states that records are updated "to reflect the change in title (if any)" but does not explicitly specify who owns the equipment after the grant ends or what that change in title would be.

The excerpts do not contain sufficient detail to definitively answer who owns equipment after grant expiration. The policy indicates:
- Title ownership belongs to "The Regents of the University of California" (excerpt [5])
- Records are maintained during the award with fund number tracking (excerpt [4])
- Upon award completion, title changes "if any" are recorded (excerpt [4])

**However, the specific ownership determination after grant expiration is not addressed in these policy excerpts.** You would need to consult the complete policy document or the referenced Contract and Grant Manual, Part 15-310, to determine post-grant equipment ownership.
Can you explain why the policy says we can't contract out for services?
The University is committed to protecting and valuing the lives of those it serves, educates, and employs as a public trust and one of the largest employers in California.

What is the policy name for procurement and supply chain management at the University of California?
The policy name is BFB-BUS-43 Purchases of Goods and Services; Supply Chain Management.
If I hire an independent contractor and they don't provide me with a valid Taxpayer Identification Number, what am I required to do?

If an independent contractor does not furnish a correct Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), such as a Social Security Number or Employer Identification Number, or does not certify that the TIN is correct, backup withholding rules require that income tax be withheld at a rate of 24% from payments made to that contractor.
As a faculty member, am I expected to spend all my working time on university activities like teaching and research, or can I pursue outside professional activities?

According to the policy, a faculty member is assumed to devote full "working" time to the University. This working time includes classroom teaching, conferences with students, studying and writing, research, committee work, administration, and public service. The policy establishes this as the expectation for faculty employment.
Hi! I just started here and I'm trying to understand the process - what are the main things we need to think about when deciding whether it's time to get rid of one of the university's vehicles?

Any decision concerning disposition of vehicles should include consideration of whether continued operation of a vehicle(s) would be unsafe. (UC-PS-12-0029_AcquisitionDispositionUniversityVehicles.pdf)
Who is responsible for maintaining accurate records of university equipment at my department?

According to the policy document structure, compliance and responsibilities for equipment management are outlined in Section IV. The specific responsible parties and their duties regarding equipment record maintenance would be detailed in that section of the UC policy on Management Control of University Equipment.
Can faculty consultants receive additional compensation for their services?
Yes, the policy on additional compensation for services as a faculty consultant is outlined in Academic Personnel Manual Section 664 (July 1, 2014).
hey do u know who's supposed to approve if someone doesn't follow the normal reviewer chain of command thing in that BUS-43 procurement policy?

The Administrator (or other individual approved by the Controller) shall approve exceptions to the reviewer reporting relationship, as specified in Policy BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main.
yo, what's the total amount of gifts u can get in a year before it becomes a problem?
The aggregate gift limit is $590, as stated in the Sources of Gifts section of the Conflict of Interest Training-Procurement-2024.pdf policy.

Can suppliers use our institutional data for marketing purposes without prior approval?
No, suppliers may not use Institutional Information for marketing purposes unless expressly approved in writing by UC. This is outlined in the appendix-data-security.pdf policy.
How long do I need to keep documentation like invoices and receipts for purchases I make on behalf of UC?

According to BUS-43 policy, you must retain documentation such as requests, approvals, invoices, receipts, packing lists, and other documentation confirming billing and receipt. However, the specific retention timeframe is not detailed in this policy excerpt. You should consult your department's records management guidelines or contact your procurement office for the exact document retention requirements.
Who has the authority to execute Purchase Agreements for goods and services under UC policy?

According to the policy excerpt, the Laboratory Director and the VP of ANR have the authority to execute Purchase Agreements for goods and services, as outlined in Bylaw 31 and the Presidential Delegation of Authority DA 2100.
We're about to order a piece of equipment for $18,000 under a Department of Defense contract. What do we need to do before we can proceed with the acquisition?

Before initiating the acquisition of equipment costing $18,000 or more under a DOD award, you must obtain an approved DD Form 1419/Industrial Plant. This form must be approved before you can move forward with the equipment purchase.
What types of controls must our unit include when implementing the Location ISMP for information security?

According to policy BFB-IS-3 section 5.2.2, units must implement a layered approach that includes administrative controls, technical controls, and physical controls. These should encompass preventative, detective, and corrective controls to address information security risks.

Um, so like... when UC is buying something expensive, over $100,000 I guess, how do they actually figure out what a fair price is? Like, what makes a price "reasonable" anyway? Is there some kind of rule or formula they use?

For transactions above $100,000, a reasonable price is established through competition sufficient to ensure an adequate market test, or set by applicable law or regulation, or supported by an appropriate price or cost analysis, as defined in BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.

The University will provide a copy of the RFP at the time of issuance when a Request for Proposal will be issued, as stated in Article 5, Contracting-Out Policy (article-5-contracting-out-1-31-20.pdf).
As a procurement manager, what am I responsible for tracking regarding our department's purchasing card program?

You are responsible for maintaining an up-to-date listing of all authorized cardholders, their Delegations of Authority, and their respective reviewers. Additionally, you must monitor departmental reconciliation activity and unresolved disputes.

What factors should be evaluated when a UC department requests approval to purchase an additional vehicle at a cost of $35,000-$45,000, and how do procurement guidelines differ when the request involves replacing a fleet vehicle versus acquiring a net new asset?

The policy UC-PS-12-0029_AcquisitionDispositionUniversityVehicles.pdf addresses determining the number of replacement or additional vehicles needed and determining the specification for the new or used vehicles.

Do I need to include the Prime/Sponsor Award number on every requisition or agreement I process?
Yes, according to the Federal Funds Checklist general requirements, the Prime/Sponsor Award number must be included on the requisition or agreement.

If misconduct is substantiated through a formal process, APM 016 contains sanctions that may be applied against you.

Under what circumstances is the University relieved of financial and legal responsibility for Government property valued at $5,000 or more, and what documentation must be provided to release the University from liability in scenarios such as loss, theft, damage exceeding $10,000, or destruction of equipment during transport or storage?

The University is relieved of responsibility for Government property upon receipt of written instructions from the Government Contracting Officer or a duly authorized representative, as stated in the UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf policy.
