Do I need to approve the transfer of University equipment when relocating to another institution?

Yes, as part of Faculty relocations to other institutions, you must coordinate and approve all transfers of University property, including no-cost transfers, and approve all donations of surplus property. (UC-FA-21-0555)
Who should I contact if I have questions about managing equipment that belongs to the Department of Energy and is being used for a UC-managed DOE project?

You should contact Ruth Satorre, Director of Corporate Accounting, at Ruth.Satorre@ucop.edu or (510) 987-0414. She is the designated contact for matters related to materiel in the custody of the Department of Energy that is used by the University in conjunction with DOE projects managed by the University.
What acquisition code should I use when entering equipment into inventory that was purchased through a Regents' Contract?
You should use acquisition code 33 (Regents' Contracts) when entering equipment into inventory that was obtained through a Regents' Contract.
URGENT: We have an error in our bid submission - what do we need to do RIGHT NOW to fix this?!
Exceptions, irregularities, or errors in quotations may be negotiated with or corrected by the bidder involved, as stated in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf policy.
If a vendor's response arrives late due to a courier delay, can we still accept it?

No, late responses may be rejected and returned unless the delay is attributable to the University. A courier delay would not be attributable to the University, so the late response could be rejected.
Can I use an endowment fund to purchase a retirement gift for a departing employee?

Yes, various non-State funds controlled by the University, including endowments and gifts, may be used for employee awards in accordance with this policy, provided you follow any restrictions that may apply to those specific funds.
As a UC processor receiving personal data from an EU controller, what must we warrant regarding the third country where we're transferring this data?

You must warrant that you have no reason to believe that the laws and practices in the third country of destination prevent you from fulfilling your obligations under the Standard Contractual Clauses. Specifically, you need to assess whether the third country's laws—including any requirements to disclose personal data or measures allowing public authority access—would prevent you from meeting your contractual obligations. However, laws and practices that respect fundamental rights and freedoms and are necessary and proportionate in a democratic society to safeguard objectives listed in Article 23(1) of the GDPR are not considered contradictory to these Clauses.
Is there a designated person or entity responsible for approving the selected controls for Critical IT Infrastructure?
The CISO must document and approve these controls. Policy: UC-IT-19-0480_IS-3_Accessible.pdf
What types of official documentation must I retain to support a university financial transaction?

According to UC Policy A-000-7, official documentation is required in support of all university financial transactions. The specific types of documentation that must be maintained are detailed in Section II (Required Documentation) of the Accounting Manual, though the excerpt provided does not list the specific document types on this page.
Can someone outside the Procurement Department get delegated purchasing authority, and if so, who decides this?

Yes, the Procurement/Supply Chain Director may provide additional delegated purchasing authority to individuals outside the Purchasing Department, but this is done under specific conditions. For details about those conditions and to determine if you qualify, you should check with your local Procurement Office.
Um, so like... how do I know if someone is supposed to be an independent contractor or not? Like, what's the difference? Does UC have like specific rules about this or something?

The individual must operate a bona fide business (incorporated, with a taxpayer identification number, business license, letterhead, separate location, etc.) and receive a flat fee for services instead of hourly payment. Policy: GU-FA-20-0506
Who is responsible for registering motor vehicles at our UC location?
The designated University location representative is responsible for registering all motor vehicles.
If my equipment fabrication request is disapproved, what happens next and how should I handle the costs?

According to the policy, the disapproved Fabrication Justification Form will be returned to you as the Principal Investigator. Any project purchases related to the disapproved fabrication should be expensed as non-capital transactions.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Who should I contact to convert a contractor to University employment?
Requests should be submitted to the location's Employee/Labor Relations Manager, as stated in Regents Policy 5402. The University must establish implementation guidelines by February 15, 2020.

metadata.source: Regents Policy 5402_ Policy Generally Prohibiting Contracting for Services _ Board of Regents.pdf

messages.content: If UC doesn't enforce a lease clause one time, does that mean we've waived all our rights to enforce that clause in the future?

No. According to the policy, if UC chooses not to enforce a provision on one occasion, that single instance does not constitute a waiver of UC's right to enforce that same provision later or enforce other provisions of the agreement. Each situation is treated independently.
Who has the authority to ensure that property disposition policies are regularly reviewed and updated?

The Executive Vice President-Chief Financial Officer has the authority to ensure that policies are regularly reviewed and updated, and that they are consistent with Government, State, University and other governance policies.
Can we offer gift incentives to suppliers who want us to purchase their goods or services?

According to the policy, incentives offered by suppliers can include gifts, whether monetary or free goods or services, as well as cash or credits based on total purchases. However, the policy defines incentives as payments offered by suppliers to encourage the University's purchase of their goods and/or services. Any use of such incentives would need to comply with UC procurement guidelines and applicable regulations, which are not detailed in this excerpt.
What happens if our local Risk Management office doesn't keep records of the exceptions we've granted to this insurance policy?

According to the policy, the local Risk Management Office must maintain records of exceptions and make them available for audit by the University Chief Risk Officer. Failure to maintain these records would prevent compliance with this requirement, and could result in findings during the University Chief Risk Officer's periodic audits and reviews. This could lead to the Chief Risk Officer issuing additional guidelines that limit the range of exceptions allowed at the local level.
URGENT: What are the SPECIFIC packaging requirements suppliers MUST comply with for UC procurement - need this answered ASAP!

Suppliers must comply with the Toxics in Packaging Prevention Act and meet all standards and requirements set forth in the Policy. Additionally, all packaging must meet at least one of the criteria listed, such as using bulk packaging or reusable packaging. (UC Terms and Conditions-04-01-25.pdf)

Under the Power of Attorney policy, which individuals are authorized to approve purchase orders for controlled substances exceeding $5,000, and what are the specific dollar thresholds at which additional approval levels are required for purchases ranging from $1,000 to $50,000?

The Controlled Substance Program Officer (CSPO) is authorized to take the actions set forth in section IV(A)(2)(b)(ii-iii) through a Power of Attorney, as specified in UC-RK-25-761_ControlledSubstances_Accessible.pdf.
URGENT: What expenses are explicitly EXCLUDED from fabricated asset acquisition costs per policy—need this answered NOW!

Departmental labor, travel, payroll expenses, and overhead are not considered part of the cost of acquiring a fabricated asset. (Policy: UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf)
How do I determine which Protection Level classification applies to the data I'm responsible for?

According to the policy excerpt, the Protection Level is determined by the anticipated record count. Protection Levels 1 and 2 apply to datasets with less than 70,000 records, while Protection Level 3 applies to more than 70,000 records. Protection Level 4 has two categories: less than 70,000 records and more than 70,000 records. The Protection Level classification you select will then determine the applicable cyber security insurance requirement in the Terms and Conditions.

When a UC department receives $250,000 in non-Federal funding to procure highly specialized laboratory analysis services that only two vendors in the region can provide, what specific justifications and documentation are required to support the selection of one supplier over the other, and are there dollar thresholds that trigger additional competitive bidding requirements?

For Non-Federal funds, professional or personal services requiring highly specialized functions, typically technical in nature, performed by a distinctly qualified supplier, and unusual and compelling urgency where immediate action is needed to avoid significant harm, loss, liability, or policy violations are allowable justifications. These are outlined in the SOURCE SELECTION & PRICE REASONABLENESS JUSTIFICATION FORM (1).docx policy.
If we issue an RFx and the lowest bidder and I can't reach agreement on the negotiated requirements, do we have to award the contract to the next lowest bidder?

No, you are not required to award to the next lowest bidder. According to the policy, if the parties are unable to reach agreement, the University may go to the next lowest bidder if it wishes, but it is not required to do so. The University holds the rights to negotiate with one or all bidders at its discretion or if it is in the best interest of the university.

As the PI on a federally funded award with anticipated annual expenditures of $25,000 over a 5-year period, should I anticipate that this procurement will trigger competitive bidding requirements, or does the aggregate value fall below the Federal $100,000 threshold for such mandatory procedures?

Yes, under Uniform Guidance and FAR, the total contract value exceeding $100,000 (even if annual expenses are under $100,000) must be treated as over the threshold and subject to competitive bidding and SSPR form requirements. Bus-43 does not override Federal regulations in this case.
What information do I need to provide to the Equipment Administrator when requesting to transfer excess property?

You need to provide the fair value of each item of property (as determined in consultation with the Useful Life Schedule), the original funding sources and agencies of all property, and justification for why you want to transfer the material rather than leaving it or selling it.

Um, so like... what are all the things I'm supposed to fill in when I'm making one of those equipment record thingies? Like, how much stuff do I actually need to write down for each piece of equipment?
All manufacturer, model number and serial number information shall be completed for each equipment record. (UC-FA-21-0555)
Should you notify the funding agency before declaring government property excess when it is no longer needed for your award?

Before declaring government property excess, it shall be screened against the needs of other awards. If there is a need for the property, the Government Contracting Officer shall be asked for authority to use or transfer it. (Policy: UC-FA-21-0555)
How long do we need to keep records for equipment that was purchased with federal funding?
Records for equipment acquired with federal funds must be retained for 3 years after final disposition of the equipment, in accordance with OMB Uniform Guidance § 200.333.
If our unit uses a cloud service provider to manage some of our institutional data, who is ultimately responsible for reporting security policy non-compliance to the CISO?

The Unit Head remains ultimately responsible for reporting any information security policy or standard that is not fully met to the CISO, even when a Service Provider manages the institutional information or IT resources on behalf of the unit. Any information security responsibilities not expressly delegated to and accepted by the Service Provider or Supplier remain the responsibility of the Unit Head.
If I'm hired as an independent contractor by UC, will the University cover my business expenses like equipment or travel costs?

According to UC policy, whether the University pays a worker's business or travel expenses is one of the key factors evaluated when determining independent contractor status. The policy does not specify a blanket rule, but rather indicates that the payment of expenses is considered as part of the overall assessment of the working relationship.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Does the IRS ruling affect how we classify our cleaning contractors under the independent contractor guidelines?

The IRS ruling indicates that the company exercised, or retained the right to exercise, the degree of direction and control necessary to establish an employer-employee relationship, as stated in the GU-FA-20-0506_UCIndependentContractorGuidelines_Accessible.pdf policy excerpt.
What do we need to submit to the Government Property Administrator after completing a physical inventory of government equipment?

You must submit two things: (1) a listing that properly identifies all discrepancies found during the physical inventory, and (2) a signed statement confirming that the physical inventory of all or certain classes of government property was completed on a specific date and that property records were found to be in agreement with the physical inventory, except for the discrepancies reported. Both the listing and signed statement must be furnished with minimum delay upon completion of the physical inventory.
When we trade in old equipment as part of a new equipment purchase, how should we record the value of the new equipment for accounting purposes?

The new equipment acquisition should be valued at its full list price, with the trade-in credit not deducted from its value. Equipment Management will then process a separate disposal transaction for the traded-in equipment, either through the purchase order or an Equipment Inventory Modification Request (EIMR) submitted by the custodial department.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Who has the authority to execute Purchase Agreements for goods and services under the UC procurement policy?

The President has delegated authority to Chancellors, Laboratory Director, and the VP of ANR to execute Purchase Agreements for goods and services, as specified in BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf under Bylaw 31 and DA 2100.
hey, so when is it actually ok to bring in temp staff for clinical stuff? like what's the situation where that's allowed?

Temporary staffing may be used in clinical operations when the University's reasonable recruitment efforts to hire employees are unable to satisfy ongoing staffing needs, as outlined in Regents Policy 5402.
I left UC six months ago. Can I now bid on a contract with the department where I used to work?

No, you cannot. The Public Contract Code imposes a flat 12-month ban on former policymaking employees entering into contracts with their former University departments. Since you left only six months ago, you are still within the restricted period and must wait at least another six months before you can bid on contracts with your former department.
If I work in UC's occupational health office and maintain records about employee workplace injuries and accommodations, do those records fall under HIPAA requirements?

No, occupational health records maintained by UC fall under Category H (Health data – other identifiable medical data not covered by HIPAA), not Category I. However, if those records contain Protected Health Information (PHI) subject to the HIPAA Privacy or Security Rule, they would then be classified as Category I and would be subject to HIPAA requirements. The distinction depends on whether your specific occupational health records meet HIPAA's definition of PHI.
Who should I contact if I have questions about the risk transfer and insurance requirements outlined in policy BFB-BUS-63?
You should contact Gary Leonard, Executive Director of General Liability, at Gary.Leonard@ucop.edu or (510) 987-9186. He is listed as the contact for this policy.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What policy section addresses the handling of UC financial assets like cash, investments, and revenue sharing agreements?
The Financial Assets section (J) of the BUS-63 Risk Matrix 9-19-2025.pdf policy covers handling of cash, UC bank accounts, investments, and revenue sharing agreements.
Does the total cost of contracting out include administrative expenses?
Yes, the cost of contracting out will include the total cost of the contract plus costs associated with administering the contract, as stated in GU-HR-23-0643_ContractingforServices_Accessible.pdf.
So like, I gave this company a contract to do work for us, and now they're trying to hire me for a job there... is that like, not allowed or something? What am I supposed to do about that?

Based on the policy excerpts provided, I cannot find specific restrictions addressing your situation—where a vendor you awarded a contract to has offered you a job.

The excerpts address:
- Restrictions on the University contracting with its own employees [Excerpt 2]
- Requirements for contractor employees working at University locations [Excerpt 4]
- An individual employee of a contractor applying for open University positions [Excerpt 3]

However, none of these excerpts directly address the reverse scenario: a University employee accepting employment from a vendor after awarding them a contract.

To answer your question accurately, I would need access to:
- Conflict of interest policies
- Post-employment restrictions or cooling-off periods
- Disclosure requirements for procurement personnel

**I recommend consulting your Procurement/Supply Chain Director or compliance office for guidance on this specific edge case.**
Can I use University equipment for personal projects if I get approval from my department head?

No. According to the policy, employees must obtain pre-approval specifically from the Chancellor or Laboratory Director to use University property for personal purposes. Approval from a department head or other supervisors does not meet the requirement stated in the policy.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
How long does the expedited arbitration process take after selecting an arbitrator?

The expedited arbitration process shall be conducted within thirty (30) calendar days of arbitrator selection, as stipulated in the Article 5.C. grievance policy (article-5-contracting-out-1-31-20.pdf).
Is it possible for a reviewer to approve more than ten cardholders?
Yes, the policy allows reviewers to approve more than ten (10) cardholders per reviewer, as stated in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
Who is responsible for the maintenance and physical security of equipment in my department?

The head of the custodial department and the Principal Investigator have primary responsibility for the care, maintenance, physical inventory and control of all inventorial equipment and other property under their jurisdiction.
When we're evaluating whether to acquire a new vehicle for our department, what are the key criteria we should assess first?

According to UC policy PS-12-0029, you should first determine whether the current fleet size meets user demand and whether necessary specific functions can be performed by existing fleet vehicles. These are the foundational questions that should be answered before proceeding with any vehicle acquisition decision.
Hey, I'm new here and I'm just trying to figure something out – do government-owned vehicles at UC need to have any special registration plates, or is there a specific requirement for that?

Yes, the University shall ensure that all Government-owned vehicles carry Government registration plates and/or identification as a Government vehicle for official use. (Policy: UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf)
What types of vehicles are considered general purpose vehicles under UC policy?

According to UC policy, general purpose vehicles are those used for the transport of people or goods. These include passenger sedans, station wagons, carryalls, pickups, vans, 4-wheel drive vehicles, flat bed trucks, and buses.
We're entering into a 3-year service agreement that will cost $80,000 per year. Do we need to go out for bid on this contract?

Yes, you would need to go out for bid. The $100,000 threshold applies per agreement, not as an annual amount. Since your total 3-year agreement is $240,000, it exceeds the $100,000 threshold and therefore requires formal bidding.
What are the main topics covered in the UC controlled substances policy updates?

According to the policy excerpt, the main topics covered include: (1) defining the Campus Designation form of DEA Registration, (2) providing specific procedures regarding Powers of Attorney, (3) addressing requirements for DEA Registrations other than Campus Designation registrations such as individual schedule I DEA Registrations, and (4) providing guidance on import, export, interstate and intrastate use, transfer and transport of Controlled Substances, as well as Controlled Substances Analogues and DEA-exempt chemical preparations.
Can I submit a receipt that just says 'miscellaneous supplies' as documentation for my procurement expense?

No. According to the policy, the expenditure must be described in sufficient detail on at least one document such as a web/email confirmation, supplier invoice, packing slip, or receipt. Simply labeling items as 'miscellaneous supplies' is not sufficient documentation.
Can UC sell surplus firearms and ammunition through regular property disposition channels?

No. The disposition of firearms and ammunition is subject to federal regulations under CFR Title 27, Part 178 (Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, and Firearms), as well as California Public Contract Code Section 10334. These regulations impose specific legal requirements for handling excess firearms and ammunition that differ from standard property disposal procedures. UC employees must follow these specialized federal and state regulatory requirements rather than treating firearms and ammunition as regular excess property.
Can I give a non-cash award or gift to an employee I supervise as recognition for their excellent work performance?

Based on the policy document provided, you would need to review the specific guidelines in Section III (POLICY TEXT) and Section IV (COMPLIANCE/RESPONSIBILITIES) of UC-FA-23-672_BFB-G-41 to determine the permissible types of non-cash awards and gifts, any restrictions on supervisors giving awards to direct reports, and the proper approval and documentation procedures that must be followed. The policy excerpt indicates these details are contained in the full document, but specific authorization requirements are not shown in this excerpt.
Hi, I'm new here and still learning about all the policies. Could you explain what would be considered a financial conflict of interest according to our procurement policy?

A financial conflict of interest exists when there is a situation involving a personal interest that could improperly influence an official's action, as outlined in the Compendium of Conflict of Interest and Related Policies – Guidance I. FINANCIAL CONFLICTS GENERALLY – APPLICABLE TO ALL.
Must a separate inventory record be created for each quantity purchase?
Yes, a separate inventory sheet should be prepared for each quantity purchase, as stated in the Administrative Fund Inventory Record guidelines under UC-FO-00-0190_a-253-27.

I'm trying to figure out... so there was like a special tax thing on people who work with alcohol? And it got like... permanently taken away at some point? When did that actually happen according to the rules or something?
The Special Occupational Tax on Alcohol Occupations was permanently repealed on July 1, 2008, as stated in UC-PS-12-0031_Tax-FreeAlcoholPermitsRecordsOperations (3).pdf.
Can my spouse purchase excess property directly from the University if I work in the department that reports to the Equipment Administrator?

No. According to UC policy D.1, neither you nor your spouse (as a near relative) may buy excess property directly from the University if you are employed in a department that reports to the Equipment Administrator.
Can I use my UC purchasing account to buy personal items for my home office setup?

No. According to UC policy BFB-BUS-43, Section J on Personal Purchases, UC purchasing accounts and materials management procedures are designated for official UC business only. Personal purchases are not permitted through UC purchasing channels.
URGENT - NEED IMMEDIATE ANSWER: Who exactly has the authority RIGHT NOW to execute Purchase Agreements for goods and services under the Strategic Sourcing Initiative? This is critical!

The Laboratory Director and the VP of ANR have the authority to execute Purchase Agreements for goods and services, as specified in Bylaw 31 and the Presidential Delegation of Authority DA 2100 (BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf).
My spouse works for a vendor we are considering — what do I need to do?

Based on the policy excerpts provided, you must:

1. **Submit a Certification for Employee-Supplier Relationships** to your Location's Procurement/Supply Chain Director or designee. If the transaction involves an intercampus or Laboratory transaction, submit the certification to the Procurement/Supply Chain Director at the Location where the requirement originates.

2. **Obtain approval** before proceeding with the acquisition from this vendor. The Procurement/Supply Chain Director is responsible for notifying your department of approval or denial of your request.

3. **Re-certify prior to any extension or renewal** of the contract terms with this vendor.

The policies establish "limitations and requirements covering acquisition of goods or services when the transaction involves an employee-supplier relationship." Your spouse's employment with the vendor creates such a relationship that requires certification and approval before you can proceed.

**Note:** The excerpts provided do not specify dollar thresholds, specific approval timelines, or the criteria by which approval/denial decisions are made. You should consult the full BUS-43 policy and Employee-Supplier Relationships certification requirements for those details.
Can I share UC's institutional information with my company's accounting department so they can process the billing for this lease agreement?

Yes, you may disclose institutional information to your employees, but only if two conditions are met: first, you disclose only the institutional information that is necessary for you to perform your obligations under the agreement, and second, you inform those employees about the obligations governing access, use, and disclosure of institutional information before sharing it with them. Your company will be liable for any breach of this agreement by those employees.

Under what circumstances can bid documents for purchases exceeding $25,000 be opened in a public meeting, and are there specific dollar thresholds or contract scenarios where sealed bids must remain confidential until award notification?

Bid documents are not opened publicly unless, in the judgment of the Procurement/Supply Chain Director, a public opening will be advantageous to the University. (Policy: BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf)
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Can I use university equipment for personal purposes?

Employees shall not use University property or property in the care and custody of the University for personal purposes without pre-approval by the Chancellor or Laboratory Director. Policy: UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf
Wait, so like... if I want to work on my own stuff, am I allowed to use the university's equipment and spaces? Or is that not something I'm supposed to do?

Faculty are prohibited from using University resources or facilities on a significant scale for personal, commercial, political, or religious purposes without authorization, as stated in the compendium-of-conflict-of-interest-and-related-policies-guidance-formerly-bfb-g-39.pdf (Academic Personnel Manual Sections 015 and 016).
Do we need to have a physically signed document for this UK GDPR Addendum to be legally valid when transferring personal data?

No, according to the policy excerpt, while Annex 1A and Clause 7 of the Approved EU SCCs normally require signatures, the parties may enter into this Addendum in any way that makes it legally binding and allows data subjects to enforce their rights. The key requirement is that it be legally binding, not that it be physically signed. Entering into the Addendum through any valid method will have the same effect as signing the Approved EU SCCs.
What are my responsibilities as a department manager regarding University equipment assigned to my unit?

You are responsible for informing all staff in your location about their obligations for proper use, care, maintenance, and safekeeping of all property under your department's control. Additionally, you must work to ensure maximum use of all property assigned to your unit.
We need clarification on our controlled substance policies—if a substance has an approved new drug application, would UC consider it a Controlled Substance Analogue?

No. Under UC-RK-25-761_ControlledSubstances_Accessible.pdf, substances with an approved new drug application are explicitly excluded from being classified as Controlled Substance Analogues under section 802(32)(C)(ii).
What are the main aspects of information security that I need to focus on when handling Institutional Information?

According to the policy, you need to ensure three key aspects of security: confidentiality, integrity, and availability of Institutional Information and IT Resources. This means protecting the information from unauthorized access (confidentiality), ensuring it remains accurate and unaltered (integrity), and making sure it remains accessible when needed (availability). You should accomplish this through appropriate administrative, technical, and physical controls, and you must also protect against any reasonably anticipated threats or hazards to both Institutional Information and IT Resources.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What are the steps required for the Chancellor to re-delegate the authority to sign tax-free alcohol permit applications?

The Chancellor may re-delegate the authority by preparing a letter that sets forth the authority re-delegated, identifies the staff member by name and title, and specifies the staff member's official campus mailing address. (UC-PS-12-0031_Tax-FreeAlcoholPermitsRecordsOperations)
Can our department create a new vendor account for a logistics company to access our procurement system without getting prior approval from UC?

No. According to UC policy, you cannot create new Supplier accounts to access Institutional Information and IT Resources without express written approval from UC. You must obtain written approval from UC before setting up the vendor account.
Can you clarify what "additional approval" means when we're dealing with entertainment expense requests under UC policy?

Under UC-FA-22-0617_BUS-79, 'additional approval' refers to entertainment expenses requiring an additional level of approval versus those that specifically exceed a limit established in policy and thus require approval as an 'exception' to the standard process.

Under UC procurement policy, what is the primary reason cited for prohibiting a department from contracting with an external vendor for $50,000 worth of administrative services that could potentially be performed by existing UC staff, and how does this justification apply when a campus requests to outsource a $150,000 data management function?
The University is committed to protecting and valuing the lives of those it serves, educates, and employs as a public trust and one of the largest employers in California.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Does health data not covered by HIPAA fall under European Privacy Law (EEA and UK GDPR) according to the policy?

Yes, health data not covered by HIPAA is categorized under H.  Health data – other identifiable medical data not covered by HIPAA, and is subject to European Privacy Law (EEA and UK GDPR) as specified in the policy: appendix-data-security.pdf.
Where can I find examples of IRS rulings that help determine whether someone should be classified as an employee or independent contractor?
Exhibit B of this policy document contains examples of IRS rulings related to employee versus independent contractor determinations.
URGENT: I need to know RIGHT NOW who I should contact for advice on exceptions to indemnification requirements for a subaward agreement - can someone get back to me ASAP?

UC Legal will advise on exceptions to the indemnification requirements mandated in Standing Order 100.4(dd)(9) in subawards, material/data transfer agreements, or land access agreements. Policy: UC-RK-25-762_BFB-BUS-63
If my spouse owns stock in a company that submitted a proposal to our department, do I need to disclose this financial interest?

Yes. According to the policy, you must disclose your near-relative's financial interest in the proposal. Since your spouse is considered a near-relative, their stock ownership in the company making the quotation or proposal must be specified as part of the disclosure requirements.
hey so like who's actually supposed to handle getting rid of all that extra stuff we have lying around?

Each Chancellor or Laboratory Director is responsible for administering the disposition of property under his or her jurisdiction. The Executive Vice President-Chief Financial Officer is responsible for developing policy with respect to management and control of property, including the disposition of excess property. (UC-PS-12-0068)
Can I use my research grant funding to buy parts for my personal laptop that I use for work?

No. Under UC policy, University funds, including those from research grants (extramural sponsor awards), cannot be used to purchase component parts or assemblies for installation in employee-owned equipment. This prohibition applies under all circumstances.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Can I get approval to reimburse expenses that exceed the per-person maximum rate for meals and refreshments?

Requests for exceptions to the per-person maximum rates must include a written justification for unavoidable circumstances or necessary business purposes, as specified in UC-FA-22-0617_BUS-79. The request must document the circumstances, and exceeding the authorized rate alone is not justification for the higher reimbursement.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Who is responsible for approving contracts for services with non-University staff?
The Chancellor or designated Vice Chancellor is responsible for making these decisions, with review by the Office of the President as appropriate, per Policy BFB-BUS-43.
Um, so like... should we focus on buying stuff that saves us the most money? Or is there something else we should be thinking about when we're ordering things?
According to the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy, commodities providing the maximum savings to the University should be developed as projects early in the Strategic Plan.
URGENT: What are the immediate steps we need to take RIGHT NOW when an intercampus loan gets terminated?!

The lending department shall inform Equipment Management when the loan is terminated. Equipment Management shall inform its counterpart at the borrowing University location of the loan termination, in case the borrowing department has not notified it. (UC-FA-21-0555)
hey, do you know which object codes we're allowed to use for those indefinite inventory purchases? like what does the policy actually say about that?

Indefinite, inventorial acquisitions may be coded using (as appropriate) object code 9000 or 9900 (or University location equivalents) as specified in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
If I helped investigate a research misconduct case as a UC employee, can I later advise the researcher who was the subject of that investigation?

No. According to the policy, you may not aid, advise, counsel, consult or assist any other person in a University proceeding involving specific parties in which you participated.
