However, the disposition through a take-away program must be more cost-effective than other forms of disposition, so approval would depend on whether this method is the most cost-effective option for your department.
URGENT: What's the immediate notification timeline we need to hit if we discover a potential UC data breach RIGHT NOW?

Supplier must notify UC both orally and in writing no later than 72 calendar hours after the initial suspicion of a Security Incident and/or Breach, as outlined in ARTICLE 9 of the appendix-data-security.pdf policy.
do contractors who do covered services stuff have to pay their people the same wages and benefits as our union folks?

Yes, contracts including Covered Services must require the contractor to provide wages and benefits of equivalent value to those provided to bargaining unit employees, as stated in article-5-contracting-out-1-31-20.pdf.
Do I need to disclose financial interests in the informed consent form when I'm conducting human subject research?

Yes. According to Operating Guidance 11-04 from the Office of Research and Graduate Studies, you must provide disclosure of both investigator and institutional financial interests in human subject research consent forms.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What steps must be taken if there is a modification, change, or cancellation of insurance coverage under the policy?

The Regents of the University of California must comply with the policy provisions regarding any modification, change, or cancellation of insurance coverage, and indicate that they are an additional insured as described in the contract. Policy name: UC-RK-25-762_BFB-BUS-63_RiskTransferInsuranceRequirements_Accessible (1).pdf
Hi! I'm new here and wanted to check—can I still bid on procurement stuff even though I only have a small investment in the company worth $25,000 or less?

Yes, under the *Exception Regulation: 18702.1(b) Small Shareholder Exception*, individuals with a shareholder investment interest valued at $25,000 or less are exempt from certain conflict of interest provisions. This policy is outlined in *Conflict of Interest Training-Procurement-2024.pdf*.
Hey, I'm new here and trying to understand the procurement stuff – could someone explain what UC's responsibilities are when it comes to handling data in this agreement?
UC is the data controller as defined in the Appendix GDPR (EEA and UK) policy.
As a UC employee overseeing a subcontractor who is using University equipment, what are my obligations regarding how that equipment is handled?

According to Policy BFB-BUS-29, the subcontractor assumes responsibility and obligations for the University property while it is under their control. However, all actions of the subcontractor are subject to the terms of the prime award related to the care, utilization, storage, movement, and disposition of that property. This means you must ensure the subcontractor complies with the prime award terms governing how the equipment is managed.
If we submit an invoice that doesn't reference the PO number, will UC still process payment?

No. According to the policy, invoices must be itemized and must reference the Agreement or PO number. UC will only pay invoices that meet these requirements, so invoices without a PO number reference would not be considered acceptable and payment would not be processed until the invoice is corrected.
As a department manager, what is my responsibility for tracking equipment that was purchased with University funds?

As a department manager, you are responsible for maintaining accurate records and exercising management control over all University equipment in your department, including equipment purchased with University funds. This involves tracking the equipment's location, condition, and use to ensure proper stewardship and accountability of institutional assets.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Is the Business Associate Agreement (BAA) active without an Underlying Agreement between UC and BA?
The BAA is only operative in the event and to the extent it is incorporated into an Underlying Agreement between UC and BA, as stated in Appendix BAA.pdf.
hey so do i need to get someone's sign-off before i hand off borrowed equipment to another dept?

Yes, borrowed equipment cannot be transferred without the specific written approval of the title holder, as stated in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf section c.
If our department's new vendor needs to process personal data for us but isn't currently a party to these Standard Contractual Clauses, what steps do they need to take to become one?

The vendor can accede to these Clauses at any time with the agreement of both parties by completing the Appendix and signing Annex I.A. Once they complete the Appendix and sign Annex I.A, they will become a Party to the Clauses and will have the rights and obligations of either a data exporter or data importer based on their designation in Annex I.A.

As a PI managing federal grant funds, what documentation and records must I maintain to demonstrate compliance with university financial policies and federal funding agency requirements for all expenditures charged to my grant account?
Official documentation is required in support of university financial transactions, as stated in the UC-FO-00-0180_a-000-7 policy.
Is it permissible to donate excess property with a fair value that exceeds the de minimis threshold?
No, it is against University policy to donate excess property whose fair value is greater than de minimis. This is outlined in UC-PS-12-0068_DispositionExcessPropertyTransferProperty.pdf.
Is there a distinction between plant equipment and industrial plant equipment in the policy?

Plant equipment is included in section c) Buildings, structures and improvements thereto, while industrial plant equipment is excluded from section d) Plant equipment. This distinction is outlined in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Where can I find the documentation processes for selecting campus locations?
The documentation processes for selecting campus locations are listed in the "Notes" section at the bottom of page 2 of the Federal Funds Checklist-121525 (2).docx policy.
Do I need to record equipment loans in the database if we're just letting a department try out a piece of equipment before deciding whether to purchase it?

No, loans of equipment for demonstration or approval purposes (such as trial use prior to possible purchase) are not recorded by Equipment Management in the database. However, you must still obtain prior approval from both the Materiel Manager and the Equipment Administrator before allowing such a loan. A property number will only be assigned if the custodial department decides to purchase the equipment and a change order is issued authorizing the acquisition.
If I discover that a piece of equipment assigned to my department is missing, what should I do and how quickly?
You should report the lost equipment immediately to Equipment Management by submitting an Equipment Inventory Modification Request (EIMR), or your University location equivalent form.
What documentation do I need to provide when submitting a financial transaction for processing?

You must provide official documentation in support of your University financial transaction. According to UC policy A-000-7, official documentation is required to support all University financial transactions. The specific types of documentation needed will depend on the nature of your transaction, but all submissions must include appropriate supporting documentation as outlined in the Accounting Manual.
If our supplier leaves behind construction debris and refuses to clean it up, what can UC do about it?

According to section 12.1, UC may remove the rubbish itself and charge the cost directly to the Supplier. The Supplier is responsible for keeping UC premises free from waste accumulations and removing all rubbish, tools, scaffolding, and surplus materials, leaving the premises "broom clean" or equivalent. If there is a dispute between the Supplier and its sub-suppliers about responsibility, UC can still proceed with the cleanup and bill the Supplier for the costs.
Does the GDPR policy specify required methods for destroying data?

Data must be destroyed by 'purging' or 'physical destruction' in accordance with NIST Special Publication 800-88 Guide to Media Sanitization. The Processor will certify in writing to the Controller that such destruction has been completed. This requirement is outlined in appendix-gdpr-eea-uk-4-27-21.pdf.
Like, um, who's supposed to be in charge of all the stuff that the University buys and like, where it comes from and all that? I'm not really sure how all that works...?
The Procurement Office is responsible for managing the University's supply chain, as stated in policy BFB-BUS-43.
What should our department do if we can't enter equipment data directly into the equipment database?
At a minimum, the department shall update the data field on the record listing on the Biennial Physical Inventory.

I left UC last year and now work for a company that's bidding on a contract with UC. The contract involves the same vendor we worked with before, but it has different terms and scope. Can I participate in evaluating this new contract?

Yes, you can likely participate in evaluating this new contract. According to policy, new contracts with the same parties may be considered separate proceedings if they are based on new consideration and new terms in which you, as the former employee, did not participate. Since this contract has different terms and scope from the previous work, it would generally be treated as a new proceeding in which your prior involvement would not necessarily disqualify you.
If we agree to reimburse a supplier for travel expenses they incurred while performing work for UC, what policy should we follow for processing that reimbursement?

According to the policy, any reimbursement of Supplier's expenses that UC agrees to will be reimbursed pursuant to UC's Travel Policy, which can be found at http://www.ucop.edu/central-travel-management/resources/index.html.
Can our UC department withdraw tax-free alcohol for educational purposes if we don't have a regularly enrolled body of students attending our facility?

No. According to the federal regulations (Title 27/Section 22.104), educational organizations authorized to withdraw and use tax-free alcohol must normally maintain a regular faculty and curriculum AND must have a regularly enrolled body of students in attendance at the place where their educational activities are regularly carried on. Both conditions must be met.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What happens to unexpended funds exceeding 25% of my annual allocation?

Unused balances exceeding 25% of a recipient’s annual allocation must be returned to the accounting office at the end of the fiscal year. For recipients using the Checking Account Option, these funds must be returned when the June 30 expenditures report is filed. (UC-FO-00-0190_a-253-27.pdf)
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What training is required for workforce members under BFB-IS-3?

Locations must implement training, awareness campaigns, educational materials, and related efforts to ensure all Workforce Members understand common security risks, their roles in protecting Institutional Information, and how to comply with Location incident reporting requirements. This is outlined in Policy BFB-IS-3 section 5.2.3.

If a contractor employed by a $500,000 annual services vendor is working on-site at UC for a multi-year IT support contract, can that individual apply for an open, permanent staff position in the same department, and if hired, what are the implications for the existing contractor relationship and any associated costs?

Yes, an individual employee working for a contractor may apply for open University positions for which the University is recruiting, as stated in Section 4 of the policy article-5-contracting-out-1-31-20.pdf.
What factors should I consider when evaluating whether a quotation represents a reasonable price for a purchase contract award?

According to the policy, when determining if a quotation results in a reasonable price, you must give due consideration to overall price, delivery, technical merit, contract terms, and other relevant factors. The Procurement/Supply Chain Director makes this determination as part of awarding the purchase contract.
I'm still pretty new here, but I was wondering—who's actually in charge of managing and running the Strategic Sourcing Initiative? Is that spelled out in the policy somewhere?

The Associate Vice President and UCOP Chief Procurement Officer shall be responsible for managing and administering the Strategic Sourcing Initiative, as stated in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
If our department receives an award involving equipment, what steps must we take regarding Equipment Management?

If an award is involved, fully inform Equipment Management as to all provisions of each award document regarding the care, custody, maintenance, records, control, and all transactions involving said property so that Equipment Management may properly carry out its functions regarding inventorial equipment. Policy: UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf

Hey, I'm still pretty new here, but I'm a bit confused about something with our procurement rules. If I have a grant that's mostly federal money—like $99,999—but also has a tiny bit of state funding mixed in, which procurement regulations am I supposed to follow? Does the federal funding take priority, or do I need to follow both sets of rules?

Based on the policy excerpts provided, **Federal requirements apply to the whole transaction**.

According to excerpt [3]:

> "But, if the Federal funds portion is over the $10,000 threshold, you must adhere to Federal requirements for the whole transaction."

Since your Federal funds ($99,999) exceed the $10,000 threshold, you must follow Federal requirements for the entire $100,000 transaction, regardless of the minimal State funds amount ($1).
Does this IT policy apply to me if I'm a student research assistant working on a UC-sponsored project?

No, this policy does not generally apply to students who are not Workforce Members. However, if you are classified as a Workforce Member (such as through an employment or formal appointment status), then the policy would apply to you when you use Institutional Information or IT Resources for UC-sponsored work.

I'm planning a business lunch meeting and need to order catering. The vendor quoted me $52 per person for food, but there's also a $5 per person delivery charge. Does the delivery charge count toward my $54 lunch maximum?

Yes, the delivery charge counts toward your $54 per-person lunch maximum. According to the policy, the maximum per-person expenditure includes the cost of food and beverages, labor, sales tax, delivery charges, and other service fees. In your case, the $52 for food plus the $5 delivery charge totals $57 per person, which exceeds the $54 limit. You would need to reduce costs or find a vendor with lower delivery charges to stay within the maximum allowable amount.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
How often must the data importer provide information to the data exporter regarding data requests?
The data importer must provide information to the data exporter at regular intervals for the duration of the contract, as specified in Addendum B to Appendix GDPR - SCC_0.docx.

metadata.source: Addendum B to Appendix GDPR - SCC_0.docx

messages.content: If our department receives a donation of scientific equipment, when should we expect Equipment Management to add it to our inventory?

Equipment Management will not inventory the donated equipment until the University Location Development Office has processed and completed a Gift/Private Grant Acceptance Report (Form UDEV100 or your University location equivalent). Once that form is processed, the gift equipment will be recorded as Code 34 (Gift) and added to the inventory.
As a UC procurement officer, do I need to consider supplier diversity when selecting vendors for our department's equipment purchases?

Yes, supplier diversity is addressed in Part 3 of the UC Procurement and Supply Chain Management policy. The policy includes requirements for supplier diversity considerations as part of the procurement process.
If a data subject requests access to their personal data, what should I do as a processor?

According to the policy excerpt, if you receive a requirement to disclose data subject information (such as access requests), you must promptly inform the Controller in writing. You should continue to protect the data in accordance with the terms of the GDPR Appendix while the Controller handles the data subject's rights request.

What are the specific requirements and approval thresholds for procurements under $50,000 that utilize sole source justifications, and what documentation must be submitted when a UC department requests a non-competitive award for a $75,000 software license renewal from an existing vendor?

Procurements not involving full and open competition must comply with BUS-43 and state laws. The SS&PR form can be found on the Procurement Services’ Forms & Policies portal: https://procurement.ucop.edu/resources/p-policies/staff
What documentation do I need to provide if alcohol purchased under our tax-free permit goes missing during delivery?
If the alcohol was lost in transit, you must provide the name of the carrier and obtain the carrier's statement regarding the loss in transit.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Does the Small Business First Program apply to construction projects?

No. All contracting associated with construction is governed by the UC Facilities Manual and the associated policies and templates therein. The Small Business First Program applies to all other University, State, and Federal requirements governing the purchase of goods and services. (Policy: BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main)
I work on a federally-funded research grant. What documentation do I need to submit along with my timesheet?

You need to submit a Personnel Activity Report (PAR) that is certified in accordance with your campus instructions. This is required because your time or effort is charged in whole or in part to U.S. government funds, which includes grants from and contracts with the Federal government and subcontracts from other entities that include Federal reporting requirements.

When a UC department leases equipment valued at $50,000 or more, who bears the responsibility for paying transportation and handling costs—including freight, insurance, and delivery fees—when the equipment is shipped to the UC campus at the start of the lease and returned to the vendor at lease termination?
The Lessor will be responsible for all transportation and handling costs related to the shipment to and from UC of the leased Goods. (Policy: TC-Operating Lease-Equip Rental.docx)
Is a written agreement required when loaning equipment?
Loss of or damage to the loaned equipment will not be covered under the University’s insurance programs. Policy: UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf
If we contract out for services that would require moving an employee to a different location more than 10 miles away, does that count as displacement under this policy?

Based on the policy excerpt, a change of work location greater than ten miles would trigger the displacement definition if it results in demotion, layoff, or involuntary reduction in time due to entering into a contract for services. The relocation itself is noted as a threshold factor, but displacement occurs when that relocation leads to one of those three specific employment consequences.
Can we transfer University-owned property that was purchased with grant funding to another institution at no cost?

No-cost transfers of University-owned property acquired under a government, state, or agency award are only permitted by exception and require approval from the officer delegated to control property. Additionally, the University reserves the right to disallow no-cost transfer requests and instead require the recipient institution to purchase the property at fair value. However, no-cost transfers may be permitted where they are not prohibited under the specific terms of the award or in cases where an entire open award is transferred to the recipient institution.
If I'm an MSP appointee and I leave my position after 10 months to take a job at a different UC campus within 6 months, do I have to repay my moving expenses?

No, you would not have to repay your moving expenses. The repayment provision only applies if you voluntarily separate and do not accept a position within the UC system within 12 months from your initial appointment date. Since you accepted another position within the UC system within that 12-month window, you are exempt from the repayment requirement.
I recently left UC as an attorney and was working on a litigation matter before my departure. Can I contract with the University to continue representing them on that same case?

Yes, this is permitted. The 12-month ban does not apply to a contract for the continuation of an attorney's services on behalf of the University on a matter you were involved with prior to leaving the university. You may contract to continue your work on that matter.
What fuel economy standards must be met when purchasing University vehicles?

According to the policy, the purchase of University vehicles must be consistent with the University of California Sustainable Practices Policy. The excerpt indicates that the University is committed to energy conservation and environmental protection, and vehicle purchases should reflect these commitments. For specific fuel economy standards and requirements, refer to the UC Sustainable Practices Policy document.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Can a UC campus purchase a special purpose vehicle through a local transaction without state-wide procurement rules?

Yes, special purpose vehicles, alternative fuel vehicles, or vehicles purchased to meet special situations may be purchased as a local campus transaction, as long as such transaction is coordinated, in advance, with the Vehicle Commodity Manager. (UC-PS-12-0029_AcquisitionDispositionUniversityVehicles.pdf)
Who should I contact to make sure our lab purchases are following the Strategic Sourcing Initiative guidelines?

The Laboratory Director is responsible for purchasing and providing the goods and services required in a manner consistent with this Bulletin and with the Strategic Sourcing Initiative requirements. (Policy: BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf)
If our department wants to contract out work that's currently being done by our staff members, what factors will be considered in making that decision?

According to the policy, the decision to contract for services currently being performed by University staff will take into account several factors: the type and level of service required including any special skills and expertise needed, the impact on the local business community, and the impact on the core University functions of teaching, research, service, and patient care. Additionally, the requirements of staff personnel policies and collective bargaining agreements will be considered.
Will personal data be retained for a specified duration under this agreement?
Data shall be processed for the duration of the term of this Agreement, except as otherwise specifically set forth herein. Policy: Addendum B to Appendix GDPR - SCC_0.docx
If we have equipment that was inventorial before July 1, 2004 but is now below the $5,000 threshold, do we still need to physically inventory it?

No, you do not need to physically inventory equipment that falls below the $5,000 threshold. However, these items remain on active inventory until fully depreciated, even though they no longer have to be tracked or physically inventoried.

When a UC department loans university-owned equipment valued at $5,000 or more to an external organization or another UC campus for a period exceeding 12 months, what documentation, approval processes, and insurance requirements must be completed before the loan agreement can be executed?

The lending and receiving departments must prepare, sign, and send to Equipment Management an Equipment Inventory Modification Request (EIMR) (or equivalent form) for any loan exceeding one year, providing the property number and new location of the equipment. (Policy: UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf)
If I need to send personal data to a vendor located in a country outside the UK or EEA, what approval do I need to get first?

You must obtain prior written approval from the Controller before transferring any personal data to any country outside the UK or EEA. Additionally, any such transfer must comply with applicable data protection law and other relevant data protection laws.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Do we need to submit a form before gifted equipment can be added to the inventory?

Gifts shall not be assigned a property number and acquired to inventory until the University location Development Office has processed a "Gift/Private Grant Acceptance Report" (Form UDEV100 or University location equivalent). This requirement is outlined in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
Do I need to complete the SSPR Form if I'm purchasing from a catalog vendor and the order is $12,000 using Federal funds?

Yes, the SSPR Form is still required for catalog transactions that exceed the $10,000 Federal fund threshold. Your eProcurement system can route orders based on account string, vendor, or dollar amount to help manage this requirement.
Which object codes are we allowed to use when we're making indefinite inventorial acquisitions under the policy?

Indefinite, inventorial acquisitions may be coded using (as appropriate) object code 9000 or 9900 (or University location equivalents) as specified in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.

If we're hiring an engineer to design a new campus building renovation project that will cost $150,000 in labor and materials, do we need to go through a competitive bidding process, or can we select based on the engineer's qualifications?

You can prioritize the engineer's experience, qualifications, and skills over comparative cost. According to the policy, professional services such as engineering services are evaluated based on the supplier's qualifications and experience rather than on cost comparison alone. This approach is appropriate because professional expertise is considered more important than cost for these types of services.
URGENT: What's the competitive bidding threshold for UC purchases?? Need this answer ASAP!

The competitive bidding threshold for UC purchases is $100,000 annually for state-funded purchases, as mandated by California Public Contract Code Section 10507 et seq. [2]. For federal funds, the threshold is lower: federal contract purchases ≥$15,000 and federal grant/cooperative agreement purchases ≥$50,000 require competitive bidding [3]. However, the UC applies the stricter state threshold of $100,000 for all purchases unless exceptions apply (e.g., small business set-asides up to $250,000 with two price quotations) [2][4]. Mixed funding transactions are governed by the stricter threshold (e.g., $100,000 for state funds or federal funds ≥$10,000) [4].
Who is responsible for verifying the equipment's serial numbers and current location during the physical inventory process?

According to the policy, the Principal Investigator and the Custodial department shall perform the physical inventory together, verifying the existence, current location, utilization, and equipment identification information such as model and serial numbers.
When equipment is donated to the University as a gift, what happens after we receive it?

A property number is assigned to the gifted equipment and a record is created in the appropriate electronic database. This record must include all data elements required by the Office of the President.
URGENT: Does a supplier have the option to submit an alternative to a third-party review instead of getting a third-party certification or review? We need this answer immediately!
Yes, a supplier may use an alternative to a third-party review if approved by the responsible UC Information Security Officer, as stated in the appendix-data-security.pdf policy.
As a UC researcher who develops a patentable invention during my work, who owns the rights to that invention?

According to UC policy, the University of California owns inventions and patents developed by faculty, academic appointees, research staff, and other employees during their work at UC. The specific ownership and licensing arrangements are governed by the Inventions, Patents and Licensing section of the Conflict of Interest and Related Policies, with different provisions potentially applying based on the employee's classification (such as faculty, research staff, or management group members).
If we upgrade existing equipment and the upgrade costs $3,500, should we capitalize it or expense it?
Equipment upgrades valued at less than $5,000 should be expensed as non-capital transactions. Since your upgrade costs $3,500, it should be expensed rather than capitalized.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What are the criteria for determining if an individual is considered an independent contractor under UC policy?

The individual must operate a bona fide business (incorporated, with a taxpayer identification number, business license, letterhead, separate location, etc.) and receive a flat fee for services instead of hourly payment. Policy: GU-FA-20-0506

Under this policy, which UC programs are eligible to receive non-cash award gifts valued at $500 or more, and are there different eligibility thresholds for programs receiving gifts under $500 versus those exceeding $5,000?

The following programs are eligible: SRDP or related campus award programs, Clinical Enterprise Recognition Plan (CEMPR), and Professional development program awards. Policy: UC-FA-23-672_BFB-G-41_EmployeeNon-CashAwardGifts_Accessible.pdf
Can I use a University vehicle for personal errands during my lunch break?

The policy excerpt provided does not contain specific guidelines regarding personal use of University vehicles. To obtain an accurate answer about personal use policies, you should consult the complete UC Policy BFB-BUS-8 or contact your department's fleet management office, as this information is not included in the acquisition and disposition section provided.
Can you clarify who on our team should be inspecting the goods and services when they arrive and handling any discrepancies we find?

The end user department is responsible for inspection of goods and services that should be conducted immediately upon receipt or performance (when practical) and reconciling discrepancies promptly. Policy: BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf
Can we loan equipment to another UC campus or to an external organization, and what documentation do we need?

Yes, equipment may be loaned between departments, campuses, or to external organizations after the required approvals have been obtained. A property record must be maintained for the loaned equipment until the loan is terminated or title to the equipment is transferred to the University. You should use the appropriate acquisition code when documenting the loan.
I'm new here and was wondering—who handles ordering controlled substances at the university? Is there a specific person or department I should contact for that?

The Materiel Manager is responsible for the procurement of Controlled Substances, DEA Listed Chemicals, and California Precursor Chemicals for Authorized University Activities, in compliance with DEA registrations, University or Laboratory policies, and the requirements of the location’s Campus Controlled Substance Program. (UC-RK-25-761_ControlledSubstances_Accessible.pdf)
Um, so like... who is the person or people that have to say "yes, okay" to the controls that somebody picked for the really important IT stuff? Like, who gets to approve which controls are used?
The CISO must document and approve these controls. Policy: UC-IT-19-0480_IS-3_Accessible.pdf
Where can I find a comprehensive glossary of terms related to UC's cyber risk management and incident response policies?
A comprehensive glossary of terms can be found at https://security.ucop.edu/policies/it-
URGENT: How many cardholders can a reviewer actually approve - is there a hard limit at ten or can they go over that? Need this answered ASAP!
Yes, the policy allows reviewers to approve more than ten (10) cardholders per reviewer, as stated in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
Can our department purchase a used vehicle directly from a private dealer, or does it need to go through a specific process?

According to the policy, the purchase of used vehicles shall be a local transaction as outlined in Section V (PROCEDURES) of the document. You would need to refer to Section V of the full policy document for the specific procedural requirements that govern how your department must conduct this local transaction.

What UC policy governs whether a senior manager earning $250,000+ annually can spend up to 20% of their time on outside consulting work, speaking engagements, or board positions, and what are the specific dollar thresholds or approval requirements that apply when these outside activities generate $50,000 or more in annual compensation?
Regents Policy 7707: Senior Management Group Outside Professional Activities (January 17, 2019).
My department head approved an exception to cover my moving expenses, but I'm unsure what documentation I need to submit for reimbursement. What should I provide?

According to the policy, claims for reimbursement of actual expenses must be supported by original receipts or electronic receipts. Make sure to gather all receipts related to your moving costs and submit them along with your reimbursement request to your campus accounts payable office.
If I'm transferring equipment to another UC campus as part of a faculty move, do I need to go through Equipment Management at both locations?

Yes. According to UC Policy BFB-BUS-29, all intercampus transfers of equipment must be coordinated through Equipment Management at each University location. The receiving location typically pays for the transfer via an intercampus journal of funds. The equipment will retain the same property number and will appear on the receiving campus's inventory records.
As a UC employee, what are the main areas covered by Regents Policy 1111 that I need to be aware of?

Regents Policy 1111 sets forth general standards covering: fair dealing; individual responsibility and accountability; respect for others; compliance with applicable laws and regulations; compliance with applicable university policies, procedures, and other forms of guidance; conflicts of interest or commitment; ethical conduct of research; records confidentiality and privacy; access controls; internal controls; use of university resources; financial reporting; and reporting violations with protection from retaliation.

Under our federal award, can the University accept responsibility for the actions and conduct of third parties, including contractors and external collaborators, when executing subawards or agreements related to this project?

No. A contract between Contractors/External Users and the University may not include an agreement by which the University assumes liability for conduct of persons other than University officers, agents, employees, students, invitees, and guests. See Regents’ governing documents (currently Regents’ Standing Order 100.4(dd)(9)).
When evaluating suppliers for our department's office supply contract, how should we interpret 'to the maximum possible extent' when it comes to sustainable products?

According to the policy excerpt, suppliers must conduct business using environmentally, socially, and economically sustainable products and services to the maximum possible extent that is consistent with the Agreement and with UC Sustainable Practices Policy. This means you should require sustainable products to the greatest degree feasible while still maintaining compliance with your specific contract terms and the referenced UC Sustainable Practices Policy. The 'maximum possible extent' is bounded by what remains practical and consistent with your particular Agreement.
If we experience a security incident affecting UC's institutional information, what documentation are we required to provide to UC?

Upon UC's request, you must prepare a report detailing corrective and preventive actions taken in response to the breach or security incident. Additionally, knowledgeable Supplier employees and agents must participate in after-action analysis, including root cause analysis and preventive action planning.
What should I do with the results of a physical inventory once I've completed it?
All physical inventories must be completed and returned to Equipment Management within the mandated period.
Can we use University funds to reimburse a student for a taxable meal?
No, a taxable meal furnished to a student is not reimbursable unless the meal is provided as part of a scholarship or fellowship award, per UC-FA-22-0617.
I need to locate the detailed accounting and reporting guidelines for our department's leases and installment purchase contracts—where would I find this information?

The detailed rules and procedures for accounting and reporting for leases and installment purchase contracts are specified in the Accounting Manual Chapter L-217-11/Accounting and Reporting for Leases and Installment Purchase Contracts, herein incorporated by reference from UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
If I keep my personal laptop in my office at UC for my own use after work, do I need to report it to Equipment Management?

No, you do not need to report personally-owned property kept on campus for purely personal use to Equipment Management. However, be aware that the University is not responsible for loss of or damage to such personal property.
Can you clarify what we should consider a financial conflict of interest according to our procurement policy?

A financial conflict of interest exists when there is a situation involving a personal interest that could improperly influence an official's action, as outlined in the Compendium of Conflict of Interest and Related Policies – Guidance I. FINANCIAL CONFLICTS GENERALLY – APPLICABLE TO ALL.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Can I hire a near relative as a staff member at UC?

The Personnel Policy for Staff Members, Section F. Employment of Near Relatives (January 1, 2018) outlines guidelines for employing near relatives, but the excerpt does not specify whether this is permitted or prohibited.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What happens to the fund number and fund source code for equipment acquired under an award when the award is completed or terminated?
The fund number and fund source code remain unchanged, even after the award is completed or terminated, as per UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf.
When was this Risk Transfer and Insurance Requirements policy last revised before the April 1, 2012 reformatting?
The policy was revised on 11/8/2010, which replaced the previous version from 10/10/2007.
I'm new here and was wondering—who actually manages the procurement card program at UC?
The University's procurement card program is managed by each campus’ purchasing unit, in consultation with the campus Controller. (Policy: BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf)
Hi, I'm new here and had a question - if UC gets rid of equipment that's broken or no longer usable, and the Government needs to be paid back for it, what's the process for handling that?

The University shall be relieved of liability upon reimbursement to the Government, as stated in UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf. Additionally, shipping documents or other instruments evidencing disposal shall be appropriately cross-referenced on the determination document.
Are encumbrance transactions recorded using specific forms according to the policy?

The following forms are used to record encumbrance transactions and serve as the official documentation for those transactions: 1) Purchase order copy or a copy of the contract on the given transaction. (UC-FO-00-0180_a-000-7.pdf)
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Does using UC IT resources for research activities impact my responsibility to preserve academic freedom?

The policy BFB-IS-3 states that UC is committed to preserving academic freedom and research collaboration through the responsible use of Institutional Information and IT Resources. All Workforce Members share responsibilities to protect these resources.
When we switch to a new distilled spirits vendor, what should we do with the photocopies of our old permit that the previous vendor has?

According to UC Policy BFB-BUS-2, the University is responsible for obtaining and destroying all photocopies of its permit from the distilled spirits vendor when another vendor is awarded the University contract. You should request that the old vendor return all photocopies so they can be properly destroyed.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Can we use databases other than the SBA Small Business Dynamic Search Database when looking for suppliers?

Yes, alternate databases from third-party suppliers that some locations have access to may be utilized as an alternative to the SBA Small Business Dynamic Search Database. This is outlined in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What does the new cardholder training include according to the policy?
The new cardholder training includes a review of local policies and procedures regarding procurement card usage, as stated in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main Policy.pdf.
hey so what's the deal when a leased uni vehicle's contract is up? like do we just give it back or what?
At the end of the contract term, the property must be returned to the lessor at the place agreed to by the parties, as stated in UC-PS-12-0029_AcquisitionDispositionUniversityVehicles.pdf.
Can I use the same password across my UC email account and my departmental research database?

No. According to UC policy, you must prevent the use of passphrases or passwords that are common across multiple unrelated UC sites or units. You should use unique passwords for your UC email account and your departmental research database to comply with this requirement.
If our campus needs to implement a new security standard quickly due to an urgent security threat, do we have to complete all the consultation steps before issuing it?
No. According to the policy, in exigent circumstances, the ITLC can issue or amend a standard on an interim basis and complete the consultation process afterward, rather than before issuance.
URGENT: Can I immediately take a job at a company I was directly involved in procuring for while at UC? Need to know NOW if this is allowed!

Under the Permanent Ban, you cannot help the other side if you participated in a proceeding (negotiations, planning, decision-making) as stated in the UC Post-Employment & Revolving Door Guidance policy.
Who is responsible for administering small business and supplier diversity policies at our campus?

The Escalation Authority, or the comparable position, is the primary campus/medical center leader with delegated responsibility for the administration of policies related to small business and supplier diversity.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What is the jurisdiction for resolving disputes under this policy?

Any dispute arising from this Addendum is resolved by the courts of England and Wales, unless the laws and/or courts of Scotland or Northern Ireland have been expressly selected by the Parties. (Policy: Addendum C (UK GDPR) template to SCC_0.docx)

messages.content: Where should I look to find the official definition and requirements for a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) that we're considering for a procurement?

According to the policy, the official source for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) definitions and requirements is the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA). The policy identifies the SBA as the authoritative source for this business classification.

As a PI managing Non-Federal funds on my grant, what documented justifications can I rely upon to support my selection of a supplier when the project requires highly specialized services that may have limited vendor availability?

For Non-Federal funds, professional or personal services requiring highly specialized functions, typically technical in nature, performed by a distinctly qualified supplier, and unusual and compelling urgency where immediate action is needed to avoid significant harm, loss, liability, or policy violations are allowable justifications. These are outlined in the SOURCE SELECTION & PRICE REASONABLENESS JUSTIFICATION FORM (1).docx policy.

If the Government provides us with manufacturing drawings and maintenance instructions for equipment we're building under a grant, how should we handle the storage and organization of these materials?

According to the policy, manufacturing or assembly drawings, installation instructions, operation, repair, or maintenance instructions furnished by the Government should be listed and filed in accordance with good industrial practices. This means you need to maintain organized records of all such Government-provided data and information.
When we sell or trade in a university vehicle, where should the proceeds from that sale be directed according to UC policy?

According to UC-PS-12-0029, the application of proceeds from the sale, trade-in, or transfer of university property, including vehicles, is governed by Business and Finance Bulletin A-51. You should consult that bulletin for specific guidance on how to handle and allocate the financial proceeds from vehicle dispositions.
Should accessories attached to plant equipment be recorded separately?
Accessory and auxiliary equipment is recorded on the record of the item of plant equipment. (UC-FA-21-0555)
Where can I find the contact information for my campus's Conflict of Interest Coordinator if I need to report a potential conflict of interest?

According to the UC Compendium of Conflict of Interest and Related Policies, there is a List of Campus Conflict of Interest Coordinators available in the Appendix that provides contact information for coordinators at each UC campus.
Can I request a university vehicle for permanent assignment to my department, or are vehicles only available for temporary use?

Based on the policy BFB-BUS-8 on Acquisition and Disposition of University Vehicles, the excerpt provided does not contain specific details about permanent versus temporary vehicle assignments. To determine whether your department can request permanent vehicle assignment, you would need to review the full policy document or contact your campus Fleet Management office for guidance on acquisition and assignment procedures.
As a PI administering federal funds, where can I access guidance on conflict-of-interest policies that I need to comply with when conducting procurements under this grant?

The Compendium of Conflict-of-Interest Policies, Acceptance of Personal Gifts, and University Conflict-of-Interest Code are available in the Conflict of Interest Training-Procurement-2024.pdf policy document.
Who is responsible for providing privacy notices and responding to data subject requests for information about how their personal data is being processed?

According to Section E.1 of the Agreement, the Controller is responsible for providing data subjects with required information under Applicable Data Protection Law at the time of data collection, as well as responding to any information requests from data subjects about the processing of their personal data. However, this responsibility does not apply if Section D.9 of the Agreement applies.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
Does shipping any portion of the goods automatically accept the Terms and Conditions of Purchase?

Yes, Supplier accepts all of the Agreement’s terms and conditions either in writing, by shipping any portion of the Goods, or performing any portion of the Services. (UC Terms and Conditions-04-01-25.pdf)
My sister just applied for a position in my department. Can I be involved in reviewing her application or participating in the hiring decision?

No. According to the policy, you may not participate in the process of reviewing or decision-making on any matter concerning the appointment of a near relative. You must recuse yourself from all aspects of your sister's hiring process, including reviewing her application and participating in any hiring decisions.
Do we need to collect a Certificate of Insurance from all contractors before they start work, or only from some?

It depends on the contract type. For High Risk contracts, you must obtain a Certificate of Insurance (or a signed self-insurance statement from an authorized officer) before the contractor commences work. For all other contracts, you only need to request and collect the Certificate of Insurance upon the University's request, rather than requiring it upfront.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What steps must be taken when an intercampus loan is terminated?

The lending department shall inform Equipment Management when the loan is terminated. Equipment Management shall inform its counterpart at the borrowing University location of the loan termination, in case the borrowing department has not notified it. (UC-FA-21-0555)
When we have equipment purchased with federal funding that's no longer needed, what should we do with it?

According to UC policy, the University should first request disposition via transfer of title to the University, unless the award terms explicitly prohibit this. If that's not possible, the University should then request that the Government either remove the items from final inventory or enter into a storage agreement to cover them.
What specific maintenance activities should I be performing on equipment assigned to my department to comply with the care requirements?

According to the policy, you should conduct a preventive maintenance program that includes lubrication, cleaning, calibration, and inspection on a regular schedule. This helps maintain the equipment in the condition it was received in or better, allowing the expected useful life to be met or exceeded. Normal wear is accepted, but you must provide the care necessary to preserve the equipment's functionality and lifespan.
Do I need to maintain detailed records for office supplies and lab consumables that are government-owned?

No, expendable or consumable items are not subject to specific record-keeping requirements. However, you must maintain information that supports utilization and allows for annual reporting of the balance of government-owned material by award.
Um, so there's like this permanent ban thing... what exactly are we not allowed to do under that? Like, which activities get you in trouble with it?

The permanent ban prohibits former employees from providing 'backroom' assistance to their new employer, including aiding, advising, counseling, consulting, or assisting any person other than the State of California with the intent to influence a proceeding. It also bans acting as an agent or attorney for others, making formal/informal appearances, or communicating to influence the outcome of a proceeding in which the individual participated while employed by the University. This policy is outlined in mm-postemployment-coi-rules-10-2023.pdf.

As a Principal Investigator managing federal grant funds, what is the rationale for requiring our Contractor/External User to maintain insurance coverage, and how does this requirement support our institution's compliance obligations?

The insurance protects the University from loss, injury or damage caused by the negligent or intentional acts of the Contractor/External User. The requirement that the Contractor/External User have adequate insurance coverage naming the Regents as an additional insured protects the University from loss or damage due to the negligence of the Contractor/External User. Policy: UC-RK-25-762_BFB-BUS-63_RiskTransferInsuranceRequirements_Accessible (1).pdf
What information do I need to provide to Equipment Management when registering a motor vehicle at my UC location?

You need to supply Equipment Management with the following information: a description of the vehicle, the license number, a University vehicle number, and the California Department of Motor Vehicles/Vehicle Identification Number (VIN), which is 17 digits. Motor vehicles are recorded in the same manner as any other inventorial equipment.
As a PI on a federally funded grant, can I claim a loss if hospital property used in the conduct of this research is damaged while in my custody as an independent contractor?

No, independent contractors are not liable for losses related to the hospital's property, as they are contractually guaranteed compensation and bear no risk of loss beyond that typically assumed by employees, per the GU-FA-20-0506_UCIndependentContractorGuidelines_Accessible.pdf policy.
Do I need to get approval from the Research Advisory Panel of California (RAPC) before starting my research project that involves Schedule I controlled substances?

If you are a Principal Investigator planning to conduct research projects in California using Schedule I and/or II Controlled Substances, you may be required to obtain RAPC's review and approval consistent with California law. To determine whether you need RAPC review and approval for your specific project, you should consult the RAPC website for guidance on the requirements and process.
How do I determine if someone I'm working with should be classified as an employee versus an independent contractor?

The University uses IRS Classification Factors to make this determination. There are two main areas to consider: Behavioral Control, which examines whether the University has the right to direct and control the details and means of how the worker performs services (including instructions about when, where, and how to do the job), and Financial Control, which examines the University's right to direct and control the economic aspects of the worker's activities. If the University has the right to control both the behavioral and financial aspects, the worker is likely an employee rather than an independent contractor.
hey quick q - do we expense all repair and replacement parts no matter how much they cost?

Yes, Repair and replacement components, regardless of cost, shall be expensed as non-capital transactions. (Policy: UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf, section c)
If I work part-time and receive pay from two different funding sources, what leave documentation do I need to maintain?

You must maintain documentation showing leave utilization from each full accounting unit from which you receive pay. Additionally, you should maintain records separately identifying sick, vacation, and other types of leave accruals and utilizations, showing the balance on each fund from which you are paid. However, if your campus has an automated leave accrual system, you only need to maintain documentation showing leave utilization.
Hey, I'm new here and just got assigned a leased university vehicle. What am I supposed to do with it when the lease is up?
At the end of the contract term, the property must be returned to the lessor at the place agreed to by the parties, as stated in UC-PS-12-0029_AcquisitionDispositionUniversityVehicles.pdf.

What specific account codes or cost center codes should be used when recording intercampus loans valued at $50,000 or more, and are there different coding requirements for loans under $50,000 or for loans that span multiple fiscal years?
The borrowing University location uses acquisition code 37, while the lending University location uses the appropriate loan code. This is outlined in UC-FA-21-0555.

URGENT: We need an immediate answer - who the hell is responsible for running audits and putting out guidelines based on those audit findings under the UC Risk Transfer Insurance Requirements policy?? This needs to be clarified NOW.

The University Chief Risk Officer is responsible for conducting audits and may issue additional guidelines as needed that may limit the range of exceptions allowed at the local level, per the UC-RK-25-762_BFB-BUS-63_RiskTransferInsuranceRequirements_Accessible (1).pdf policy.
As a department manager, how many procurement cardholders can I approve before I need to involve a reviewer?

According to the policy, a reviewer can approve more than ten (10) cardholders. This means that as a department manager, you would need to involve a reviewer if you need to approve more than ten cardholders. The policy does not specify a limit for individual manager approvals below this threshold, but any approvals exceeding ten cardholders require reviewer approval.
If I'm procuring goods and services through the Small Business First Program, what other requirements do I need to follow besides the program itself?

All other University, State, and Federal requirements governing the purchase of goods and services will apply to the Small Business First Program. Additionally, if your procurement involves construction, all contracting must be governed by the UC Facilities Manual and its associated policies and templates.
Can I move government property from one UC campus to an off-campus location without getting approval first?

No. According to the policy, you must obtain prior written approval from the Government Property Administrator before moving government property to off-campus sites. Additionally, you must follow receipt of a shipping or transfer document or other instrument when making such moves.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What transaction code should be used when adding university-owned equipment to the asset value as a capital transaction?
Transaction code 50 (or University location equivalent) shall be used, as specified in UC-FA-21-0555.

If the Risk Management Office requires $5 million in general liability insurance for a $250,000 equipment procurement, but the campus administrator responsible for the department's $2 million annual budget believes $2 million coverage is sufficient, what is the formal dispute resolution process and which office has final authority to approve the purchase order?
The final determination will be made by the University Chief Risk Officer (or designee), as stated in the UC-RK-25-762_BFB-BUS-63_RiskTransferInsuranceRequirements_Accessible (1).pdf policy.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What form must be used to request the loan of university equipment?
The Equipment Inventory Modification Request (EIMR) form (or equivalent form) must be used, as outlined in UC-FA-21-0555.
Are department heads eligible to be issued a procurement card under the terms of this federally funded award?

No, department heads cannot be issued a procurement card as they are considered subordinates of procurement cardholders, which compromises the independence required for expenditure verification. This is outlined in UC Policy BFB-BUS-43.

If a department needs to purchase $50,000 worth of specialized equipment but the standard UC Template Documents don't address the unique licensing requirements for that equipment type, what specific steps and approvals must the procurement office complete according to policy before proceeding with the purchase agreement?
When an exception occurs, the Procurement/Supply Chain Director must document the purchase file to reflect the reason for the exception, as stated in Policy BFB-BUS-43.
When we lease equipment, what value should we record in the equipment database - the total amount we'll pay over the lease term, or something else?

You should record the capitalized value of the equipment as the cash value of the equipment as of the inception date of the lease. This means you record the equipment's fair market value at the start of the lease, not the total payments you'll make over time. Interest or other financing costs are not included in this recorded value.
If we're purchasing new lab equipment and trading in our old equipment as part of the deal, how should we classify the equipment we're turning in?

According to UC policy, equipment that is surrendered upon the purchase of new equipment is classified as 'traded-in equipment.' This is the formal designation for equipment being exchanged as part of a new equipment purchase transaction.
Can I donate a used laboratory microscope worth $5,000 that we no longer need to the local community college?

No, you cannot donate that microscope. According to UC policy, donations of excess property are only permitted when the fair value is de minimis—meaning below the costs required for handling, record keeping, storage, removal, and other disposition costs. Since the microscope's fair value of $5,000 is significantly greater than de minimis costs, this donation would not be approved. UC policy explicitly prohibits donations of excess property whose fair value exceeds the de minimis threshold.
What factors should we consider in our department when deciding whether to classify a worker as an independent contractor versus a regular employee?

An employer has a reasonable basis for not treating a worker as an employee if it relied on judicial precedent, published rulings, technical advice, or a letter ruling issued to the employer. This is outlined in the GU-FA-20-0506_UCIndependentContractorGuidelines_Accessible.pdf policy.
When we receive component parts for equipment on different dates, which date should we use as the transaction date for the upgrade?

According to the policy, the transaction date shall be the receipt date of the component parts. This means you should use the date when the component parts are received, regardless of when other parts arrive or when the upgrade is completed.
URGENT: What immediate assessment mechanisms are in place RIGHT NOW to ensure the university is actually complying with procurement card policies? We need answers ASAP!

The university conducts assessments that include reviewing a statistical sample of cardholder records (source documentation) to determine compliance with local procurement card policies and procedures, as outlined in the BUS-43_ProcurementSupplyChainManagement_Main policy.

If a UC department verbally agrees to pay an instructor $5,000-$15,000 per semester to teach one or two evening courses without interfering with their full-time employment elsewhere, does UC policy classify this arrangement as an independent contractor relationship, or does it require a formal written agreement and different employment classification?

Yes, according to Exhibit B Situation #1 in the GU-FA-20-0506_UCIndependentContractorGuidelines_Accessible.pdf policy, instructors engaged under an oral agreement to teach part-time without conflicting with their regular jobs are classified as independent contractors under IRS rulings.

I'm new here and I'm trying to figure out who I need to get approval from when we're buying goods and services related to Agriculture and Natural Resources or if a Laboratory Director is involved—can someone help clarify that for me?

The Agriculture and Natural Resources, or Laboratory Director involved and the Executive Vice President - Chief Financial Officer (or designee) determine on a case-by-case basis. Policy: University of California – Policy BFB-BUS-43
If we discover that Addendum A is missing required information under data protection law, what should we do?

According to the policy, the Parties will cooperate to amend Appendix GDPR in a writing signed by both Parties to include any additional information required by Applicable Data Protection Law or if the Agreement otherwise requires amendment.
If a contractor we hired to clean our building is sued because someone was injured from their negligent work, who pays for the legal defense?

According to the indemnification provision in the contract, the contractor would be required to pay for the University's legal defense, as well as any settlement or judgment against the University. This is because the contractor agreed to indemnify the University for claims caused by the goods or services they provided under the contract.
Um, so like... if I need to move for work or something, is there money that UC gives you for that? And like, how do I actually ask for it? Do I just email someone or...?
The procedures section of the policy (UC-FA-18-0381_BFB-G-13_MovingRelocationPolicy) outlines the process for requesting a relocation allowance, including required documentation and approval steps.
What steps do I need to take after drafting a re-delegation letter for TTB authority?

You need to: (1) send the re-delegation letter to the TTB National Revenue Center with a cover letter requesting approval of the proposed re-delegation of authority, (2) ensure an approved copy of the letter is returned to you as the originator, and (3) send a copy of the re-delegation letter to the Systemwide Policy Director for the official records of the CFO Finance.
If I work for a contractor that provides services to UC, am I allowed to apply for open positions that the University is hiring for?
Yes. According to the policy, nothing in this Article prohibits an individual employee working for a contractor from applying for open University positions for which the University is recruiting.
Can the same person who makes purchases with a procurement card also review those purchases for administrative compliance?

No. According to the policy, the responsibilities of a cardholder who is authorized to make purchases with a procurement card must be separate from the individual assigned to conduct an administrative review of the purchase. These duties cannot be performed by the same person.
What should I do as a borrowing department when we're finished using borrowed equipment?
You should inform Equipment Management that the loan is terminated. Equipment Management will then terminate the loan in the equipment database.
Can I use a purchase order to pay someone for services instead of putting them on payroll?

No. According to UC policy, university purchasing procedures may not be used in lieu of placing an individual on the payroll. An individual can only be retained as an independent contractor if a legal determination has been made that an employer-employee relationship does not exist.
I'm still pretty new here and just trying to understand the policy – could you help clarify what counts as a decision that "directly relates" to a prospective employer?

The policy states that a decision 'directly relates' to a prospective employer if it is about the prospective employer, but the excerpt does not provide further specifics. Policy: mm-postemployment-coi-rules-10-2023.pdf
When should I contact the Office of General Counsel regarding the disposition of excess property?
You should consult the Office of General Counsel when there are legal or regulatory questions or risks related to specific dispositions or donations of excess property.

As a Principal Investigator managing federal grant funds, I need to understand the university's policies regarding position elimination due to outsourcing of services—specifically, what guidelines govern when such actions can occur and how they might impact my ability to maintain continuity of federally-funded research activities.
Displacement of staff due to contracting decisions may be allowed if it is related to business or financial necessity, as outlined in the GU-HR-23-0643_ContractingforServices_Accessible.pdf policy.
If I'm a Qualified Individual (QI) and don't get hired for the first UC position I apply for, what happens next?

If you are disqualified for the initial position, you may be considered for another position at the same location. However, the policy does not guarantee placement in an alternative position - it only states that you may be considered for other available positions at that same location.
Can you clarify what dollar amount triggers the competitive bidding requirement for our department's purchases?

The competitive bidding threshold for UC purchases is $100,000 annually for state-funded purchases, as mandated by California Public Contract Code Section 10507 et seq. [2]. For federal funds, the threshold is lower: federal contract purchases ≥$15,000 and federal grant/cooperative agreement purchases ≥$50,000 require competitive bidding [3]. However, the UC applies the stricter state threshold of $100,000 for all purchases unless exceptions apply (e.g., small business set-asides up to $250,000 with two price quotations) [2][4]. Mixed funding transactions are governed by the stricter threshold (e.g., $100,000 for state funds or federal funds ≥$10,000) [4].
When equipment is returned from being written off, what acquisition code should we use to restore it to active inventory?

According to Policy BFB-BUS-29, acquisition code 45 should be used to restore equipment to active inventory, provided that the equipment's remaining undepreciated value exceeds the inventorial equipment threshold.
If my department has excess equipment that we trade in toward the purchase of new lab instruments, how will the trade-in value be credited to us?

According to UC policy, when University property is traded in, your department will be credited with the trade-in allowance. This credit is generally provided in the form of an entry on a purchase order for new equipment, property, or store credit.
When we need to add more information to the Appendix GDPR, what's the process for making those changes?
The Parties will cooperate to amend Addendum A in a writing signed by both Parties, as stated in Appendix GDPR.

Hi everyone! I'm brand new here and still getting up to speed on all the policies. I was wondering—does UC have a specific list of items that are considered high-theft risk, like laptops? Just trying to make sure I understand the procurement rules correctly!
Yes, laptops are classified as theft-sensitive items under the UC-FA-21-0555_BUS-29_ManagementControlUniversityEquipment_Accessible.pdf policy. These items should be expensed; not capitalized.
Does our department need cyber security insurance if we handle 65,000 records at Level 4 protection?

No, cyber security insurance is not required for Level 4 data with 65,000 records. According to the policy, the insurance requirement is triggered when there are more than 70,000 records at Level 4 protection. Since your anticipated record count is less than 70,000, the insurance requirement does not apply.
If I need to purchase office supplies for my department, do I need to follow the procurement procedures outlined in BUS-43?

Yes, purchases of goods and services, including office supplies, fall under the scope of UC Policy BFB-BUS-43 on Procurement and Supply Chain Management. You must follow the procurement procedures outlined in this policy when making purchases for your department.

If a UC employee books a $4,500 first-class airfare ticket for a mandatory conference attendance, can that expense be reimbursed from the Administrative Fund, or must the employee be reimbursed only up to the $2,800 economy class fare that was available for the same route?

First-class airfare may be reimbursed from the Administrative Fund if it is authorized under the circumstances set forth in G-28, Policy and Regulations Governing Travel, as specified in UC-FO-00-0190_a-253-27.pdf.
You are a UC procurement policy expert. Answer questions strictly based on UC and UCSC policy documents. Always cite the policy source. If the answer is not in the policy, say so clearly.
What are the guidelines for classifying and managing IT assets under the BFB-IS-3 policy?
Policy BFB-IS-3, subsection 8 outlines the process for classifying, accounting for, and managing assets.
If we need to purchase office supplies from our current vendor for $75,000 annually, do we have to go through a competitive bidding process?

No, competitive bidding is not required. Since your annual expenditure with this supplier is $100,000 or less, negotiation is allowed. However, the Procurement/Supply Chain Director may still determine that competition is necessary to develop a source, validate prices, or for other compelling business reasons. Additionally, since your purchase falls between $10,000-$250,000 annually, you should consider awarding it to a Small Business or Disabled Veteran Business Enterprise wherever practicable, as the University supports small businesses through its set-aside program.
Can the Equipment Management department provide training to our custodial staff on how to properly safeguard university equipment?

Yes. Equipment Management may provide training to custodial department personnel to enhance their understanding of University policy, location procedures, and federal regulatory requirements regarding safeguarding and verification of inventorial property. They can also provide training and guidance on best practices for safeguarding and managing equipment and other inventorial assets.

If a faculty member hosts a one-time meeting with 5 students and purchases $75 worth of coffee and pastries, can this expense be reimbursed under UC policy?
